proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: The technical governing body of AAIF responsible for technical projects, working groups, and lifecycle governance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) serves as the primary technical steering body for the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), assisting the Governing Board with project reviews, lifecycle management, and working group coordination[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Architecture / Specification
## Composition
Each Platinum Member of AAIF appoints one representative to the TC[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. The TC elects an annual Chair and optional Co-Chair to preside over meetings.

## Responsibilities
The TC's responsibilities include:
- Establishing, managing, and archiving Working Groups[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Coordinating collaboration across Technical Projects and setting overall technical direction[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Recommending projects to the Governing Board for acceptance as Technical Projects[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Implementing and maintaining the Project Lifecycle Policy[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Recommending resource priorities to the Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Decision-Making and Voting
- **Lazy Consensus**: TC proposals are approved automatically after 72 hours if no formal objection is recorded[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Voting**: If an objection is raised or formal voting is needed, each voting member receives one vote. Quorum requires at least 50% member presence, and electronic votes require a majority of all voting members[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Amendments**: Charter amendments require approval by two-thirds of the TC and Governing Board approval[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Lifecycle History
The Technical Committee Charter was formally adopted on March 3, 2026[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group developing landscape analyses, gap analyses, and governance guidance for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an AAIF working group focused on mapping existing legal and regulatory frameworks, assessing risks in agentic AI, and developing standardized guidance for oversight and compliance[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Architecture / Specification
## Deliverables Model
The working group follows a three-step working model[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:
1. **Landscape Analysis**: Reviewing current industry standards, regulations (such as EU AI Act, GDPR, and eIDAS 2), and existing organizational risk frameworks[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
2. **Gap Analysis**: Identifying emerging agentic AI challenges not covered by existing frameworks[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
3. **Distilled Guidance**: Establishing principles and governance recommendations for organizations deploying agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

## Operating Model
The working group meets on a biweekly cadence, coordinating via shared documents with Discord as a secondary channel[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]. Working group charters and outputs report to the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

# Lifecycle History
The working group held its kickoff meeting on February 19, 2026, establishing governance guidelines and initiating chair nominations[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. On March 5, 2026, the group adopted its three-step deliverable strategy[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating shared agent observability, behavioral trace models, and alignment across ecosystem standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group chartered to build a shared understanding of agent observability across practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. The working group functions as a coordination forum to bridge LLM-level telemetry with workflow-level agent understanding, producing trace models, gap analyses, and implementation guidance [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Scope and Mandate
The working group focuses on vendor-neutral observability conventions and interoperability across agent frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Developing standardized behavioral trace representations across multi-turn interactions, tool invocations, and multi-modal transformations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Standards Alignment**: Coordinating with external standards bodies—including OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context—to contribute upstream and avoid ecosystem fragmentation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Auditability and Safety**: Establishing observability practices that support enterprise debugging, behavioral evaluation, safety guarantees, and compliance [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Governance
The working group operates under the technical governance of the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and follows Linux Foundation community governance practices [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.title: Case Study Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Guidelines and requirements for AAIF member organizations publishing case studies demonstrating measurable business impact.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Case Study Guidelines establish criteria and review procedures for member organizations publishing case studies on real-world adoption of open agentic AI standards [^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]. Case studies highlight practical implementations of ecosystem technologies—such as MCP, goose, and AGENTS.md—focusing on agentic maturity, cross-platform interoperability, and measurable business acceleration [^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

# Submission Formats and Requirements
AAIF accepts case studies through two primary formats [^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]:

- **Written Case Studies**: Long-form articles outlining business challenges, technical architectures, adoption phases, and quantified business outcomes [^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].
- **Webinar Case Studies**: Recorded 20–30 minute presentations with Q&A sessions distributed across foundation channels [^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

All submissions require documented tangible impact and must maintain vendor neutrality and factual accuracy [^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

mutations.rationale: Document the AAIF Agentic AI Landscape project, including its scope, generation engine, and entry inclusion criteria based on the repository documentation.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: An interactive catalog and visual map categorizing open-source software, projects, and open standards across the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape provides an interactive overview and categorization of open source software, open standards, and member initiatives across the agentic AI domain[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Built using the CNCF Landscape2 tooling, the landscape indexes prominent community technologies and organizational offerings to facilitate ecosystem navigation[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Inclusion Criteria
Entries submitted for inclusion in the landscape must adhere to defined baseline criteria[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **Open Source Focus**: Projects must be open source, typically have at least 1,000 GitHub stars, and fit into a single established landscape category[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Exclusions**: Proprietary standards, closed-source products, commercial editions of open-source tools, and closed-source tools that merely implement open-source standards are not accepted[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Single Category Mapping**: An organization or project is generally mapped to only one category to highlight its primary offering[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Logo Assets**: Projects must provide SVG-format stacked logos with non-inverted, transparent or white backgrounds and English typography[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is configured via `landscape.yml` and hosted logo assets within the `aaif/aaif-landscape` repository[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Generation builds run daily using the `cncf/landscape2` compiler, integrating external entity metadata from sources like Crunchbase and GitHub[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

proposed_concept.title: Code of Conduct
proposed_concept.description: Rules, expected behaviors, and enforcement mechanisms ensuring an inclusive and harassment-free environment across AAIF activities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Code of Conduct establishes community standards and enforcement procedures to foster an inclusive, welcoming, and safe environment across all foundation activities [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Architecture / Specification
The Code of Conduct governs interactions within the foundation's official operations [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]:

- **Scope**: Covers Governing Board, [Technical Committee](./technical-committee.md), Working Group, and Outreach Committee meetings, as well as broader foundation channels [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].
- **Events**: Foundation-produced events operate under the Linux Foundation Events Code of Conduct in conjunction with this policy [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].
- **Technical Projects**: Technical projects under the AAIF umbrella maintain and enforce individual project-level codes of conduct [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].
- **Behavioral Standards**: Requires inclusive language, respect for diverse viewpoints, and constructive collaboration while strictly prohibiting harassment, discrimination, personal attacks, and non-consensual disclosure of private information [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual, communicative, and design standards defining the neutral, collaborative, and trustworthy identity of the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the core visual identity, design rules, and editorial tone for all Agentic AI Foundation assets, publications, presentations, and marketing deliverables [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

# Architecture / Specification
The brand is anchored on three core pillars [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]:

- **Neutral**: Emphasizes vendor-neutrality, open governance, and transparent standards without implying ownership or control by any single vendor [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].
- **Collaborative**: Focuses on cross-industry cooperation and shared ecosystem goals using collective phrasing rather than hero-centric framing [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].
- **Trustworthy**: Builds upon Linux Foundation credibility through precise claims, high-contrast layouts, and grounded communication rather than speculative AI hype [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

The primary brand palette relies on pure white (`#ffffff`) and black (`#000000`) for high contrast and readability [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

proposed_concept.title: Public Agent Skills
proposed_concept.description: Standardized, portable skill bundles equipping AI agents with specialized capabilities, domain knowledge, and AAIF procedures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
AAIF Public Agent Skills are portable packages containing domain instructions, references, scripts, and static assets designed to enable AI agents to perform specialized tasks according to the Agent Skills specification [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

# Architecture / Specification
Each agent skill resides in its own directory structured around a primary `SKILL.md` file containing YAML frontmatter and instructional Markdown, with optional directories for static `assets/`, background `references/`, and executable `scripts/` [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

Skills can be distributed, installed globally, or installed per-project via the Skills CLI (`npx skills`) and are dynamically invoked by compatible AI agent environments based on conversational context [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security and privacy threat models, shared taxonomies, design patterns, and protocol review for agentic architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to addressing the security, privacy, safety, and trust challenges unique to autonomous and multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The group develops threat models, best practice frameworks, architectural guardrails, and standardized taxonomies across member projects and external integrations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification

### Cross-Working Group Taxonomy
The SP WG leads the cross-working group taxonomy effort across AAIF, providing an initial baseline taxonomy derived from working group deliverables to establish consistent terminology across all AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

### Protocol and Ecosystem Engagement
The working group actively monitors and provides security and privacy feedback for external protocol enhancements, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) initiatives such as MCP Interceptors (data privacy and redaction hooks) and MCP Apps (UI boundary crossing) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-28**: Presented WG charter to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md); initiated self-organizing async workstreams, established the baseline taxonomy for cross-WG alignment, and scheduled joint reviews with MCP initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Public Agent Resources and Skills
proposed_concept.description: Standardized, portable skill bundles, recipes, prompts, and testing workflows enabling AI agents to operate within AAIF environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Public Agent Resources are reusable, open-source agent capabilities, prompt templates, repeatable workflows, and evaluation pipelines curated under the `aaif/public-agents` repository [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]. These assets provide plug-and-play domain knowledge, guidance compliance, and interaction workflows for autonomous agents across the AAIF ecosystem [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

# Architecture / Specification

The repository organizes public agent assets into structured directories:

- `skills/`: Standardized capability modules providing domain-specific expertise, workflow automation, and tool execution instructions, including [Brand Guidelines](../policies-guidelines/brand-guidelines.md) enforcement [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7] [^evt-public-agents-pr-1].
- `recipes/`: Multi-step, repeatable agent execution workflows and orchestration tasks [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `prompts/`: Standardized prompt definitions and templates designed for task consistency [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `docs/`: Contribution guidelines and technical documentation [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

### Model Integration and Testing Workflows
The repository maintains GitHub Actions inference workflows to validate agent interactions across external LLM APIs:

- `copilot-test-action`: Connects to GitHub Models (`https://models.github.ai`) using repository token credentials to catalog available models and execute test completions [^evt-public-agents-file-b248ae41d1f0-0667ce2f] [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `gemini-test-action`: Connects directly to the Google Gemini API to validate completions across configurable model endpoints [^evt-public-agents-file-ae1d68d00103-0e76c626] [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

# Lifecycle History

- **PR #1**: Added the AAIF Brand Guidelines skill bundle to standardize organizational visual and voice requirements [^evt-public-agents-pr-1].

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing vendor-neutral standards for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization across organizations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust (I&T) Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative formed to define and advance vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and architectural viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c] Its purpose is to ensure that agents can be discovered across platforms, prove their provenance and operational identity, establish delegated authority on behalf of humans or services, and enforce policy constraints across organizational boundaries.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on several foundational domains across both enterprise and consumer agent architectures:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance:** Formats and mechanisms for agent identification, authentication protocols, and metadata describing runtime environment, producing software, and owning operator.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Delegation and Authority Chains:** Representations of agency, human-on-the-loop delegation, service acting chains, and explicit boundaries on delegated operational authority.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Authorization and Consent Models:** Fine-grained, short-lived authorization schemes, human approvals, and policy constraints regulating what an agent is permitted to execute.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust:** Mechanisms enabling disparate organizations to establish mutual trust and evaluate cross-boundary agent requests.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Agent Discovery and Trust-Relevant Metadata:** Structured metadata facilitating safe discovery, observability, and traceability in coordination with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

Out of scope are the ratification of formal SDO standards, production identity infrastructure hosting, broad ethical policies (coordinated with the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)), and comprehensive execution security controls (coordinated with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

# Governance and Leadership
The group operates under the technical governance of the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and is led by chair Grant Miller.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

mutations.rationale: Captures the editorial standards, contributor eligibility rules, and intake workflows for the AAIF blog.

proposed_concept.title: Blog Guidelines and Content Intake Process
proposed_concept.description: Editorial standards, contributor eligibility criteria, and intake workflows for publishing content on the AAIF blog.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) blog serves as a community publishing platform on aaif.io for technical guides, project releases, case studies, and thought leadership across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. Content intake and publication are managed by the Linux Foundation team to maintain editorial quality and vendor neutrality [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Contributor Scope
Submissions are accepted across several participant categories [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]:
- **Member Companies:** Permitted vendor-neutral posts, restricted to at most one or two concluding sentences with a single external link [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Project Maintainers & Contributors:** Announcements, deep dives, and roadmaps for AAIF-hosted projects such as Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, and AGENTS.md [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Working Groups & Technical Committee:** Official updates and guidance authored on behalf of AAIF bodies [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Community Contributors & Event Participants:** Educational articles, case studies, and event recaps [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

## Content Criteria and Submission Rules
- **Neutrality:** Posts must avoid promotional language, commercial bias, or disparagement of any open-source project [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Originality & Timeliness:** Content must be original, previously unpublished, and generally reflective of work within the past two months [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Format & Lead Time:** Drafts should follow a narrative structure (typically 600–1,500 words) and require approximately a two-week lead time for review and scheduling [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c][^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed].

## Tooling and Agent Assistance
Contributors may utilize the `aaif-blog-guidelines` agent skill from [Public Agent Skills](../ecosystem/public-agent-skills.md) to validate drafts against editorial guidelines and assemble submission packages [^evt-foundation-pr-2][^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating shared agent observability, behavioral trace models, and alignment across standards bodies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) advances agent observability across the Agentic AI Foundation by convening practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Functioning as a coordination forum rather than a competing standards organization, the group focuses on standardizing visibility into session-level and workflow-level agent behavior where single-call LLM tracing is insufficient [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Mandate and Guiding Principles
- **Coordinate First:** The working group defaults to collaborating with existing initiatives (including OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context) and producing new specifications only when clear industry gaps are identified [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Vendor & Framework Neutrality:** Specifications and conventions ensure trace portability across agent frameworks and telemetry backends, preventing proprietary lock-in [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

## Focus Areas
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** Founding focus area addressing multi-turn interaction traces, tool execution tracking, and content lineage across modalities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Accountability & Auditing:** Defining trace formats and telemetry conventions required for production debugging, safety evaluations, and enterprise auditability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-15:** Charter ratified by working group members [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **2026-05-13:** Charter formally approved under chair Pavan Sudheendra [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security and privacy threat models, shared taxonomies, and design patterns for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA — Security & Privacy for Agentic AI) establishes security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Operating under the Agentic AI Foundation, the group produces open threat models, taxonomies, and architectural patterns to address risks specific to agent autonomy, tool invocation, and sensitive data processing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope
- **In Scope:** Threat modeling and attack analysis (e.g., prompt injection, confused deputy scenarios, memory vulnerabilities), security architecture patterns, agent control and containment mechanisms, and data protection practices [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Out of Scope:** Ethics and value judgments (deferred to [Governance, Risk & Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)), legal regulatory compliance interpretation, and product certification programs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

## Cross-Working Group Integration
The group serves as an intersecting discipline across all AAIF working groups, sharing threat models and collaborating closely with [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) on agent boundaries and authentication [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-13:** Charter approved under chair Alex Frazer [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

mutations.rationale: Update Security & Privacy WG concept with leadership, governance, scope boundaries, deliverable sequencing, and external alignment from the draft charter and recent working group proceedings.

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, containment mechanisms, and cross-working group review checklists for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (S&P WG) establishes vendor-neutral security architecture, threat models, containment mechanisms, and privacy-preserving design patterns across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. It addresses agent-specific risks including multi-agent persuasion, indirect prompt injection, tool invocation vulnerabilities, delegated authorization, cascading failures, and goal drift[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

# Governance & Operations
The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer alongside Co-Chair Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. The group operates through consensus and biweekly open meetings, using workstream-specific coordination channels and escalating to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) when formal dispute resolution or quorum fallback is required[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. Official charter voting and governance workflows are managed through the Linux Foundation LFX platform[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Scope & Deliverables
The working group focuses on technical threat analysis, containment architecture, and evaluation harnesses while explicitly scoping out legal regulatory interpretation and ethics/bias policy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. Core deliverables and workstreams include:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Primary near-term deliverable analyzing agent attack surfaces, threat vectors, and mitigation gaps[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Cross-Working Group Security & Privacy Review Checklist**: Baseline review criteria to assist other AAIF working groups in identifying security and privacy implications across their specifications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Security & Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Technical catalog documenting concrete implementation patterns—such as execution hooks, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and least-privilege containment—alongside anti-patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: High-level guidance providing operational security recommendations for deployers and developers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Taxonomy Integration**: Initial taxonomy drafting incubated in the working group has transitioned into an AAIF foundation-wide cross-working group initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

The working group also maintains external liaisons with adjacent standards efforts and protocol groups, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem and AARM[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Client Protocol (ACP)
proposed_concept.description: Standardized communication protocol connecting code editors and IDEs to AI coding agents across local and remote transports.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Client Protocol (ACP) standardizes communication between code editors or IDEs and AI coding agents, providing a common interface layer analogous to how the Language Server Protocol (LSP) standardized language server tooling[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1]. ACP was created by Zed Industries and co-developed with JetBrains to solve the $M \times N$ integration challenge where every new agent-editor combination previously demanded custom integration[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

ACP has been proposed for AAIF project adoption under the sponsorship of Technical Committee members[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

# Architecture / Specification
ACP focuses on the developer-tooling and agent UX session layer while maintaining synergy with broader data connectivity standards[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1]:
- **Transport Layers**: Implements JSON-RPC over standard input/output (`stdio`) for local agents, with active implementations for HTTP and WebSocket transports for remote agent execution[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].
- **MCP Complementarity**: ACP standardizes editor-to-agent interactions, complementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP) which handles model-to-tool and model-to-data connectivity. ACP reuses MCP JSON representations and allows client IDEs to configure MCP servers for attached agents[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].
- **Ecosystem Implementations**: Integrates with multiple client environments including Zed, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, and Emacs, as well as agents including Goose, Cline, Cursor, OpenHands, and GitHub Copilot[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

# Governance & Process
ACP is licensed under Apache 2.0 and operates an open Request for Dialog (RFD) process for protocol specification changes and architectural decision-making[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

- **Agentic AI Project Watchlist**: Features a decoupled watchlist tracking prominent open-source agentic AI projects aligned with LFX Insights momentum metrics[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance framework detailing proposal requirements, stage criteria (Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and annual review processes for AAIF technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy defines the formal governance framework for open technical projects joining, progressing through, and retiring within the AAIF[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Administered in coordination with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy outlines submission requirements, maturity stages, and annual evaluation procedures to support alignment across the ecosystem.

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Stages
The lifecycle categorizes projects across three distinct stages[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- **Growth Stage**: Intended for active, evolving projects demonstrating ecosystem relevance, emerging community adoption, and alignment with foundation objectives.
- **Impact Stage**: Designated for mature, widely adopted projects providing critical infrastructure, standardized specifications, and stable multi-organization governance.
- **Emeritus Stage**: Designated for retired projects or those with minimal maintenance activity that have completed their lifecycle or transitioned to maintenance mode[^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

## Proposal Requirements
Technical project proposals submitted through the project proposals repository must provide foundational metadata and operational documentation[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- Project name, description, origin, and mission alignment
- Demonstrated use cases, adoption evidence, and relations to existing AAIF initiatives
- Technical Committee sponsorship and leadership structure
- OSI-approved permissive open-source license
- Public repository, issue tracking, CI/CD automated release mechanics, and specification contribution processes
- External dependencies, official communication channels, infrastructure requests, and documented governance practices

## Annual Review Process
Project progression and continued stage alignment are evaluated through an annual review process to verify ongoing health, community participation, and compliance with governance criteria[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Submission criteria, proposal requirements, and review processes for AAIF member organizations proposing new Working Groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines define the criteria and process for proposing new Working Groups within the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Working Groups serve as structured, time-bound collaborations of subject matter experts convened to advance research, develop vendor-neutral standards, and produce actionable guidance across technical, governance, safety, and policy domains.

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligibility
Submissions are open exclusively to Foundation Member organizations in good standing across all membership tiers[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Proposals submitted from non-member organizations are not reviewed.

## Proposal Requirements
Proposals for new working groups must provide structured information including[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:
- **Submitter Information**: Proposer name, organizational affiliation, role, contact details, leadership availability, and membership tier.
- **Identity & Focus**: Clear, concise working group name and a single-sentence plain-language summary.
- **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Specific gaps, industry challenges, agentic AI relevance, and strategic alignment with AAIF objectives.
- **Scope & Deliverables**: Defined outputs such as technical reports, whitepapers, frameworks, benchmarks, open tooling, or policy guidance.
- **Timeline & Structure**: Target meeting cadence and lifecycle duration, typically operating on a 12–24 month charter cycle.
- **Membership & Expertise**: Required stakeholder perspectives and initial expressions of community commitment.
- **Impact & Urgency**: Justification of why the initiative requires foundation backing and structured cross-industry collaboration.

proposed_concept.title: Social Media Governance and Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Editorial standards, channel intake workflows, and amplification criteria for official AAIF social media communications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Social Media Governance and Guidelines govern content strategy, public communication standards, and social media amplification for the Agentic AI Foundation under Linux Foundation leadership[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]. The policy outlines platform tone, submission workflows, and criteria for featuring open-source agentic AI developments across official foundation channels.

# Architecture / Specification

## Communication Tone & Baseline
Official AAIF channels maintain a neutral, professional, inclusive, and vendor-neutral tone tailored to a global developer and artificial intelligence audience[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]. Key baseline principles include:
- **Domain Relevance**: Focus strictly on the open-source AI ecosystem, official releases, community events, and technical resources.
- **Neutrality & Anti-Promotion**: Generic self-promotion, proprietary product marketing, consulting pitches, and sponsored content are prohibited.
- **Attribution**: Proper attribution for open-source licenses, technical contributions, and community work is required.
- **Platform-Specific Style**: Tailored engagement across platforms, including punchy updates on X, professional case studies and technical milestones on LinkedIn, and conversational dialogue on Bluesky.

## Submission and Reposting Workflow
Content intake is managed through distinct channels depending on the amplification format[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]:
- **Direct Reposts**: Submitted via dedicated foundation Discord amplification channels for official releases, working group announcements, and foundation-led events.
- **Organic AAIF Posts**: Submitted through the foundation content intake form for structured consideration.
- **Community Projects**: Highlighted exclusively when demonstrating concrete implementation of AAIF standards and specifications.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, reference architectures, and interoperability patterns for AI agent commerce workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working group focused on cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, reference models, and terminology for commerce workflows conducted by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, the group serves as a neutral forum to prevent ecosystem fragmentation across emerging commerce protocols while maintaining strict protocol neutrality[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Scope and Deliverables

The working group focuses on interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns across the agentic commerce lifecycle, coordinating with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) on delegation and buyer identity[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

Key areas within scope include:
- **Discovery & Negotiation**: Standard interfaces between agents and merchants for product discovery, offers, terms, and availability[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Cart & Checkout**: Cart composition, validation, and checkout handoff between agent and merchant systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Identity & Delegated Authority**: Buyer identity, agent authority scoping, and consent conveyance[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Agentic Payments**: Interfacing between agents, wallets, and payment networks for intent, authorization, and settlement signals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Fraud Signaling**: Exchanging risk-posture signals between agents, merchants, and risk systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Human-in-the-Loop & Boundaries**: Escalation, confirmation protocols, and post-purchase lifecycle workflows including dispute and order status conveyance[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

The group explicitly excludes authoring competing commerce protocol specifications, operating payment rails, or building end-user marketplace hardware and UI[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History

The Agentic Commerce Working Group charter was formally approved on May 15, 2026[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, containment mechanisms, and privacy guardrails for autonomous AI agent ecosystems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative tasked with establishing security threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, containment mechanisms, and privacy guardrails for autonomous AI agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. The working group operates collaborative workstreams spanning threat modeling, best practice guides, and design pattern catalogs to secure multi-agent interactions across the ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Scope and Deliverables

The working group organizes its technical outputs across several active workstreams and deliverables:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Developing threat models and security gap analyses for agentic workloads, overlapping with cross-foundation taxonomy efforts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive implementation guidance for secure deployment and operation of autonomous agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural and containment patterns addressing common multi-agent attack surfaces[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Security and privacy evaluation criteria for sibling AAIF working group deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Taxonomy & Landscape Alignment**: Coordinated through cross-WG leadership to classify security tools and guardrail categories[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Lifecycle History

Following formal approval of its charter in May 2026, the working group instituted a self-selection leadership model across its Discord workstream channels and aligned deliverable schedules with cross-foundation taxonomy initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group serving as a bridge between global AI policy developments, regulatory standards, and technical agentic architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (GRRA WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group established to bridge global AI regulatory frameworks and technical agentic AI architectures[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]. The group addresses novel risks, the lack of cohesive governance standards, and interoperability gaps across enterprise agent deployments[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Scope and Responsibilities
The working group focuses on synthesizing emerging regulations, policy frameworks, and technical governance mechanisms across agent systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]:
- **Policy and Standards Tracking**: Monitoring global AI regulations, standards, and best practices impacting agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- **Protocol Governance**: Analyzing how agent protocols (such as Model Context Protocol) are implemented within organizational governance processes[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- **Technical Governance Deliverables**: Researching AI Agent Bill of Materials (AIBOM) covering models, scaffolding, tools, and APIs; formal methods and formats for action reversibility and undo infrastructure; human-in-the-loop patterns; and risk assessment classifications[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

Explicitly out of scope is providing legal advice, delivering compliance solutions, or endorsing specific commercial vendors[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Leadership and Governance
The working group is chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and operates under the technical governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

proposed_concept.description: Submission criteria, intake workflow, review labels, and approval voting rules for forming new AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines define the formal intake, review, and voting procedure for establishing new working groups within the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Proposals are submitted asynchronously via issue templates and evaluated by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Intake and Review Process
Applicants submit a structured Working Group Proposal issue to the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Submissions are tracked on the Working Group Proposals Board and triaged for discussion in scheduled Technical Committee meetings[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Status Labels
Proposals are categorized using five formal tracking states[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:
- `New`: Newly submitted proposal placed in the triage backlog.
- `Approved`: Accepted by the Technical Committee and Governing Board.
- `Declined`: Proposal rejected with explanatory comments.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Clarifications or additional information requested by reviewers.
- `Too Early`: Proposal not yet mature enough for WG status, accompanied by guidance on reapplication.

## Approval Criteria
To be accepted, a working group proposal requires a simple majority vote from members of the Technical Committee and remains subject to final approval by the Governing Board[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates technical standards, telemetry schemas, and distributed trace representations across agentic AI workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. The working group collaborates with other AAIF initiatives, including cross-working group taxonomy and landscape workstreams, to establish consistent visibility into autonomous agent execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Organization and Focus Areas
The working group organizes its technical initiatives through dedicated focus groups and asynchronous GitHub collaboration[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]:
- **Multi-Agent Systems Observability**: Focuses on trace structures and interaction telemetry in distributed, multi-agent architectures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Observability and Protocols**: Evaluates protocol-level observability and telemetry integration across standard agent interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Explores reasoning traces and cognitive step monitoring within autonomous workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

Governance and cross-group alignment are coordinated under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops vendor-neutral threat models, containment mechanisms, and baseline security and privacy controls for agentic systems across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical efforts into four core workstreams alongside cross-cutting foundation initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:

- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing security and privacy assessment criteria for AAIF projects and working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg, drafting operational guidelines for deploying secure agent runtimes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, analyzing attack surfaces unique to autonomous agent interactions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas, maintaining standard implementation patterns for isolation, least privilege, and safe tool use [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as the working group's delegates to the cross-cutting `../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Lifecycle History

On 2026-06-09, the working group confirmed workstream lead appointments and delegates to the cross-WG taxonomy initiative while transitioning to an asynchronous monthly reporting workflow with the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF body responsible for standardizing terminology across working groups and curating the landscape of agentic AI runtimes and frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates as an open collaboration coordinated across AAIF working groups:

- **Leadership**: Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].
- **Inter-WG Coordination**: Each working group designates representatives, such as the `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` delegates, to review cross-cutting definitions and resolve taxonomy conflicts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Landscape Maintenance**: Curates decoupled project datasets that map the ecosystem visualization in `../ecosystem/agentic-ai-landscape.md` via pull-request-driven workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Lifecycle History

In June 2026, the workstream established formal delegate participation across AAIF working groups and instituted monthly reporting templates for asynchronous reviews by the `../governance/technical-committee.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].

# Overview

The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group aligns technical implementations with emerging global AI policies, regulatory standards, and compliance frameworks across the AAIF ecosystem [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open specifications and telemetry schemas for tracking, debugging, and auditing multi-agent systems and agent-tool interactions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].

# Architecture / Specification

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, containment mechanisms, and cross-group security review checklists for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes security threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, containment mechanisms, and review standards across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. The group operates as an intersecting layer across all AAIF working groups, conducting security and privacy reviews on emerging specifications and architectural artifacts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams
The working group organizes its technical activities into several distinct workstreams:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Evaluates existing AI threat modeling frameworks (including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) to identify gaps specific to agentic AI—such as multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation vulnerabilities, delegated authorization boundaries, and supply chain integrity (system prompt integrity, model provenance, and tool manifest verification)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. Led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates reusable, problem-context-solution design patterns and anti-patterns for agentic architectures, covering runtime hooks, checkpointing, human-in-the-loop controls, privacy-preserving execution (zero-knowledge proofs, trusted execution environments, encrypted vector databases), blast radius containment, secure memory retention/deletion, and agent containment/intervention mechanisms (kill switches, rollback, permission downgrade, off-task detection)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Defines review checklists and intake procedures to assess deliverables from peer working groups through a security and privacy lens[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Initial target groups include [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), and [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

## Deliverables Management and Lifecycle
Deliverables follow an explicit status lifecycle governed by formal working group decisions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]:

- **Draft**: Work in progress prefixed with `DRAFT-` in filename; tracked in deliverable registries with modification dates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Final**: Approved deliverables requiring an explicit recorded decision in working group meeting notes before removing the `DRAFT-` prefix and updating document headers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Moved**: Deliverables transitioned to cross-WG initiatives or external repositories, maintained as redirect stubs to preserve inbound links and document ongoing participation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].

# Lifecycle History
The working group originally hosted a standalone taxonomy workstream, which was merged into the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream chaired by Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93]. Security and Privacy WG delegates Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) represent the working group within the cross-WG taxonomy effort[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF effort tasked with establishing common terminology, resolving conflicting conceptual definitions, and maintaining standardized domain definitions across all foundation working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. Chaired by Junjie Bu, the workstream operates through open pull request workflows with active delegate participation from individual AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Architecture / Specification

## Inter-Group Governance and Representation
Working groups across the AAIF contribute delegates to participate in taxonomy reviews and resolve domain-specific terminology conflicts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]:

- **Security and Privacy**: The [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) merged its standalone taxonomy draft into the cross-WG workstream and is represented by appointed delegates Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream was established to unify disparate vocabulary efforts across individual working groups into a single decoupled repository ([aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93]. On 2026-06-22, the Security and Privacy Working Group formally transferred its terms and definitions deliverable into this central repository[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) in the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) establishes vendor-neutral security frameworks, threat models, design patterns, and builder best practices for agentic AI architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. The group evaluates emerging risks across tool invocation, autonomous delegation, prompt injection, memory poisoning, and blast radius containment across multi-agent environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group organizes its technical outputs into dedicated workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, conducting a gap analysis of existing AI threat frameworks (including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic-specific threat surfaces such as tool invocation risks, context poisoning, excessive agency, and blast-radius management[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, delivering reusable secure and privacy-preserving design patterns formatted with problem, context, solution, and trade-off specifications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing high-level operational guidance covering secrets management, secure tool execution, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing lightweight security and privacy review mechanisms across other AAIF working group deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as the WG's designated delegates to the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Governance and Operations

The working group operates under public GitHub repositories as the system of record for maturing deliverables and contributor attribution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Workstream leads coordinate monthly updates with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) through formal review cycles[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is an AAIF-wide initiative responsible for building common terminology, resolving conflicting definitions, and standardizing conceptual models across all AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Led by Junjie Bu, the workstream synthesizes core domain vocabularies, taxonomy schemas, and capability archetypes into a unified knowledge foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Lifecycle History

The taxonomy effort originated within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) before being elevated to an official cross-working group initiative to ensure consistency across the entire foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Development is hosted in a central repository with weekly synchronizations and asynchronous review cycles[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Cross-WG Participation and Delegates

Working groups contribute domain-specific vocabularies through appointed delegates who review terminology and resolve semantic ambiguities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Each working group surfaces 10 to 20 key domain terms for alignment in the unified taxonomy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. For example, the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) participates via delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates telemetry models, behavioral trace specifications, and protocol instrumentation standards across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]. The group provides vendor-neutral frameworks for capturing, correlating, and analyzing agent execution paths, multi-agent coordination, and internal reasoning processes.

The working group collaborates closely with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to align telemetry definitions and reports regular progress to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Architecture / Specification

Work is partitioned across several specialized focus groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:

- **LLM Primitives**: Develops landscape surveys and gap analyses for core language model telemetry, utilizing an audit model aligned with MCP.
- **Agent State and Context**: Investigates runtime context propagation, session state tracking, and state persistence patterns across commercial and academic implementations.
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Defines tracing and correlation mechanisms for multi-agent workflows and delegated task hierarchies.
- **Agentic Reasoning and Memory Systems**: Evaluates white-box tracing methodologies, internal memory structures, and thought-process auditing.

# Operations and Governance

The working group operates under public issue trackers and bi-weekly synchronization meetings [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:

- **Issue Tracking & Deliverables**: Work items, deliverable trackers, and focus group deliverables are managed through the public repository Kanban boards and issue tracker [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Reporting Cadence**: Submits monthly status reports covering progress, blockers, and risks to the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Community Engagement**: Bi-weekly meetings incorporate 5-15 minute community presentation slots for external specifications and collaborative proposals [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing evaluation standards, benchmark frameworks, recovery patterns, and quality thresholds for AI agents in enterprise workloads.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group chartered to establish the standards, benchmarks, architectural patterns, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under real-world enterprise conditions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Co-chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group focuses on classifying non-deterministic agent failure modes, developing evaluation and detection frameworks, and formulating standardized recovery patterns[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope
ARWG focuses on agent and multi-agent system behaviors as integrated systems, rather than internal model training or prompt engineering[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Key technical areas within scope include:

- **Accuracy & Reliability Frameworks**: Defining evaluation dimensions, metrics, failure mode classifications, and quality thresholds for autonomous systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Reliable Architecture Patterns**: Standardizing verification loops, grounding to authoritative trust anchors, and structural requirements for deterministic alignment[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Recovery and Corrective Actions**: Developing specifications for safe-state restoration, rollback mechanisms, automated compensation, and human-in-the-loop intervention handoffs[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

### Out of Scope and Dependencies
The working group explicitly delegates telemetry trace emission standards to the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](observability-and-traceability.md), model training to model providers, and regulatory compliance policy to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Technical assumptions include the existence of immutable agent identity schemes (coordinated with [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md)), versioned configurations, and authoritative trust anchors[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

## Deliverables Program
The working group organizes its deliverables into a canonical set (D1–D6 and internal I1)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]:
- **D1 (Taxonomy & Framing)**: Architectural frame and vocabulary for accuracy, reliability, root causes, symptoms, and correction mechanisms, harmonized with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Gap Analysis & Benchmark Survey)**: Applied enterprise requirements analysis across multiple personas (product managers, operations, evaluators, data scientists) to ground evaluation protocols in operational needs[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D3–D6**: Best practice guides, design patterns, and normative evaluation protocols[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was approved on 2026-05-15[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Deliverable tracking was consolidated to D1–D6 in June 2026[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6], progressing actively on D1 taxonomy framing and D2 benchmark gap analysis[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate operational workflow, metadata schemas (SKOS Lite and CNCF Landscape), WG delegate model, standards alignment, and monthly Technical Committee reporting procedures.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative chartered to establish unified terminology, define conceptual boundaries for agentic systems, and maintain an ecosystem directory [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Its goal is to eliminate siloed definitions, prevent duplicate research, and resolve conceptual collisions across foundation working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream maintains two core architectural artifacts:
- **Taxonomy Framework**: Uses a SKOS Lite and CNCF-style metadata schema where each term includes a concise summary alongside detailed scope notes to clarify boundaries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. Terminology actively seeks alignment with established international standards such as ISO and NIST, documenting deviations where necessary [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **Ecosystem Landscape Directory**: Employs CNCF Landscape tooling to map runtimes, frameworks, protocols, and market entities, integrating with the [Agentic AI Landscape](../ecosystem/agentic-ai-landscape.md) mapping effort [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

# Governance and Workflow
The workstream functions via an asynchronous, pull-request-driven workflow coordinated with delegates from across the foundation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]:
- **Working Group Delegates and Domain Editors**: Each working group designates one or two active delegates and domain editors to review shared terms and resolve cross-workspace conflicts [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Intake and Review**: Terms are collected in shared staging documents before submission as pull requests, subject to a definition style guide and AI usage policies requiring human oversight [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
- **Technical Committee Reporting**: The workstream compiles monthly progress reports (`YYYY-MM-report.md`) submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) by the final business day of each month, followed by a 7-day review window prior to merging [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to harmonize terminology across all working groups, establish standardized semantic models, and maintain the interactive Agentic AI Landscape[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates delegates across working groups to curate core domain definitions into a unified vocabulary[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream structures foundational metadata across two key specifications:
- **Taxonomy Schema**: Defined using a SKOS-Lite data schema to model concepts, universal terms, and domain-specific vocabularies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Ecosystem Landscape**: Structured using CNCF-style configuration schemas to power the open-source market map and registry visualizations[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

Terminology intake operates via working group delegates submitting 10–20 core domain terms into a unified review spreadsheet, where cross-domain conflicts, universal categorizations, and consensus culling are resolved prior to merging pull requests into the central repository[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Charter finalized and approved across working groups; portal CI/CD publishing pipeline and SKOS-Lite schemas launched[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) establishes vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and semantic conventions for monitoring, tracing, and debugging AI agent behaviors[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. Led by chairs Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the working group focuses on execution observability, protocol tracking, and multi-agent trace models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes technical deliverables through specialized focus areas and landscape analyses:
- **Focus Groups**: Technical workstreams covering LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability, Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination), and Agentic State, Context & Reasoning[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Use Cases & Gap Analysis**: Documenting industry requirements and telemetry gaps across agent communication protocols, execution traces, and runtime states[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Integration with Resource Discovery**: Coordinating with emerging specifications such as Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) and standards like SPIFFE and ANS for verified agent identification and trace lineage[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Charter kick-off, formation of core focus groups, and initial taxonomy coordination with [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **2026-07**: Streamlined focus group operations by consolidating overlapping LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability streams[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) serves as the bridge between global AI policy developments, regulatory compliance requirements, and technical implementations across the AAIF ecosystem[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]. Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group evaluates emerging agent governance mandates and formulates compliance guidelines[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group conducts continuous mapping and comparative assessments of international policy frameworks:
- **Policy Landscape Mapping**: Cataloging and structuring existing agentic AI policy frameworks, regulatory guidance documents, and industry standards[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **Comparative & Gap Analysis**: Conducting comparative evaluations of open-source agent implementations against identified baseline compliance requirements and risk management benchmarks[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Completed baseline landscape mapping of existing agentic AI policy frameworks and initiated the comparative gap analysis sprint[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
