proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) establishes vendor-neutral threat models, security architectures, defense-in-depth patterns, and best practices for securing autonomous AI agents and runtime environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. Co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group coordinates security requirements across AAIF initiatives and liaises with external security efforts including OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group operates across five active workstream initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, conducting gap analysis across baseline frameworks (MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) to formalize threat modeling deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing actionable security guidance for agent builders and operators [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, curating architectural and mitigation design patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing intake checklists and cross-WG security evaluations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Security and Privacy delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman represent the working group within the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

## Governance and Reporting
The working group submits monthly status updates to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) by the final business day of each calendar month, subject to a 7-day async review window [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]. Reports track progress against charter success metrics including ecosystem adoption, deliverable quality, community participation, and milestone timeliness [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to establish unified terminology, definitions, and domain taxonomy across all AAIF working groups, while curating the interactive ecosystem landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. Led by Junjie Bu, the workstream includes appointed delegates from member working groups to harmonize cross-domain agent concepts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Taxonomy Workflow and Operations
The workstream operates on a phased curation workflow [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]:
- **Unified Term Review**: Collects candidate terms across working groups into a central sheet with consensus tracking and attribution columns [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Discord Feedback**: Surfaces contentious terminology in shared discussion channels before culling or refining definitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **PR-Driven Formalization**: Converts agreed-upon domain boundary definitions into versioned pull requests adhering to CNCF-style schemas and SKOS-Lite structures [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **Landscape Integration**: Connects defined taxonomy categories to the interactive [Agentic AI Landscape](../ecosystem/agentic-ai-landscape.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

## Working Group Representation
Delegates from participating working groups, such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), coordinate boundary definitions and identify distinctions between foundational concepts, such as bots versus agents and Agent Cards versus Agent Blueprints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating a shared agentic AI SKOS-Lite taxonomy and maintaining the interactive ecosystem landscape portal.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative responsible for curating a standardized glossary of agentic AI terminology and maintaining the authoritative foundation ecosystem map [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. By establishing a unified conceptual vocabulary and an interactive landscape visualization, the workstream eliminates terminology silos across technical working groups, prevents redundant ecosystem surveying, and provides enterprises with a consolidated architectural blueprint [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

The workstream operates horizontally across all AAIF working groups, including [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), and [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).

# Architecture / Specification

### Scope & Separation of Concerns
- **Consolidation over Creation:** The workstream ingests and de-duplicates domain glossaries provided by vertical working groups rather than inventing vertical specifications from scratch [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **SKOS-Lite Vocabulary Schema:** Core vocabulary entries are structured using a SKOS-Lite metadata model containing fields such as `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, and `contrastsWith` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Ecosystem Landscape Mapping:** Curates [Agentic AI Landscape](../ecosystem/agentic-ai-landscape.md) data in `landscape.yml`, categorized through iterative delegate consensus [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Portal Distribution:** An automated CI/CD pipeline deploys the Shared Taxonomy Explorer and Landscape web portal to GitHub Pages from the `main` branch upon publication [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].

### Out of Scope
- Vertical domain research papers and narrative compliance analyses [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- Core execution protocol design (such as MCP or A2A protocol specifications) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- Proprietary or closed commercial portals [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Governance

- **Chairs:** Junjie Bu (Google, Chair) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg, Co-Chair) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Charter Approval Date:** 2026-06-21 [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Meeting Cadence:** Weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT / 11:30 AM ET / 4:30 PM BST [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Communication:** Mailing list (`ws-taxonomy-landscape@lists.aaif.io`), Discord channel (`#ws-taxonomy-landscape`), and repository `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared workflow execution models, persistence primitives, and interoperability patterns across agent frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (W&PI) establishes a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems, extending open specifications and producing design patterns to allow agent workflows to operate across frameworks, tools, and execution environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Architecture / Specification

The WG addresses key challenges in agent execution through three core scope pillars [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:

1. **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics**: Defining primitives (tasks, tool calls, branching, retries), step ordering, parallelism, and agent/sub-agent handoff semantics across frameworks.
2. **Long-Running and Stateful Execution**: Patterns for workflows spanning minutes to days, handling state persistence, partial resumption, idempotency, and workflow-level audit logs (distinguished from runtime traces covered by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)).
3. **Tool Invocation and External System Coordination**: Standardized coordination interfaces connecting agents with APIs, CLIs, and enterprise backend services.

# Lifecycle History

- **Charter Approval**: Approved on 2026-05-13 and updated on 2026-07-23 [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Leadership**: Primary Contact/Chair Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Co-Chair Adam Seligman (Workato) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

proposed_concept.title: WG Identity & Trust
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing vendor-neutral standards for AI agent identity, verifiable delegation, action records, and authorization profiles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group (WG Identity & Trust) is an AAIF working group tasked with establishing vendor-neutral architectures, specifications, and taxonomy for agent identity, attestation, authentication, verifiable delegation, and execution accountability.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] The working group operates across three primary sub-working groups focused on Taxonomy, Reference Architecture, and Critical Use Cases.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# Architecture / Specification
WG Identity & Trust organizes its core technical and architectural work into key focus areas:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

- **Taxonomy:** Defines foundational terminology including Agent, Action Record, Audit Log, Consent Receipt, and Human-in-the-Loop. The Action Record is formulated as a tamper-evident, content-private, independently verifiable record of a consequential action (answering "what did this agent verifiably do?" for counterparties, auditors, or legal contexts, distinct from runtime observability traces).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Reference Architecture:** Maintains a components model spanning Discovery Metadata, Identifier, Identity, Authorization, Revocability, Evidence, Verification, and Reputation. It establishes core architectural invariants, such as ensuring sub-agents cannot hold broader permissions than their delegating agents, which cannot exceed initiating user authority.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Authorization Baseline:** Investigates profiling OAuth 2.0 as a normative baseline for cross-platform agent authorization presentations (token formats, delegation chains, and scope expressions), leaving internal backend policy enforcement autonomous.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Critical Use Cases & External Inputs:** Evaluates lifecycle interaction patterns (Internal, B2B, B2C) and incorporates external architectural inputs such as NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace (SAW) reference design (four-layer identity model, delegation records, OpenShell sandbox, and ODIS specification).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07 / 2026-08:** Co-chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE). proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (WG Agentic Commerce) is an AAIF working group responsible for cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, reference architectures, and interface boundaries for agent-mediated commerce.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760] Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group operates under a protocol-neutral charter focused on commerce-facing interfaces and signals across discovery, delegated authority, checkout, payment, fraud signaling, and post-purchase interactions.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's technical scope and core workstreams include:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]

- **Agentic Commerce Capability Map:** The group's primary deliverable, mapping interface boundaries across asynchronous product feeds, live catalog retrieval, negotiation protocols, checkout states, and post-purchase workflows.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **Payment Capability Model:** Clarifies shared abstractions across payment systems around three core primitives: handler, instrument, and credential.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393] It analyzes static payment discovery versus transaction-specific eligibility, delegated tokenization, and custom wallet integration.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]
- **Protocol Analysis & Gap Analysis:** Compares existing protocol models including ACP, UCP, and the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) challenge-credential-receipt flow to evaluate composability, trust assumptions, adapters, and translation requirements.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **Identity, Risk, and Fraud Signaling:** Examines multi-party signal propagation across shopper, agent runtime, merchant, and payment processor boundaries, separating agent identity and risk profiles from human shopper credentials.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04:** Drafted charter and initiated comparative capability mapping across discovery and checkout protocols.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **2026-05:** Approved working group charter and advanced payment-handler abstraction analyses comparing ACP, UCP, and MPP.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]

# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body focused on defining a neutral ecosystem framework for AI agents engaging in commercial transactions, purchasing, and post-purchase activities.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26] Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group evaluates protocols across discovery, negotiation, payment execution, and fulfillment while analyzing cross-cutting concerns like identity, authorization, human oversight, and fraud risk.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical domain around a problem-first commerce lifecycle model:

- **Commerce Lifecycle**: Tracks transitions across product discovery, checkout and negotiation, payment authorization, and post-purchase state handling (including returns, cancellations, refunds, and disputes).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]
- **Capability Map & Gap Analysis**: Evaluates existing protocols (such as Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), Agent Communication Protocol (ACP), Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), and x402) against the end-to-end commerce journey to identify fragmentation and unaddressed integration boundaries.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]
- **Fraud and Trust Signals**: Analyzes bounded fact sharing and risk attestations across agent, platform, merchant, and payment processor boundaries, differentiating agent risk, shopper risk, and delegation bindings.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]
- **Cross-Working Group Dependencies**: Intersects with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for delegated authority, [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) for threat modeling, and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) for event tracing.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]

# Lifecycle History

- **February 2026**: Working group launched; conducted an initial landscape survey of consumer, merchant, platform, wallet, and network participants and identified protocol fragmentation concerns.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]
- **March 2026**: Adopted a lifecycle-oriented method mapping existing protocols across discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase workflows.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]
- **June 2026**: Conducted gap analysis on fraud and trust signals, exploring portable baselines, step-up human verification, and boundaries between signal exchange and fraud-model internals.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]
- **July 2026**: Explored post-purchase state-change requirements and agent wallet integration models including AP2 intent mandates and x402 payment responses.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]

# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is an AAIF body tasked with establishing a standardized, shared vocabulary for agentic AI concepts and curating the foundation's public ecosystem landscape map.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103] Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream arbitrates terminology across all AAIF working groups using a unified review process.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates two primary tracks:

- **SKOS-Lite Taxonomy**: A sequential arbitration model where terms are first evaluated for admission into the unified terminology and subsequently assigned definitions, categories, and broader term relationships via pull requests.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]
- **Ecosystem Landscape Portal**: A public directory and visualization of open-source agent frameworks, protocols, and runtimes mapped against AAIF taxonomy domains.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Transitioned from term collection to formal arbitration; held four weekly review syncs processing 46 terms (13 admitted, 11 culled, 21 held in debate backlog). Admitted terms shipped via PR #33 to launch entries on the public taxonomy portal.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]
- **August 2026**: Cumulative review reached 67 of the 128-term backlog, with 21 admitted terms live in the taxonomy and 25 held in the debate backlog.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow architecture pattern requiring an authorized, uniquely identified human to explicitly approve an immutable proposal before executing a protected effect.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Human Approval Gate pattern ensures that actions carrying risk, audit obligations, or ownership boundaries require explicit judgment from an accountable person before execution occurs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]. The pattern pairs durable execution waiting with an immutable proposal presentation so that human authorization applies strictly to the exact payload reviewed.

# Architecture / Specification
Under this pattern, an agent or workflow engine constructs an immutable proposal and enters a durable wait state while surfacing the proposal to an authorized human interface[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

```text
immutable proposal ──► present to authorized human ──► explicit decision
                              │                           │
                              └── durable wait ─────────┘
                                          │
                          decision record: who · what · when
```

Key invariants required across implementations include[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]:
- Approvers must be uniquely identified human principals; shared accounts do not qualify.
- The interaction surface displays the exact, immutable proposal version bound to the decision.
- Decisions must be explicit; timeouts, delivery failures, or system errors never imply approval.
- The decision record captures the proposal version, approver identity, decision, and timestamp under a shared run identity.
- Any proposal modification invalidates pending reviews and requires a new approval decision.
- Pending approvals enforce deadlines with explicit expiry or escalation paths, backed by idempotency protections against duplicate execution.

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Reference Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural model organizing AAIF reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs and composable workflow patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Reference Architecture Model is an architectural decision proposed within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to structure reference architectures around concrete practitioner jobs rather than structural agent counts[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. This approach separates end-to-end operational compositions from reusable sub-patterns.

# Architecture / Specification
The decision establishes explicit definitions and separation of concerns across workstream artifacts[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]:
- **Reference Architectures**: Complete compositions of reusable patterns, capabilities, boundaries, operational guarantees, and exit states solving a named practitioner job.
- **Patterns**: Independently adoptable solutions to recurring workflow sub-problems (such as the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)) that define their own invariants and failure modes.
- **Structural Roles**: Classifications like single-agent or multi-agent topologies are treated as internal implementation characteristics rather than top-level architectural taxonomy categories.
- **Validation**: Scenarios and use cases serve to validate architectures, identifying missing variants or distinct practitioner jobs.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-ref-arch` skill is an automated agent capability curated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to evaluate open-source AI agent tools, frameworks, and specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b]. It automates the generation of structured AAIF reference architecture documents and observability assessments.

# Architecture / Specification
The skill executes a standardized multi-step evaluation workflow[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b]:
1. **Source Gathering**: Inspects target repositories, READMEs, architecture schemas, APIs, and reference implementations.
2. **Reference Architecture Production**: Generates structured markdown specifying project metadata, scope layer (primitive, orchestration, or system), prerequisites, ASCII architecture diagrams, and instrumentation mechanics.
3. **Telemetry & Cost Assessment**: Compiles sample trace outputs, cost profiles, validation criteria, and known operational limitations.
4. **Structured Commit**: Formats and stores the evaluation assessment for inclusion in AAIF knowledge repositories.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates telemetry specifications, behavioral trace models, and execution visibility across multi-agent environments and LLM primitives in the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]. The group focuses on standardized tracing from local runtime executions to cross-boundary agent interactions, establishing common telemetry payloads and evaluation hooks.

The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

# Architecture / Specification

### Focus Group Structure
To address execution bottlenecks and streamline proposal reviews, the working group restructured its operational tracks into three core focus areas[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]:
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability** (Lead: Zayne Turner): Focuses on Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) observability, tracing skill discovery, pre-execution trust decisions, and making skills first-class citizens in telemetry models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination** (Lead: Ty Smith): Develops modular observability maps and agentic runtime context telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Agentic State & Context** (Lead: Govindaraj): Covers reasoning and state observability gap and landscape analyses[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

### Technical Work Items
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A standard recommendation bridging application-layer trace libraries with the OpenTelemetry (OTel) core specification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) & Agent Action Capsules (AAC)**: Collaborations exploring CBOR-encoded verifiable telemetry and peer-to-peer observability stacks in conjunction with LibP2P and IETF/IRTF accountability efforts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Cross-WG Taxonomy Coordination**: Continuous alignment with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to integrate universal and observability-specific terminology[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) mission by establishing a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]. It produces interoperability guidelines, open specification extensions, and design patterns that allow AI agent workflows to operate seamlessly across diverse frameworks, tools, and execution environments.

# Governance and Operations

### Leadership
The working group leadership was appointed by the Platinum and Gold members for the term spanning March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]:
- **Chair**: Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Co-Chair**: Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

### Meeting Cadence
The working group meets biweekly on Thursdays at 8:00 AM PT[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical outputs across several collaborative workstreams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]:
- **Taxonomy**: Establishing a shared core vocabulary for agent workflows to eliminate ambiguity across technical deliverables[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
- **Reference Architectures**: Documenting workflow architecture patterns applying standardized terminology and runtime principles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Analyzing concrete multi-step enterprise and autonomous agent use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group operates under the Agentic AI Foundation to establish unified threat models, defense-in-depth architecture patterns, and operational security frameworks for agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3]. It coordinates deliverable workstreams across threat modeling, best practices, and design pattern catalogs while aligning security-specific terms with the foundational taxonomy initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical outputs across several core deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3]:

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Evaluates failure modes and threat vectors specific to autonomous agent runtime environments.
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical guidance spanning secrets management, secure tool invocation (including Model Context Protocol and supply chain vectors), guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable security and mitigation architectures for agent deployment.
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to standardize security and privacy terminology[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].

Specific architectural domains such as identity and delegated authorization architecture (e.g., SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693) are scoped out of this group and handled by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06**: Transitioned from formation to active execution across five workstreams, transitioning taxonomy efforts to the cross-WG stream and producing first drafts for threat modeling and best practices[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].
- **2026-07**: Published initial drafts for the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Best Practices Guide as pull requests and finalized the structure for the Design Patterns Catalog[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3].

# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates telemetry specifications, execution trace models, and visibility standards for autonomous AI agents within the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]. The group maintains open contribution standards and formal working methods to ensure deliverable tracking, transparent status reporting, and cross-group collaboration remain discoverable and accountable on GitHub[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

# Architecture / Specification

The group operates on a GitHub-centric workflow where repository issues and pull requests serve as the primary source of truth for work items, decisions, and durable artifacts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

## Work Tracking and Lifecycle States

Work items are managed through structured GitHub issue templates tracking the outcome, workstream, owner, next steps, and acceptance criteria[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50]. Standardized status markers include[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:

- `needs owner`: Valid work identified but lacking an active driver.
- `scoping`: Boundaries, inputs, and desired outcomes are being defined.
- `in progress`: Active drafting, research, or coordination.
- `ready for review`: Awaiting feedback, decision, or approval.
- `blocked`: Dependent on external decisions or inputs.
- `done`: Landed, integrated, or formally resolved.

## Governance and Reporting Cadence

The working group maintains an active operating rhythm synchronized with regular meetings and reports up to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on a monthly cadence using merged repository artifacts and tracked issues as the source material[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Security guidance detailing failure patterns and decision frameworks across secrets, tool invocation, guardrails, evals, and forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a practitioner guideline produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to address operational and architectural security challenges in autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]. It structures recommendations around paired failure patterns, defensive controls, and practical decision frameworks across five distinct technical domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification

The guide outlines security controls and evaluation methodologies across five primary domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:

1. **Secrets Management**: Mitigating leakage, context-window exposure, and credential proliferation in agent execution environments.
2. **Secure Tool Invocation**: Managing integration risks, supply chain integrity, and communication protocols such as Model Context Protocol (MCP).
3. **Guardrails**: Implementing defense-in-depth filters, validation gates, and input/output guardrails during prompt execution and tool calls.
4. **Evaluation Frameworks**: Systematically benchmarking vulnerability resilience and security regressions.
5. **Post-Incident Forensics**: Preserving tamper-evident execution logs, agent telemetry, and decision trails for retrospective analysis.

## Scoping Boundaries

Identity management and delegated authorization models (such as SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693) are maintained separately by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to preserve separation of concerns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, review checklists, and security best practices for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPAA) establishes security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI ecosystem within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. Its mission is to produce open threat models, shared taxonomy contributions, and design patterns that model providers, tool builders, and peer working groups can adopt to implement shared responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

# Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group organizes its technical activities around five core workstreams and deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Benchmarking agent security threats and gaps against established industry frameworks including MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF, while aligning threat models with STRIDE and PASTA methodologies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical defense-in-depth and operational guidance for secure agent deployment, collaborating with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) on agent authorization, authentication, human attribution, and human-in-the-loop safeguards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural templates and reusable design patterns addressing agent isolation, signed tool invocations, and runtime sandboxing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: A cross-functional review mechanism to assess specifications across sister working groups, resolve scope boundaries, and establish baseline security requirements[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Curating security- and privacy-specific terms (such as guardrails, constraints, and runtime limits) into the cross-cutting unified taxonomy managed by the [Taxonomy and Landscape workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Governance and Operations

- **Leadership**: Chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and Co-Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), appointed for the term March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- **Meetings**: Meets biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT on Zoom LFX, maintaining publicly accessible meeting archives, recordings, and open Discord channels[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **PR and Acceptance Workflow**: Technical deliverables are developed in the open on GitHub; working group pull requests within charter scope merge after working group review and consensus without requiring advance [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) approval, with monthly reports submitted to the TC[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Hardware-isolated execution pattern placing policy decision points and evidence signers in a confidential environment while keeping the agent outside the trust boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Attested Isolated Runtime is a security design pattern for deployments where the infrastructure operator is inside the threat model[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. Developed within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), it isolates the policy enforcement point and evidence signing keys inside a hardware confidential computing boundary while leaving the AI agent outside.

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern defines four core requirements for confidential agent policy enforcement[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:

1. **Isolate the Enforcement Point, Exclude the Agent:** The policy decision point and evidence signer run in a hardware-isolated environment (such as AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, ARM CCA, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing, or TPM 2.0). The agent execution engine itself remains outside the trusted computing base (TCB) because agent code processes untrusted, attacker-influenced input as normal operation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
2. **Internal Key Generation:** Cryptographic signing keys are generated inside the isolated boundary and bound to hardware measurements.
3. **Policy Sealing:** Policy bundles, system prompts, tool schemas, and model weight digests are sealed to cryptographic measurements and released only upon successful appraisal[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
4. **Independent Verifier Appraisal:** An external, independent verifier appraises per-unit-of-work attestation evidence before sensitive data release (aligned with RFC 9334, RFC 9711, RFC 8747, IETF SCITT, and SLSA)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

A software-only emulation mode is specified as a valid deployment for testing, development, and non-confidential hardware environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Open Questions

The working group is reviewing three open architectural questions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:

- Whether the agent should strictly remain outside the trust boundary or if specialized agent modules belong inside the TCB.
- The exact scope of measured artifacts, specifically how dynamic state like retrieved context and working memory should be managed.
- Establishing a shared assurance vocabulary (signed, attested, transparency-anchored) coordinated with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized agent skill for first-pass issue classification, severity assessment, root-cause hypothesizing, and prompt injection containment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Issue Analysis skill provides a structured workflow for AI agents to perform first-pass triage and root-cause analysis on repository issue submissions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. It establishes rigorous boundaries treating all issue content as untrusted data rather than instructions, mitigating indirect prompt injection.

# Architecture / Specification

The skill executes across four distinct workflow phases[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:

1. **Data Containment and Injection Detection:** Issue content is isolated inside delimited blocks and treated exclusively as data. Directives attempting to override agent instructions or trigger unauthorized actions flag `injectionSuspected` with explanatory notes[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
2. **Codebase Grounding:** The agent inspects local source code in read-only mode to substantiate reported symptoms against concrete implementation files rather than abstract subsystems[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
3. **Historical Reference Matching:** The agent matches the issue against past curated human reviews to align severity ratings and root-cause reasoning[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b].
4. **Structured Drafting:** Findings are synthesized into classified bug or security reports containing reproducibility state, concrete hypotheses, and actionable remediations[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive market map and open-source directory maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18]. It catalogs open-source AI agent runtimes, protocol implementations, developer tooling, and gateway infrastructure across the ecosystem.

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape groups tools and platforms into structured infrastructure categories:

- **Frameworks & Infrastructure / Orchestration & Multi-Agent:** Production-grade AI gateways and orchestration runtimes managing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, agent-to-agent communication, and model inference routing (e.g., Higress and AgentGateway)[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].
- **Protocols & Standards:** Projects implementing standardized agent interfaces such as the [Agent Client Protocol](../projects/agent-client-protocol.md).
- **Developer Tooling & Skills:** Curated agent capabilities and skills bundles, such as [Public Agent Skills](../ecosystem/public-agent-skills.md).

mutations.rationale: Incorporate the official template structure, classification taxonomy, and reference format from the submission-analyser skill files.

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized agent skill template and workflow for first-pass issue classification, severity assessment, component isolation, and diagnostic recommendations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `issue-analysis` skill defines a standardized analytical template and workflow for AI agents performing first-pass intake, classification, and triage on project issues and feature requests [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]. It focuses agent output on maintainer-centric summaries, concrete component scoping, structured hypothesis testing, and actionable next steps without generating unverified patches.

# Architecture / Specification

The skill mandates a structured report format containing seven core analytical sections [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]:

- **Summary**: A single-paragraph restatement of the issue in maintainer terms allowing rapid assessment without reading the original thread [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Classification**:
  - `Type`: `bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, or `ambiguous` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  - `Severity`: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `informational` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  - `Reproducibility`: `reproducible`, `not-reproducible`, `insufficient-information`, or `not-applicable` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  - `Severity rationale`: A 1–2 sentence justification evaluating user impact, precedent, and existing workarounds [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Affected components**: Explicit paths or module names (e.g., `src/config/loader.ts`) rather than generic component descriptions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].
- **Root-cause hypotheses**: Mechanism descriptions explaining the underlying defect or design constraint alongside criteria to confirm or refute them [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].
- **Suggested actions**: Ordered diagnostic steps, files to inspect, or information requests prioritized for maintainers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Open questions**: Specific follow-up inquiries directed to the reporter before taking action [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Related past reviews**: Citations to relevant reference examples and past analysis cases [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].

# References

- [Public Agent Skills](../ecosystem/public-agent-skills.md)
- [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../policies-guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)

mutations.rationale: Establish reference architecture for OpenTelemetry as the vendor-neutral observability substrate for AI agents based on WG Observability documentation.

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture: OpenTelemetry
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral observability framework and collector pipeline for instrumenting, processing, and exporting AI agent traces, metrics, and logs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
OpenTelemetry (OTel) provides a vendor-neutral observability framework that standardizes the collection, processing, and export of traces, metrics, and logs across AI agent infrastructure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]. Maintained under the guidance of the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), this reference architecture defines telemetry pipelines connecting instrumented AI agents, LLM gateways, and MCP servers to downstream observability backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

# Architecture / Specification
The OpenTelemetry architecture for agentic systems operates across three core layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]:
- **Instrumented Applications**: AI agents, LLM gateways, and tool servers emit trace spans and metrics formatted with standardized semantic conventions (`gen_ai.*` attributes) using language SDKs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **Wire Protocol**: Telemetry is transmitted over OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) via gRPC (port 4317) or HTTP/Protobuf/JSON (port 4318) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **Collector Pipeline**: The OpenTelemetry Collector receives telemetry through pluggable receivers, applies filtering and batch processing, and routes signals via exporters to target storage backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

mutations.rationale: Establish reference architecture for PyTorch Profiler hardware and op dispatch tracing from WG Observability documentation.

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture: PyTorch Profiler
proposed_concept.description: Execution tracing framework bridging PyTorch operator dispatch and ATen backend execution to GPU kernels and Chrome Trace timeline formats.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The PyTorch Profiler reference architecture documents runtime execution path capture from Python-level tensor operator dispatch through the C++ ATen backend to underlying GPU hardware kernel execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7]. Coordinated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it details how framework-level semantics are correlated with accelerator activities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7].

# Architecture / Specification
The profiler integrates directly into PyTorch's execution dispatcher and hardware tracing backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7]:
- **Op Dispatch Callbacks**: `RecordFunction` hooks capture operator names, input tensor shapes, data types, and Python/C++ stack traces at dispatch time [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7].
- **Hardware Tracing Substrate**: Bundled Kineto runtime interfaces with NVIDIA CUPTI and AMD roctracer to trace CUDA/HIP kernel launches, memory allocations, and inter-device communication [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7].
- **Trace Output**: Generates Chrome Trace Format JSON consumable by timeline analysis tools including Perfetto, TensorBoard, and Holistic Trace Analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7].

mutations.rationale: Establish reference architecture for Linux kernel FTrace infrastructure from WG Observability documentation.

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture: FTrace
proposed_concept.description: In-kernel tracing framework providing zero-overhead function tracing and event recording via the tracefs filesystem interface.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
FTrace is the built-in Linux kernel function tracing and event recording infrastructure managed via the virtual `tracefs` filesystem interface [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1]. Curated under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), this reference architecture describes low-friction kernel execution inspection without mandatory external userspace dependencies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].

# Architecture / Specification
FTrace instrumentation relies on compiler-assisted hooks and in-kernel buffering [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1]:
- **Dynamic Patching**: Kernel functions compiled with `-mfentry` contain 5-byte NOP instructions when inactive, dynamically patched via `text_poke_bp` to invoke tracing callers when enabled [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].
- **Tracefs Control**: Tracing configuration, event filtering, and output streams are managed through `/sys/kernel/tracing/` (or debugfs mounts) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].
- **Tracer Engines**: Supports function tracing, function graph call-tree execution timing, static tracepoint events, and in-kernel histogram triggers written to per-CPU lock-free ring buffers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].

mutations.rationale: Comparative aggregate assessment of Linux kernel tracing technologies (LTTng, perf, FTrace) from WG Observability.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Kernel Tracing Comparative Assessment
proposed_concept.description: Comparative assessment of Linux tracing frameworks analyzing architectural trade-offs between LTTng, perf, and FTrace.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Linux kernel tracing assessment compares the three primary kernel instrumentation frameworks—LTTng, perf, and FTrace—evaluating their data paths, performance overheads, and suitability for system-level observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]. Curated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the evaluation highlights architectural trade-offs across userspace tracing, hardware performance counters, and built-in kernel diagnostics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].

# Architecture / Specification
The frameworks present distinct operational models and feature coverage [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]:
- **LTTng**: Employs external kernel modules and userspace daemons (LTTng-UST) with lock-free per-CPU ring buffers, exporting Common Trace Format (CTF) binary streams optimized for high throughput with minimal overhead (~50–150 ns per enabled tracepoint) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
- **perf**: Integrates directly into the kernel and userspace tooling (`perf_events`), specializing in hardware Performance Monitoring Unit (PMU) counters, sampling, uprobes, and system profiling writing to `perf.data` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
- **FTrace**: Standard in-tree kernel infrastructure operated via `tracefs`, optimized for function entry/exit graph tracing and zero-dependency debugging [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].

mutations.rationale: Authoritative reference architecture assessment documenting the Agent Trace open specification for line-level code attribution across AI coding agents.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Trace
proposed_concept.description: Open specification and reference hook architecture capturing line-level code attribution traces emitted during AI coding agent sessions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent Trace is an open telemetry specification for capturing granular, line-level code attribution and execution history from AI coding agents like Cursor and Claude Code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756]. It operates as a local-first telemetry layer recording model provenance, prompt interactions, file edits, and shell command executions within a version-controlled repository [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

Maintained under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the architecture defines event dispatch hooks and structured JSONL append logging without requiring centralized collection backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

# Architecture / Specification

Agent Trace captures lifecycle hooks emitted during agent editing and execution sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756]:

- **Hook Dispatcher**: Intercepts IDE and agent events (`afterFileEdit`, `afterTabFileEdit`, `afterShellExecution`, `PostToolUse`, `sessionStart/End`) passed via JSON on standard input [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].
- **Trace Output**: Appends structured trace records to `.agent-trace/traces.jsonl`, binding edits to file paths, diffs, model identifiers, conversation context, and VCS revisions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].
- **Decoupled Consumption**: Decouples write-path trace emission from downstream aggregation tools, CI policy gates, or compliance dashboards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

mutations.rationale: Authoritative reference architecture assessment of NVIDIA Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute GPU profiling tools in AI agent infrastructure.

proposed_concept.title: NVIDIA Nsight
proposed_concept.description: GPU profiling and timeline tracing suite for hardware counter analysis, kernel execution metrics, and multi-GPU communication across CUDA AI workloads.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

NVIDIA Nsight is a GPU profiling and performance analysis suite composed of Nsight Systems (`nsys`) for system-wide timeline tracing and Nsight Compute (`ncu`) for per-kernel hardware counter profiling [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff]. It evaluates hardware accelerator performance across model execution and AI workload dispatch [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].

Evaluated within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), Nsight bridges the application framework layer (e.g., [PyTorch Profiler](pytorch-profiler.md)) and CUDA driver runtimes down to GPU hardware counters [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].

# Architecture / Specification

The Nsight architecture operates at the orchestration and hardware execution layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff]:

- **CUPTI Instrumentation**: The CUDA Profiling Tools Interface intercepts runtime API calls, kernel launches (`cuLaunchKernel`), memory transfers, and synchronization primitives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].
- **NVTX Range Annotations**: Enables applications and libraries (cuDNN, cuBLAS, NCCL) to inject user-defined markers and hierarchical range annotations across training and inference passes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].
- **Timeline Tracing vs. Kernel Replay**: Nsight Systems tracks end-to-end multi-GPU timelines with minimal overhead, while Nsight Compute uses multi-pass kernel replay to measure tensor core utilization, memory bandwidth, and occupancy [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].

mutations.rationale: Authoritative reference architecture assessment evaluating Datadog LLM Observability and APM infrastructure for AI agent runtimes.

proposed_concept.title: Datadog
proposed_concept.description: Full-stack commercial observability platform providing APM distributed tracing, LLM Observability SDKs, and infrastructure monitoring for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Datadog is an integrated SaaS observability platform providing end-to-end distributed tracing, metrics, logging, and dedicated LLM Observability for AI agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df]. It combines host/container agents with language-specific APM and LLM tracing SDKs to capture agent, tool, workflow, and model invocation telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].

Evaluated within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), Datadog provides a complete vendor pipeline spanning collection, ingestion, storage, visualization, and alerting [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].

# Architecture / Specification

The platform architecture is structured across application instrumentation, local collectors, and SaaS analytics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df]:

- **LLM Observability SDK**: `ddtrace.llmobs` instruments AI agent code with dedicated spans (`agent`, `workflow`, `tool`, `llm`), capturing prompt/completion text, token counts, model metadata, latency, and estimated cost [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].
- **Datadog Agent**: Host/daemon container collecting traces (port 8126), metrics, and logs, aggregating and buffering telemetry before egress [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].
- **Correlated APM Pipeline**: Unifies LLM span trees with traditional distributed traces from gateways, databases, queues, and external APIs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].

mutations.rationale: Authoritative reference architecture assessment documenting LTTng Userspace Tracing (UST) shared-memory lock-free instrumentation.

proposed_concept.title: LTTng-UST
proposed_concept.description: High-throughput, low-overhead userspace tracing framework recording application events into shared-memory ring buffers without kernel transitions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

LTTng Userspace Tracing (LTTng-UST) is a high-performance instrumentation library that records trace events directly from application code into shared-memory ring buffers with near-zero overhead [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c]. It executes on the fast path without kernel transitions or system call locks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c].

Maintained under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) tracing taxonomy, LTTng-UST complements kernel tracing solutions like [ftrace](ftrace.md) and provides unprivileged userspace event extraction in Common Trace Format (CTF) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c].

# Architecture / Specification

LTTng-UST instrumentation operates via decoupled daemons and shared memory [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c]:

- **Tracepoint Providers**: Static C/C++ tracepoints or language agents (Python, Java JUL/Log4j) compiled into the application execute Userspace RCU (`liburcu`) primitives to check trace enablement and write payload data [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c].
- **Shared-Memory Buffers**: Per-process or per-channel ring buffers residing in `/dev/shm` isolate writer threads from consumer threads [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c].
- **Consumer and Session Daemons**: Unprivileged user session daemons coordinate tracing sessions while asynchronous consumer daemons extract event streams into binary CTF files on disk [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c].

mutations.rationale: Authoritative reference architecture assessment detailing Linux device driver tracing, structured logging, dynamic debug, and subsystem tracepoints.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing
proposed_concept.description: Multi-tier instrumentation and debugging framework for Linux device drivers utilizing structured logging, dynamic debug, tracepoints, and bus monitors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux Driver Tracing covers the layered instrumentation and debugging mechanisms available in the Linux kernel for device drivers and hardware subsystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]. It bridges generic kernel tracing infrastructures such as [ftrace](ftrace.md) and userspace tools with driver-specific diagnostic interfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

Cataloged by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), driver tracing provides runtime visibility into device interactions across USB, network, block, GPU/DRM, and bus controllers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

# Architecture / Specification

The driver tracing architecture spans five primary instrumentation layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]:

- **Structured Device Logging**: Standardized macros (`dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, `dev_err`, `dev_warn`) emitting device-attributed messages into the kernel ring buffer (`printk` / `dmesg`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`)**: Runtime call-site control allowing fine-grained toggling of debug log statements by module, file, function, line, or format string without recompilation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Static Kernel Tracepoints**: `TRACE_EVENT()` macros defining structured, typed binary event payloads consumed via `tracefs` or `perf` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Bus and Subsystem Tracers**: Protocol-level sniffers including `usbmon`, `blktrace`, and `devcoredump` for hardware fault extraction and packet analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

mutations.rationale: Captures the Common Trace Format (CTF) reference architecture establishing binary trace encoding standards across kernel and userspace tracers.

proposed_concept.title: Common Trace Format (CTF)
proposed_concept.description: Self-describing binary trace encoding format optimized for zero-copy write paths and nanosecond-precision event capture via embedded TSDL metadata.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Common Trace Format (CTF) specification defines a self-describing binary trace encoding optimized for zero-copy write paths, enabling trace producers to record high-frequency events at nanosecond precision with minimal compute overhead [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf]. CTF operates as the wire and storage encoding layer beneath tracing infrastructure rather than a standalone runtime tool [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf].

CTF is produced by tracers such as [LTTng-UST](./lttng-ust.md) and barectf and consumed by diagnostic readers including Babeltrace2 and [Trace Compass](./trace-compass.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf].

# Architecture / Specification

A CTF trace is organized as a file system directory containing an embedded plain-text metadata stream written in Trace Stream Description Language (TSDL) alongside one or more binary event data streams [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf]:
- **TSDL Metadata (`metadata`)**: Defines trace environment parameters, clock sources (frequencies, precisions), packet context layouts, and event field payload schemas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf].
- **Binary Data Streams (`channel*_*`)**: Native-endian, bit-packed event streams segmented into discrete packets with header contexts (timestamps, packet sizes, content sizes, packet sequence numbers, and dropped event counters) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf].
- **Zero-Copy Serialization**: Producers append raw binary structs directly to ring buffer allocations without intermediate text serialization or memory copies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf].

# Validation and Diagnostics

Trace validity is verified by inspecting packet magic headers (`0xc1fc1fc1`) and parsing stream contents against metadata using Babeltrace2 CLI utilities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf].

# References

- Working Group: [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Related Architecture: [LTTng Userspace Tracing](./lttng-ust.md)
- Related Architecture: [Eclipse Trace Compass](./trace-compass.md)

mutations.rationale: Captures the LTTng kernel tracing reference architecture describing high-throughput kernel event extraction via lock-free ring buffers.

proposed_concept.title: LTTng Kernel Tracing
proposed_concept.description: High-throughput, low-overhead Linux kernel tracing framework capturing system events into per-CPU lock-free ring buffers formatted as CTF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

LTTng (Linux Trace Toolkit: next generation) provides high-throughput, low-overhead Linux kernel tracing through per-CPU lock-free ring buffers and the [Common Trace Format](./common-trace-format.md), enabling always-on production tracing with nanosecond-precision timestamping [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e].

Operating at the system infrastructure layer, LTTng instruments kernel subsystems—such as task scheduling, block I/O, networking, memory management, and system call entry/exit hooks—streaming binary events through a multi-daemon pipeline to persistent trace archives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e].

# Architecture / Specification

The LTTng kernel tracing pipeline is composed of the following components [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e]:
- **Kernel Probe Modules (`lttng-modules`)**: Attach callbacks to static kernel tracepoints, evaluate in-kernel filter bytecode, and serialize binary event fields directly into memory [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e].
- **Lock-Free Ring Buffers**: Per-CPU shared-memory buffers divided into sub-buffers allowing atomic index reservation without locking or syscall overhead on the recording path [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e].
- **Session and Consumer Daemons**: The `lttng-sessiond` service manages session orchestration and probe activation, while `lttng-consumerd` asynchronously drains completed sub-buffers to disk or relay networks in CTF binary format [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e].

# References

- Working Group: [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Architecture: [Common Trace Format](./common-trace-format.md)
- Architecture: [LTTng Userspace Tracing](./lttng-ust.md)
- Resource: [Linux Kernel Tracing Comparison](../resources/linux-kernel-tracing-comparison.md)

mutations.rationale: Documents the Linux perf reference architecture for PMU-driven hardware counter sampling and kernel event profiling.

proposed_concept.title: Linux perf
proposed_concept.description: Hardware-assisted CPU profiling and event tracing framework utilizing CPU Performance Monitoring Units and the perf_events kernel subsystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux `perf` (perf_events) provides hardware-assisted performance profiling and execution tracing spanning from hardware Performance Monitoring Units (PMUs) through the kernel's `perf_events` subsystem to userspace analysis utilities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1]. It enables counting and sampling modes across hardware counters (CPU cycles, instructions, cache misses, branch mispredictions), software tracepoints, and dynamic probes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1].

# Architecture / Specification

The perf architecture operates across three distinct operational layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1]:
- **Hardware PMU Layer**: CPU hardware counters and advanced capture facilities (such as Intel PT branch packets and Last Branch Record rings) configured to trigger non-maskable interrupts (NMIs) upon counter overflow [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1].
- **Kernel `perf_events` Subsystem**: Managed via the `perf_event_open()` syscall, creating kernel event instances mapped to per-process or per-CPU ring buffers with lock-free mmap rings [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1].
- **Userspace Utilities**: CLI tooling (`perf stat`, `perf record`, `perf report`, `perf script`, `perf trace`) enabling live counter aggregation, stack unwinding (FP/DWARF/LBR), and flame graph generation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1].

# References

- Working Group: [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Architecture: [ftrace](./ftrace.md)
- Resource: [Linux Kernel Tracing Comparison](../resources/linux-kernel-tracing-comparison.md)

mutations.rationale: Documents the Wireshark and TShark reference architecture for packet capture, protocol dissection, and network trace export.

proposed_concept.title: Wireshark Network Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Deep packet inspection and protocol analysis architecture utilizing privilege-separated capture engines and modular multi-layer protocol dissectors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Wireshark is a deep packet inspection and network protocol analysis framework that captures raw wire packets, reconstructs multi-layer protocol state, and extracts structured telemetry for offline diagnostics and live inspection [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1]. Operating at the network transport and interface layer, it provides visibility into inter-host distributed communication, API flows, and RPC transport [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1].

# Architecture / Specification

The capture and analysis engine follows a privilege-separated, modular design [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1]:
- **Privilege-Separated Capture Engine (`dumpcap`)**: Minimal attack-surface capture process holding elevated privileges (`CAP_NET_RAW` / `libpcap`) to stream network frames from packet sockets into PCAPNG files [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1].
- **Dissector Engine (`libwireshark`)**: Modular protocol parser library supporting over 3,000 protocol dissectors arranged hierarchically to parse encapsulated frame payloads from Ethernet up through application layers (HTTP/2, gRPC, TLS) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1].
- **Structured Export Interfaces**: TShark and analysis engines output packet representations into JSON, PDML, and text streams, incorporating decrypted payload extraction when session key material is available [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1].

# References

- Working Group: [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Architecture: [Trace Compass](./trace-compass.md)

mutations.rationale: Captures the Eclipse Trace Compass and Incubator reference architecture for multi-layer trace correlation and interval tree state systems.

proposed_concept.title: Eclipse Trace Compass
proposed_concept.description: Multi-format trace analysis and visualization framework correlating kernel, userspace, GPU, and network traces via a disk-backed state system engine.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Eclipse Trace Compass is a multi-format trace analysis and visualization framework that correlates heterogeneous trace streams—including kernel, userspace, GPU, network, and AI framework traces—through a unified state-system engine [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a]. Instead of acting as a trace producer, Trace Compass ingests multi-source traces to reconstruct end-to-end timeline state across hardware counters, OS schedulers, and high-level execution graphs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].

# Architecture / Specification

Trace Compass centers on a modular trace intake, state reconstruction, and presentation pipeline [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a]:
- **Multi-Format Input Parsers**: Native ingestion for [Common Trace Format (CTF)](./common-trace-format.md), [ftrace](./ftrace.md), [perf](./perf.md), PCAP/PCAPNG, and Chrome Trace JSON (such as [PyTorch Profiler](./pytorch-profiler.md) outputs) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].
- **State System Engine**: Builds history trees and disk-backed interval trees that track attribute state transitions over time, enabling sub-millisecond timeline queries across gigabyte-scale trace archives without full re-scans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].
- **Trace Synchronization**: Correlates independent clock domains across multi-node or host-guest systems using convex-hull algorithms and shared network or RPC exchange points [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].
- **Trace Server Protocol (TSP)**: Enables headless and remote trace querying via RESTful APIs, decoupling trace computation backends from front-end analysis clients and AI model inspection extensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].

# References

- Architecture: [LTTng Userspace Tracing](./lttng-ust.md)
