mutations.rationale: Updates Linux driver tracing reference architecture with comprehensive coverage of dynamic debug, subsystem-specific tracers, and hardware counter models.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing Mechanisms
proposed_concept.description: Multi-tier instrumentation and debugging framework for Linux device drivers utilizing structured logging, dynamic debug, tracepoints, and debugfs state inspection.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux Driver Tracing Mechanisms provide a layered set of observability, telemetry, and debugging primitives specifically tailored for kernel device drivers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]. Spanning structured device logging (`dev_dbg`), dynamic debug control (`dyndbg`), custom tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`), subsystem tracers (`usbmon`, `blktrace`), debugfs inspection nodes, and crash snapshots (`devcoredump`), these facilities enable granular observation of hardware-software interaction without driver recompilation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].

# Architecture / Specification

The driver observation model encompasses four core monitoring layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]:
- **Structured Logging and Dynamic Debug**: Drivers embed standard `dev_dbg()`, `dev_info()`, and `dev_err()` callsites decorated with struct `device` identifiers. Through the dynamic debug control interface (`/sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control`), administrators selectively enable individual callsites, source files, or driver modules at runtime with zero overhead when disabled [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
- **Tracepoint Event Subsystem**: Subsystem-specific `TRACE_EVENT` macros provide statically typed, binary-serialized event capture exposed via `tracefs` and consumable by [ftrace](./ftrace.md), [perf](./perf.md), and [LTTng](./lttng-kernel.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
- **Hardware Counter and State Inspection**: Hardware metrics (PCIe AER, NVMe error logs, network interface ring counters, GPU execution engines) are queried through sysfs attributes, debugfs directories, and perf events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
- **Post-Mortem Diagnostics (`devcoredump`)**: Kernel infrastructure capturing device register dumps and state snapshots upon hardware failure for non-destructive offline analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].

# References

- Working Group: [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Architecture: [ftrace](./ftrace.md)
- Architecture: [Linux perf](./perf.md)
- Resource: [Linux Kernel Tracing Comparison](../resources/linux-kernel-tracing-comparison.md)

mutations.rationale: Add PostHog reference architecture documenting client-side telemetry ingestion, PII sanitization, and product analytics integration for AI agent runtimes.

proposed_concept.title: PostHog Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Open product analytics and event telemetry sink capturing sanitized behavioral events and adoption metrics from AI agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

PostHog operates as an external telemetry and product analytics sink for AI agent frameworks, capturing structured adoption, session lifecycle, and error metrics without exposing personally identifiable information (PII) or sensitive prompts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]. Within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), PostHog represents an ingestion pattern for high-level practitioner usage analytics distinct from low-level execution tracing.

# Architecture / Specification

Agent runtimes, such as [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md), interface directly with the PostHog Capture API (`https://us.i.posthog.com/capture/` or `eu.i.posthog.com`) using lightweight HTTPS POST payloads without requiring full vendor SDKs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]:

- **Client Pipeline**: Implements an installation tracker (generating a persistent UUID v4), event builders for lifecycle phases (`session_start`, `error`, `onboarding_*`), and a dedicated PII sanitizer stripping paths, tokens, emails, and API keys [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].
- **Payload Format**: Sends JSON containing `api_key`, `event`, `distinct_id`, `properties`, and `timestamp` directly to the PostHog ingestion pipeline [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].
- **Storage and Processing**: Ingested events flow through Kafka into ClickHouse, enabling cohort segmentation, funnel analysis, and feature flag management [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].

# References

- PostHog Reference Architecture in [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].

mutations.rationale: Add AMD roctracer and rocprofiler reference architecture detailing GPU kernel dispatch, MFMA matrix core tracing, and ROCm profiling workflows.

proposed_concept.title: AMD roctracer and rocprofiler Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Open-source GPU profiling stack for tracing HIP/HSA runtime API dispatches, hardware performance counters, and matrix core utilization on AMD Instinct accelerators.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AMD ROCm profiling stack—comprising `roctracer`, `rocprofiler`, and the unified `rocprofiler-sdk`—provides deterministic performance counter collection and API dispatch tracing across AMD Instinct accelerators (CDNA2/CDNA3 architectures) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f]. It allows AI runtime maintainers to correlate high-level framework operations with low-level Matrix Core (MFMA) execution and High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) throughput [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].

# Architecture / Specification

The ROCm profiling architecture operates across multiple runtime layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f]:

- **Application and Framework Layer**: PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX emit user annotations via `ROCTX` markers, interacting with `rocBLAS`, `MIOpen`, and `RCCL` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].
- **Runtime Interception**: `roctracer` hooks HIP and HSA runtime calls, recording kernel launch timestamps (`hipLaunchKernel`) and activity duration [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].
- **Hardware Performance Counters**: `rocprofiler` queries hardware Performance Monitoring Units (PMUs) via the Kernel Fusion Driver (KFD) and `amdgpu` kernel module, measuring VALU/MFMA instruction counts (`SQ_INSTS_VALU_MFMA_F16`) and memory bus activity (`FETCH_SIZE`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].
- **Timeline Correlation**: Tools such as Omnitrace and Omniperf export timeline traces in Perfetto-compatible JSON formats and state graphs, complementing [PyTorch Profiler](../reference-architectures/pytorch-profiler.md) and [NVIDIA Nsight](../reference-architectures/nvidia-nsight.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].

# References

- AMD roctracer/rocprofiler Reference Architecture in [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].

mutations.rationale: Add TMLL reference architecture documenting automated machine learning trace analysis exposed to AI agents via Model Context Protocol.

proposed_concept.title: TMLL Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Trace analysis machine learning library bridging Eclipse Trace Compass time-series states to AI agent workflows via Model Context Protocol tools.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

TMLL (Trace-Server Machine Learning Library) is an analytical orchestration framework that applies automated machine learning pipelines (such as Isolation Forest, changepoint detection, and ARIMA forecasting) to execution traces produced by [Trace Compass](../reference-architectures/trace-compass.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b]. It exposes deterministic trace analytics as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools for AI agents to diagnose latency regressions and anomalies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].

# Architecture / Specification

TMLL acts as an intermediate bridge between deterministic trace servers and reasoning agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b]:

- **Trace Ingestion Layer**: Connects via REST using the Trace Server Protocol (TSP) to Trace Compass Server, reading state system time-series data without parsing raw trace binaries directly [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].
- **Statistical & ML Engine**: Utilizes scikit-learn, statsmodels, and ruptures to perform anomaly detection, change-point analysis (PELT/BOCPD), idle resource detection, and memory leak analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].
- **MCP Server Surface**: Exposes standardized tools (`ensure_server`, `detect_anomalies`, `detect_changepoints`, `detect_memory_leak`, `plot_xy_with_anomalies`) over standard I/O (stdio JSON-RPC) directly consumable by AI agent environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].

# References

- TMLL Reference Architecture in [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].

mutations.rationale: Add Goose reference architecture detailing the full agent runtime lifecycle, MCP/ACP protocols, security scanning, and multi-sink telemetry.

proposed_concept.title: Goose Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Open-source extensible AI agent runtime integrating multi-turn tool execution, permission management, Model Context Protocol, and multi-sink telemetry export.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Goose is an open-source, general-purpose desktop and terminal AI agent runtime written in Rust [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]. It coordinates the entire execution loop between client interfaces, LLM inference providers, extension capabilities via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and [Agent Client Protocol](../projects/agent-client-protocol.md), security validation layers, and distributed telemetry export sinks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

# Architecture / Specification

The Goose system architecture consists of four primary structural tiers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]:

- **Client Interfaces**: CLI binary (`goose`), Electron desktop application, or external IDE extensions communicating via REST, SSE, or stdio ACP [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Goose Server (`goosed`)**: Axum-based HTTP server managing session persistence in SQLite, context window compaction, permission gating, and scheduled execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Agent Core & Extension Engine**: Orchestrates multi-turn model interaction (`provider_chat`), security inspection (regex and ML scanners), and subagent delegation across local and remote MCP extensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Observability Layer**: Emits hierarchical spans (`agent_reply`, `provider_chat`, `tool_execution`) simultaneously to [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md) collectors, [Langfuse](../reference-architectures/langfuse.md) tracing servers, and [PostHog](../reference-architectures/posthog.md) product analytics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

# References

- Goose Reference Architecture in [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

mutations.rationale: Add Langfuse reference architecture documenting hierarchical span ingestion, generation metadata tracking, and evaluation batching for AI agents.

proposed_concept.title: Langfuse Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Dedicated open-source LLM observability backend providing hierarchical trace ingestion, generation tracking, and evaluation metrics for AI agent frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Langfuse is an open-source LLM observability and evaluation backend that records detailed hierarchical execution trees of AI agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44]. It captures span timing, prompt and generation input/output payloads, model parameters, and token cost attribution for complex multi-step agent executions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].

# Architecture / Specification

Integration between agent runtimes (such as [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md)) and Langfuse follows a structured observation model [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44]:

- **Subscriber Layer**: A `tracing_subscriber::Layer` intercepts internal runtime events, mapping span lifetimes to Langfuse observation IDs and flattens metadata (inputs, outputs, model configuration) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].
- **Batch Manager**: Asynchronously accumulates observation events and flushes payloads periodically (e.g., every 5 seconds) via authenticated HTTP POST requests to `/api/public/ingestion` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].
- **Data Model**: Organizes execution into Traces containing child Spans and Generations, tracking prompt token counts, latency breakdowns, and user session identifiers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].

# References

- Langfuse Reference Architecture in [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].

mutations.rationale: Add GPU driver tracing reference architecture covering cross-vendor tensor operation profiling across NVIDIA CUPTI, AMD ROCm, and Intel oneAPI.

proposed_concept.title: GPU Driver Tracing for AI Acceleration Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Cross-vendor GPU acceleration tracing architecture capturing tensor core utilization, driver submissions, and hardware metrics across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel platforms.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

GPU driver tracing for AI acceleration defines the architectural mechanisms used to monitor tensor operations, mixed-precision compute, high-bandwidth memory transfers, and multi-GPU collective communications across hardware vendors [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826]. It provides complete visibility from framework-level dispatch (such as PyTorch or TensorFlow) down to hardware tensor execution units [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].

# Architecture / Specification

The cross-vendor GPU tracing stack spans three key hardware ecosystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826]:

- **NVIDIA Ecosystem**: Uses CUPTI and Nsight tools alongside Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM) to capture Tensor Core active percentages (`TENSOR_ACTIVE`), SM occupancy, and NCCL multi-GPU collectives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].
- **AMD Ecosystem**: Uses `roctracer` and `rocprofiler` to trace HIP API launches, KFD driver scheduling, and Matrix Core instruction counts (`SQ_INSTS_VALU_MFMA_F16`) on CDNA architectures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].
- **Intel Ecosystem**: Uses oneAPI Level Zero tracing and Observation Architecture (OA) counters to measure Xe Matrix Extensions (XMX) engine utilization and command queue latencies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].
- **Framework Correlation**: Binds high-level operator markers (NVTX, ROCTX) to hardware performance counters via [PyTorch Profiler](../reference-architectures/pytorch-profiler.md) and [AMD rocprofiler](../reference-architectures/amd-rocprofiler.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].

# References

- GPU AI Tracing Reference Architecture in [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].

mutations.rationale: Update the issue analysis skill with authoritative architectural details from the Flue 2.0 implementation, reference corpus indexing, cross-repository dispatch security, and prompt injection handling.

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized agent skill and execution scaffold for evaluating GitHub issues against repository context, past analysis precedent, and security boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis Skill is a standardized agent capability and execution scaffold designed for automated, context-grounded issue triage and assessment across repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. Implemented using Flue 2.0 runtime primitives and the Pi model layer, it inspects inbound issue submissions, correlates them with historical hand-written reference analyses, and publishes findings into external records without requiring write permissions to the source code repository [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill architecture is structured around least-privilege automation, progressive context disclosure, and strict data-instruction separation [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

## Progressive Context Retrieval and Reference Corpus
Rather than incurring context overhead from global histories or maintaining specialized vector stores, the skill utilizes a file-based reference corpus [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]:
- **Frontmatter Indexing:** Past analyses are stored as structured markdown files with frontmatter containing metadata such as `issue-number`, `issue-type`, `severity`, `tags`, and `components` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Selective Loading:** The agent inspects the frontmatter headers across reference documents, selects the 3–5 most relevant historical precedents matching the target issue's components and tags, and loads only those full bodies into the execution context [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Synthetic Precedent Management:** Synthetic bootstrap files carry `example: true` flags and are excluded from being cited as real precedent [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

## Cross-Repository Trust Boundaries and Permissions
The analysis agent executes in an isolated tooling repository distinct from the target repository being analyzed [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]:
- **Dispatch Invocation:** Target repositories trigger analyses via `workflow_dispatch` using a fine-grained personal access token (`ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN`) with `Actions: write` scope only, avoiding `Contents: write` scopes that could introduce code execution vectors [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Zero-Write Target Repositories:** The agent operates completely read-only against the target repository; it does not post issue comments, push code, or mutate pull requests [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Separation of Egress:** Output reports are published to external destinations (e.g., Google Docs and Discord channels) via dedicated integration tools, keeping runtime secrets encapsulated from model prompts [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

## Adversarial Robustness and Injection Handling
Inbound issue titles, descriptions, and comments are treated strictly as untrusted data rather than operational instructions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]:
- **Data Framing:** Issue payloads are passed within nonce-delimited data envelopes [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Manipulation Telemetry:** When prompt injection or instruction hijacking is detected in issue text, the agent is instructed to flag `injectionSuspected: true`, document the attempt in `injectionNotes`, and continue evaluating the remaining technical claims [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Action Pinning and Faux Testing:** Actions in continuous integration workflows are pinned to full commit SHAs, and verification is performed against mock provider backends (`FLUE_FAUX=1`) without exposing production credentials [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].

# References
- Related guideline: [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../policies-guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)
- Skill catalog: [Public Agent Skills](../ecosystem/public-agent-skills.md)

mutations.rationale: Incorporate operational security patterns from the submission analyzer threat model and CI pipeline including cross-repo token bounding, SHA pinning, and prompt injection logging.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Security guidance detailing threat models, least-privilege token boundaries, action pinning, and prompt injection defense patterns for AI agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agentic AI Security Best Practices outlines actionable design patterns, boundary controls, and threat modeling frameworks for executing autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents in continuous integration and developer workflows [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. It focuses on isolating untrusted inputs, eliminating privilege escalation pathways, and securing runtime integrations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# Architecture / Specification
Securing agentic workflows requires layered defense mechanisms across pipeline triggers, execution sandboxes, and integration tools [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].

## Threat Model Fundamentals
Autonomous agent systems operating on public repositories face an open adversary profile where untrusted third parties can submit arbitrarily crafted text (e.g., issues, PR descriptions, comments) directly into agent context [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].
- **Untrusted Input Separation:** All external user text must be treated as untrusted data rather than system instructions, isolated inside explicit delimiters or nonces [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Prompt Injection Auditing:** Agents should record suspected prompt injection attempts using structured telemetry (e.g., `injectionSuspected: true` and descriptive notes) rather than quietly discarding or executing adversarial instructions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

## Cross-Repository Trust Boundaries
When agent execution is partitioned across separate tooling and target repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]:
- **Scope Minimization:** Trigger tokens between repositories (such as `ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN`) must use fine-grained permissions granting only `Actions: write` to invoke `workflow_dispatch`, avoiding `Contents: write` scopes that allow repository file modifications [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Input Validation:** Dispatch inputs (such as issue numbers and target repository identifiers) must be strictly validated against rigid regular expressions before being processed by scripts or commands [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Zero Target Repository Writes:** Agents should avoid holding write tokens to repositories under analysis, mitigating the blast radius of potential prompt injection exploits [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

## CI/CD Pipeline and Supply Chain Hardening
Agent execution environments must adhere to strict supply chain constraints [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926]:
- **Immutable Action Pinning:** All third-party GitHub Actions must be pinned to full commit SHAs rather than mutable semantic tags to prevent upstream supply-chain compromises [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].
- **Offline Faux Verification:** Core skill validation and CLI workflows should be verified offline using mock providers (`FLUE_FAUX=1`) to test agent logic without exposing live credentials in test environments [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].
- **Encapsulated Secrets:** Tool execution code must encapsulate API keys and tokens internally, preventing the model layer from viewing, printing, or summarizing sensitive environment variables [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# References
- Reference implementation: [Issue Analysis Skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md)
- Working group: [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- Pattern: [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Agent Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized agent skill and Flue execution harness evaluating GitHub issues against repository context with read-only sandbox boundaries and multi-vendor Copilot routing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis skill and automated agent harness evaluates incoming GitHub issues against repository documentation, architecture guidelines, and taxonomy standards to produce structured triage assessments [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]. Operating on the Flue runtime, the agent routes inference requests through GitHub Copilot's multi-model provider catalog and publishes reports out-of-band to Google Docs and Discord without maintaining write access to the source code repository [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

# Architecture / Specification
The issue analysis agent architecture integrates execution constraints, authentication flows, and containment boundaries:

- **Execution Runtime and Model Routing**: Implemented using Flue and `pi-ai`, the harness routes all model completions through the `github-copilot` provider [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]. It configures a primary model (`github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7`) and an automated workflow fallback (`github-copilot/gpt-5.4`) across different model families without requiring secondary vendor credentials [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]. `useModel()` scoping binds model selection to individual submission lifecycles without mid-run swapping [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].
- **Copilot Token Exchange**: Under CI workflows, `copilot-requests: write` permissions permit exchanging the workflow's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for short-lived session bearer tokens at `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`, avoiding direct inference PAT restrictions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].
- **Principle of Least Privilege**: Workflow permissions are constrained strictly to `contents: read` and `copilot-requests: write` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. Repository write permissions (`issues: write`) are explicitly denied, neutralizing prompt injection vectors that attempt to modify workflows or code through attacker-controlled issue text [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- **Out-of-Band Integration**: Issues are ingested via read-only GitHub API adapters with bot-filtering guards (`isBot`) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]. Analysis results are exported as Google Docs using single multipart Drive uploads and broadcast to Discord webhooks with mention sanitization (`allowed_mentions: { parse: [] }`) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].
- **Injection Detection**: Output schemas include `injectionSuspected` and `injectionNotes` telemetry fields to record adversarial prompt injection attempts as structured findings [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

# Lifecycle History
Developed under the AAIF tooling workstream as Flue 2.0, standardizing on built-in Copilot provider routing and decoupled cross-repository dispatch workflows [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing multi-layer telemetry standards, behavioral trace models, dynamic verification, and execution visibility for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates telemetry standards, behavioral trace models, and execution visibility frameworks across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]. The group develops specifications linking high-level agent reasoning, tool invocations, and action capsules down to system runtimes, network stacks, and hardware acceleration infrastructure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group directs multiple technical tracks and focus groups:

- **Five-Layer Observability Architecture**: Addresses full-stack tracing across five discrete layers, identifying that existing application-level frameworks such as [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md) primarily cover Layer 5 (application logic) while leaving gaps across kernel, accelerator, driver, and lower network tiers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Protocols and Primitives Focus Group**: Standardizes cross-layer data encryption, transport primitives, and wire representations for high-throughput, privacy-preserving agent telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **State, Context, and Reasoning Focus Group**: Defines semantic models for tracking reasoning loops, context compaction states, session-level replays, and semantic graph representations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Behavioral Trace Models & Agent Action Capsules**: Standardizes execution attribution and capsule verification models (including [Agent Trace](../reference-architectures/agent-trace.md) integrations) to capture end-to-end agent lineage and security operations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Security & Dynamic Verification**: Coordinates Merkle link graphs for tamper-evident event chains and dynamic rule-based verification across build and execution artifacts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Lifecycle History
During the 2026-08-19 meeting, the working group reviewed accepted observability taxonomy terms, established open participation across its focus groups, and initiated a gap analysis covering full-stack tracing beyond application-level OTel [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Architecture Principles
proposed_concept.description: Eight core design principles for composing patterns, capability roles, and control boundaries into workflow reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Workflow Architecture Principles guide contributors and reviewers in composing patterns, capability roles, and boundaries into agentic workflow reference architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181]. Established by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), they serve as shared, vendor-neutral design guidance rather than prescriptive runtime or topology constraints[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181].

# Architecture / Specification

The specification defines eight foundational design principles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181]:

1. **Design around practitioner jobs, not agent count**: Name and organize architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs (e.g., human-approved operation, bounded autonomous remediation) rather than arbitrary agent counts or topologies[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181]. See also [Job-Oriented Architecture Model](../decisions/job-oriented-architecture-model.md).
2. **Prefer the smallest safe amount of autonomy**: Maximize deterministic workflow logic, rules, and policy checks for admission and effect control; restrict agent model reasoning to open-ended interpretation or candidate generation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181].
3. **Make authority and external effects explicit**: Clearly define distinct roles for proposing results, validating acceptability, authorizing actions, executing effects, and holding run state[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181].
4. **Protect consequential effects structurally**: Ensure critical external mutations do not rely purely on agent instruction following. Enforce boundaries via human gates, policy engines, constrained executors, and idempotent reconciliation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181]. See [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
5. **Design for failure, recovery, and explicit outcomes**: Systematically handle invalid inputs, failed checks, restarts, duplicates, timeouts, budget exhaustion, and escalations, explicitly recording terminal states[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181].
6. **Compose reusable patterns; do not duplicate their guarantees**: Reference established patterns for recurring problems and address only composition-level risks and boundary interactions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181].
7. **Keep requirements portable and implementation-neutral**: Use logical capability roles (e.g., "durable state store", "constrained effect executor") rather than specific vendor runtimes or hosting providers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181].
8. **Validate guidance against real scenarios**: Ground reference architectures in worked scenarios and validation records to confirm job fit and uncover missing pattern invariants[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026**: Merged into `wg-workflows-and-process-integration` repository under `workstreams/reference-architectures/principles.md`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181].

# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body established to standardize multi-layer telemetry, behavioral trace specifications, execution capture hooks, and post-hoc verification mechanisms across agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on vendor-neutral observability interfaces bridging model invocations, tool interactions, userspace runtime environments, and kernel-level execution traces. Core areas of work include:
- Correlating high-level agent sessions with distributed telemetry formats such as [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md) and [Common Trace Format](../reference-architectures/common-trace-format.md).
- Capturing fine-grained code attribution and execution histories via [Agent Trace](../reference-architectures/agent-trace.md).
- Interoperating with kernel and hardware tracing facilities across CPU and GPU hardware.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-15**: The Observability & Traceability WG formally approved its working group charter[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].
- **2026-04-21**: WG charter submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for formal review and adoption[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].

The `aaif-taxonomy-contributions` skill provides structured instructions and validation logic for AI agents preparing contributions to the AAIF Taxonomy and Landscape workstream [^evt-public-agents-pr-3]. It automates contribution triage, pre-submission checks, and adherence to data schemas [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill addresses common contributor routing errors and enforces quality bars [^evt-public-agents-pr-3]:

- **Pre-Draft Checks**: Verifies that proposed terms or landscape tools are not already registered or under active review in open pull requests [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Schema & Quality Verification**: Strips marketing language and superlatives from landscape candidate descriptions while conforming entries to the schema [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Dynamic Specification Retrieval**: Directs agents to fetch live repository documentation before drafting, ensuring resilience against schema changes [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines vendor-neutral specifications, data formats, and behavioral trace models for monitoring, debugging, and auditing AI agent execution across local and distributed environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its deliverables across multiple telemetry and compliance layers:
- **Behavioral Trace Models**: Structuring agent execution, tool invocations, reasoning loops, and multi-agent interaction timelines.
- **Tamper-Evident Evidence (Use Case E4)**: Standardizing verifiable audit trails for compliance and dispute resolution using Merkle-chained signed records, RFC 3161 timestamps, WORM storage, and evidence-grade scoring ladders [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **External & Internal Liaisons**: Maintaining formal liaison trackers and intake coordination across OpenTelemetry GenAI, W3C Trace Context, OWASP AOS, and internal AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

# Overview
The Single-Agent Workflow Reference Architecture (SAW-RA) Documentation Blueprint establishes the standardized structural framework for documenting single-agent workflow reference architectures within the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

# Architecture / Specification
The blueprint divides reference architecture documentation into six core sections [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b]:
1. **Foundations**: Scope, boundaries, core terminology, design principles, and architectural invariants [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].
2. **Architecture Model**: Reference models, primitive catalogs, runtime execution components, and composition rules [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].
3. **Patterns and Selection**: Pattern taxonomy, selection heuristics, and a reusable pattern catalog [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].
4. **Enterprise Readiness**: Enterprise control overlays, security postures, and readiness criteria [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].
5. **Workflow Lifecycle**: End-to-end guidance spanning workflow design, assessment, testing, operations, and conformance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].
6. **Evolution and Supporting Material**: Roadmap, migration strategies, and technical appendices [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].

proposed_concept.title: Durable Wait
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern converting in-memory execution waits into durable state records to survive process termination, deploys, and restarts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Durable Wait pattern decouples workflow run persistence from transient host process lifecycles, enabling workflows to pause for hours or days awaiting external events, timer expirations, or human intervention [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7]. By transforming a physical blocking thread or process wait into a logically recorded parked state, the workflow run survives process restarts, host crashes, and scheduled deploys without consuming active runtime memory [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].

This pattern is foundational for architectures requiring asynchronous external input, such as the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].

# Architecture / Specification

### Parking and Resume Mechanism

When a workflow enters a wait condition:
1. **State Recording**: The execution engine captures current execution position, intermediate inputs/context, and correlation identity into persistent storage [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].
2. **Parked State**: The process releases in-memory execution; the persisted record represents the entire run [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].
3. **Event Correlation & Resume**: When an external event or timeout occurs, the system matches the event to the run identity, loads the context record, and resumes execution at the designated activity [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-33].

### Core Invariants

- **Process Survivability**: Parked runs must survive host terminations, restarts, and redeployments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].
- **Context and Position Fidelity**: Continuation restores exact position and prior knowledge without recomputing state from scratch [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].
- **Idempotent Resume**: Duplicate wake-up events trigger execution resumption at most once [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].
- **Discoverability**: Suspended runs remain queryable and discoverable across restarts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining intake, technical evaluation, engagement bars, voting gates, and onboarding workflows for AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Project Proposal Process is the operational procedure executing the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../governance/project-lifecycle-policy.md) under the authority of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Designed to favor asynchronous and offline workflows across a distributed technical committee, the procedure enforces engagement standards, automated compliance evaluations, and formal committee voting gates for new and migrating projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification

### Sequential Process Steps

1. **Initial Intake**: The CTO and an automated Intake Agent screen submissions for baseline completeness, license compliance, and scope alignment [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
2. **TC Q&A Window**: A public review window where Technical Committee members engage with proposals. The framework requires meeting a minimum breadth-of-engagement bar across TC members, with an on-demand TC supporter mechanism if engagement stalls [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Submissions may optionally include an on-demand live presentation.
3. **Parallel Contributor Paperwork**: Submitter completes necessary licensing and governance prerequisites concurrently with review [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
4. **TC Vote**: Technical Committee conducts a binding admission and initial stage vote via LFX Vote [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
5. **Governing Board Approval**: The Governing Board reviews resource impact and confirms admission [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
6. **LF Legal Formation**: Finalization of contribution agreements, technical charter, and trademark transfers [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
7. **Technical Onboarding**: Migration of repository infrastructure, permissions, and CI/CD pipelines under Linux Foundation IT oversight [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

mutations.rationale: Add the comprehensive comparison of agentic workflow orchestration patterns from industry documentation.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Workflow Patterns Comparison
proposed_concept.description: Comparative taxonomy and evaluation matrix of industry agentic AI workflow orchestration patterns from major cloud providers and research labs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Workflow Orchestration Patterns Comparison is a reference document cataloging, categorizing, and comparing architectural workflow patterns across major industry frameworks, including AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Anthropic [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab]. The document maps pattern complexity, agency levels, concrete use cases, and selection criteria to guide practitioners in choosing between deterministic orchestration, single-agent loops, and complex multi-agent architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab].

# Architecture / Specification

### Pattern Spectrum

- **Minimal / Low Agency**: Includes *LLM-Augmented Workflows*, *Routing / Triage*, and *Prompt Chaining*, prioritizing deterministic control, low cost, and step-level validation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-33].
- **Moderate Agency**: Encompasses *Single-Agent (ReAct)*, *Sequential Multi-Agent*, *Parallel Multi-Agent*, *Iterative Loop*, and *Review & Critique (Maker-Checker)* patterns balancing tool use with structured execution bounds [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab].
- **High / Complex Agency**: Covers *Coordinator (Orchestrator-Workers)*, *Hierarchical Task Decomposition*, *Swarm (Roundtable)*, and *Hybrid (Plan & Solve)* patterns designed for dynamic task decomposition and autonomous problem-solving [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab].
- **Control Boundaries**: Integrates *Human-in-the-Loop* approval points and *Custom Logic* for governance, compliance, and deterministic fail-safes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab].

mutations.rationale: Introduces the Deterministic Acceptance Gate pattern merged into the workflows reference architecture workstream.

proposed_concept.title: Deterministic Acceptance Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern evaluating candidate results against explicit, repeatable checks and scope rules rather than model self-assessment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Deterministic Acceptance Gate pattern provides an objective, repeatable verification mechanism that evaluates candidate results produced by an agent against explicit acceptance criteria and scope boundaries rather than relying on model self-assessment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]. It ensures that candidate changes are backed by verifiable evidence before being permitted to advance within an agentic workflow [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern evaluates an exact candidate artifact against declared policy rules and deterministic checks such as unit test suites, schema validation, and linting rules [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

Key invariants include [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]:
- Acceptance criteria are declared before candidate evaluation occurs.
- The gate operates independently of the model or agent that produced the candidate result.
- Acceptance evidence is strictly bound to the exact candidate artifact version or digest.
- Passing verification checks is insufficient if task scope or authorization policies are violated.
- A failed, unavailable, or ambiguous check result fails closed and never counts as acceptance.

# References
- [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../reference-architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](bounded-convergence-loop.md)
- [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md)

mutations.rationale: Introduces the Bounded Convergence Loop pattern merged into the workflows reference architecture workstream.

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Convergence Loop
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern safely iterating agent execution within strict time, cost, and iteration limits until a deterministic gate passes or defined termination is reached.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Convergence Loop pattern governs iterative agent-assisted problem solving by constraining retries within explicit scope, time, cost, and iteration limits until an independent deterministic gate evaluates the candidate result as acceptable [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]. This prevents runaway execution, budget exhaustion, or self-certified success during autonomous tasks [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

# Architecture / Specification
The loop admits a bounded task with predetermined scope and allowed tools, executes an agent attempt, and routes the output to a deterministic gate [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

Key invariants include [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]:
- Explicit task scope, tool capabilities, and acceptance criteria are fixed before iteration begins.
- The agent is prohibited from self-certifying convergence.
- Every retry consumes from a declared budget including iteration limits and time or cost caps.
- All attempts, gate outcomes, and terminal transitions (success, escalation, abstention, or failure) are durably recorded in workflow state.
- Workflow restarts resume from recorded state without resetting attempt budgets.

# References
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Durable Wait](durable-wait.md)
- [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../reference-architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)

mutations.rationale: Introduces the Proposal/Execution Split pattern separating agent intent generation from authorization and execution.

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern separating probabilistic agent intent generation, deterministic authorization, and workflow-controlled execution into distinct boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal/Execution Split pattern establishes strict separation of concerns across the protected-effect boundary by isolating probabilistic intent generation from authorization and execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]. Under this pattern, an AI agent only produces immutable proposal data, while an independent authorization gate authorizes the action and a workflow-controlled executor applies the protected effect [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern divides workflow progression into three distinct roles [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]:
1. **Proposer (Agent)**: Generates a proposed modification or payload without direct execution privileges.
2. **Authorization Authority**: Evaluates and signs off on the exact candidate proposal against security policy or human review.
3. **Executor (System)**: A non-agent, workflow-controlled runtime component that executes the authorized proposal against external systems.

Key invariants mandate that authorization attaches to the exact proposed payload, that authorization gates fail closed upon timeout or error, and that all proposals, decisions, and executed effects are durably recorded in the system of record [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

# References
- [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md)
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](bounded-convergence-loop.md)

mutations.rationale: Adds the Bounded Autonomous Remediation reference architecture introduced in PR #26.

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Job-oriented reference architecture orchestrating autonomous agent iteration over fenced problems under deterministic gates, bounded budgets, and controlled execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a job-oriented reference architecture designed for autonomous problem resolution on fenced, pre-qualified tasks without requiring human pre-approval for every iteration [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26]. The workflow bounds agent autonomy using strict tool and data limits, evaluates progress via an independent deterministic gate, and allows external effects only for verified candidate solutions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture composes three core patterns to enforce safety and bounded execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26]:
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Controls repetitive diagnosis and patching attempts within fixed time, cost, and iteration limits.
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Runs automated tests, linters, or schema verifications to evaluate candidate solutions objectively without relying on model self-assessment.
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Ensures the agent only generates proposals, leaving final application of changes to workflow-controlled executors.

Human operators are engaged via escalation paths only when the loop fails to converge, budgets expire, or scope violations occur [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

# References
- [Job-Oriented Architecture Model](../decisions/job-oriented-architecture-model.md)
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md)
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance framework detailing proposal requirements, stage criteria (Sandbox, Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and transition processes for AAIF technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Project Lifecycle Policy defines the official progression stages, entry criteria, and review processes for technical projects governed under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]. It establishes transparent governance pathways for onboarding emerging projects into Sandbox, advancing mature projects to Growth and Impact stages, and archiving inactive efforts under Emeritus status [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The project lifecycle defines four distinct operational stages [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]:
- **Sandbox**: Entry stage for early-stage initiatives, experimental tools, and novel specifications seeking neutral collaboration and foundation incubation.
- **Growth**: Stage for active projects demonstrating multi-organization adoption, sustained contributor diversity, structured release management, and formal security policies.
- **Impact**: Highest maturity tier for mission-critical, widely deployed standards and runtimes demonstrating significant ecosystem governance and long-term sustainability.
- **Emeritus**: Stage for retired or deprecated projects transitioning out of active development.

Transitions between stages require formal Technical Committee review and approval according to established voting gates [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

# References
- [Technical Committee](technical-committee.md)
- [Project Proposal Process](project-proposal-process.md)

mutations.rationale: Establishes the core workflow vocabulary and taxonomy definitions defined by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group.

proposed_concept.title: Core Workflow Terms
proposed_concept.description: Foundational vocabulary for agentic AI workflows defining activities, executions, state, context, control flow, and coordination models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Core Workflow Terms provide a standardized, shared vocabulary for agentic AI workflow architectures, reference implementations, and interoperability models within the AAIF Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. The taxonomy defines fundamental concepts including activities, executions, state, and coordination patterns to ensure uniform semantics across workflow specifications.

Following working group consensus, the taxonomy formally replaces the terms "Workflow Step" and "Workflow Task" with "Activity", positioning Activity as the standalone foundational primitive to avoid circular definitions with workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

# Architecture / Specification
The vocabulary organizes core workflow semantics into foundational concepts, execution properties, and coordination mechanisms [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]:

- **Activity**: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].
- **Workflow**: The primary unit of structured, multi-activity work with a defined goal and outcome, composed of one or more activities, their relationships, and execution logic [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow Execution**: A runtime instance of a workflow definition, where multiple concurrent executions maintain independent execution state and lifecycles [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow State**: Information representing the current condition of a workflow execution at a specific point in time, including progress and resumption data [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow Context**: Shared runtime information across activities and workflow boundaries, containing inputs, metadata, shared data, execution history, configuration, and external resource references [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Control Flow**: Logic governing order, conditions, branching, iteration, parallelism, and synchronization of activity executions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Trigger**: An event, signal, condition, schedule, or request initiating or advancing a workflow execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Durability & Determinism**: Durability guarantees the preservation of execution state across interruptions or failures, while determinism ensures consistent execution behavior given identical inputs, state, and execution history [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Coordination & Actors**: Defines structural patterns including orchestration, choreography, composition, roles, agent cards, human-in-the-loop gates, discovery, handoffs, plans, and dry runs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08 (In Review)**: Initial core vocabulary formulated and updated in `terms.md` to establish Activity as the baseline primitive replacing workflow steps [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared workflow execution models, activity schemas, persistence primitives, and coordination patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group develops vendor-neutral execution models, taxonomy standards, activity schemas, persistence primitives, and multi-agent coordination frameworks for agentic systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. The working group establishes reference architectures and patterns that enable reliable, durable, and deterministic execution of complex AI agent workflows across enterprise environments.

The group works in close collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and relates directly to workflow principles codified in [Workflow Architecture Principles](../policies-guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md) and [Single-Agent Workflow Blueprint](../policies-guidelines/single-agent-workflow-blueprint.md).

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on core areas of agentic workflow infrastructure:

- **Core Taxonomy**: Establishing standardized terminology in [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md), formally defining activities as independent bounded primitives, workflow executions, durable state, and shared context [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].
- **Coordination Models**: Specifying orchestration, choreography, dynamic plan generation, and handoff mechanisms across multi-agent ensembles [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Control and Reliability**: Formalizing trigger mechanisms, lifecycle transitions, durable execution guarantees, and deterministic acceptance gates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Human & Actor Integration**: Defining standardized interfaces for human-in-the-loop approvals, agent cards, and role delegations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: Adopted standardized `Activity` terminology in place of workflow steps and published the initial review draft of core workflow taxonomy terms [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

mutations.rationale: Updates the Agentic Commerce Working Group document with post-purchase cross-boundary evidence, audit requirements, and machine-readable verdict envelope proposals.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging open specifications, capability maps, and protocol interfaces for agent-mediated purchasing and post-purchase auditability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group catalogs open specifications, capability maps, and protocol interfaces for agent-mediated commerce, purchasing flows, payment interactions, and post-purchase settlement [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]. The group focuses on interoperability across buyer agents, merchant platforms, payment gateways, and risk evaluation systems.

The working group coordinates closely with sibling working groups, relying on primitives from the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for delegated authority and agent identity, and the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) for telemetry and audit log capture [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's Capability Map and Gap Analysis deliverable covers end-to-end transaction phases, including post-purchase cross-boundary evidence and audit capabilities [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]:

- **Evidence Binding**: Establishing verifiable receipts and audit records binding actions to delegations, transactions, and identities for dispute resolution [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Signal Provenance**: Tracking whether capability and risk signals originate from the agent, platform, merchant, or payment provider [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Authorization Strength for State Changes**: Governing the evidentiary requirements for order cancellations, returns, refunds, and dispute remedies [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Machine-Readable Verdict Envelope**: Standardizing an 8-field verification contract containing verdict classification (`supported`, `contradicted`, `unresolvable`), verifier identity, signature, evidence references, canonical RFC 8785 hashes, verification basis, witness scope, and freshness timestamp [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: Proposed post-purchase cross-boundary evidence, audit capability rows, and machine-readable verdict envelope contract for the Capability Map and Gap Analysis deliverable [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing evaluation standards, benchmark frameworks, recovery patterns, and quality metrics for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group develops vendor-neutral evaluation standards, failure classification taxonomies, benchmark frameworks, recovery patterns, and quality metrics for autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]. The group aims to systematically reduce non-deterministic errors, hallucination risks, and execution drift in agentic workflows.

The working group is chaired by Jordan Auge (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid) and contributes directly to the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's active roadmap focuses on two core deliverables [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]:

- **Deliverable 1 (D1 - Terminology & Taxonomy)**: Defining structured error classification, hallucination taxonomies, and recovery terminology batches for shared cross-WG alignment [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].
- **Deliverable 2 (D2 - Gap Analysis & Practitioner Survey)**: Gathering empirical operational pain points, error recovery challenges, and prioritization feedback from industry practitioners with firsthand agentic deployment experience [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: Consolidated review loops, advanced D1 terminology review in PR #8, and opened the D2 practitioner survey specification in PR #9 for Technical Committee reach-out and broader rollout [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Community Pulse Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized skill for drafting community organizer update Slack posts from channel activity, chapter logs, and calendar events.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-community-pulse` skill aggregates organizer updates across Slack channels, local chapter records, intake spreadsheets, and calendar platforms to draft periodic AAIF Community Organizer Updates without directly publishing them [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill gathers context across several operational sources [^evt-community-events-pr-37]:
- **Slack Reads**: Uses the `aaif_events.slack` client with required scope checks to fetch read-only message history from `#local-champs`.
- **Secure Local Cache**: Stores fetched Slack history in an isolated `0600` local `.pulse-cache/` directory created via atomic file descriptor operations (`tempfile.mkstemp` and `os.replace`), which must be cleared after drafting.
- **External Sources**: Scans Google Workspace chapter tracking drives, intake sheets via `gws`, and community Luma calendars.
- **Repository Changes**: Inspects organizer-facing repository diffs using `git log`.
- **Human Gate**: Only outputs draft post text for a human organizer to review and send [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

# Lifecycle History
- Introduced and merged in `aaif/community-events#37` with hardened Slack API pagination, path validation, and permission checks [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

# References
- [Community Events Repository](https://github.com/aaif/community-events/pull/37)

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating a shared agentic AI SKOS-Lite taxonomy and maintaining the interactive ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream curates a standardized SKOS-Lite taxonomy for agentic AI concepts and maintains the ecosystem landscape cataloging open runtimes, frameworks, and protocols across AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream coordinates terminology intake, definition alignment, and landscape categorization across domain working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]:
- **Unified Terminology Review**: Reviews candidate terms from working groups including [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Governance, Risk and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md).
- **Definition Review Workflow**: Drafts structured definitions in pull requests, defining explicit conceptual relationships (e.g., `Skill` vs. `Tool`, `Kill switch` vs. `Reversibility`, `Harness` vs. `Meta-harness`, and `Delegation` vs. `Handoff`).
- **Landscape Governance**: Categorizes frameworks and tools within the [Agentic AI Landscape](../ecosystem/agentic-ai-landscape.md), managing proposals such as Attestation & Verifiable Evidence categories.

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Conducted three terminology syncs reviewing 53 candidate terms (37 kept, 15 culled, 1 held for debate), merged the `Harness` definition (PR #37), and moved 19 accepted terms into pull request reviews [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, capability maps, and protocol evaluations for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI commerce transactions, encompassing pre-purchase discovery, execution, and post-purchase lifecycle management [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on core deliverables across commerce interfaces [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]:

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing multi-layer telemetry standards, behavioral trace models, tamper-evident evidence, and execution capture.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group develops open telemetry standards, execution schemas, and behavioral tracing models for AI agent runtimes across userspace, framework, and kernel layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].

# Architecture / Specification
The group develops standardized observability specifications and execution models [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A multi-task roadmap establishing reproducible telemetry baselines across independent agent runtimes (such as [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md) and companion SDKs) to differentiate instrumentation bugs from missing semantic standards.
- **Session and Turn Correlation**: Telemetry specifications connecting multi-turn and paused/resumed conversations across distinct distributed traces without requiring long-lived continuous root spans.
- **Evidence and Audit Integration**: Telemetry structures providing verifiable evidence records in coordination with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).
- **Reference Architecture Instrumentation**: Alignment with distributed tracing ecosystems like [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md), [Agent Trace](../reference-architectures/agent-trace.md), and system tracing tools [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Initiated the nine-task Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan, including baseline captures across runtimes (Issue #40) and cross-trace turn continuity validation (Issue #43) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].

# References

The `aaif-sync-badges` skill automates the creation and synchronization of official AAIF chapter organizer badges across local community chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-38]. proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow architecture pattern requiring an authorized, uniquely identified human to explicitly approve agent proposals before external execution or publication.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Human Approval Gate pattern introduces a deterministic checkpoint where probabilistic agent actions are paused pending explicit verification and sign-off by an authorized human operator [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]. This decouples candidate artifact generation from live modification of external state.

# Architecture / Specification

- **Proposal and Publication Boundaries**: Agents generate candidate content or actions without direct publishing privileges [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Validated Use Cases**: Evaluated across knowledge-base updates, FAQ modifications, product release notes, and catalog listing descriptions to ensure strict boundary separation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **State Retention**: Integrates with [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) and [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) to suspend execution safely while awaiting human review.

# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides baseline defensive requirements and implementation rules for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]. It addresses prompt injection mitigations, least-privilege token separation, execution fences, and kill-switch architectures.

# Architecture / Specification

- **Core Controls**: Defines perimeter security, sandbox containment, and deterministic policy enforcement points [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Actionable Static Analysis Rules**: Translates narrative guidelines into executable static-analysis verification rules across major AI SDK implementations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Domain Boundaries**: Excludes identity issuance and verifiable delegation specifications, which are governed directly by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing multi-layer telemetry standards, behavioral trace models, tamper-evident action capsules, and system-level observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines interoperable standards, semantic conventions, and reference architectures for tracing agent execution, tool invocations, and system-level interactions across distributed multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Architecture / Specification

- **Behavior Trace Model**: Standardizes run-level and step-level agent execution spans, provider API mappings, streaming, and tool invocation tracing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].
- **Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) Lifecycle**: Validates telemetry for discovery, provenance, governance, trust evaluation, and admission decisions correlated with skill runtime execution in [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md) via OTLP [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].
- **Lower-Layer Observability**: Extends trace correlation below application L7 down to kernel, syscall, and network protocol layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Agent Action Capsules**: Explores cryptographically verifiable, tamper-evident action ledger primitives bridging regulatory compliance with agent execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
