proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Guidelines and Design System
proposed_concept.description: Visual design, typography, surface, and asset usage standards defining the neutral, flat design system and official brand representations for the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Design System defines the core visual language, color tokens, typography, surface rules, and asset usage standards across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. It establishes a neutral, authoritative, and flat aesthetic designed for clarity in technical reports, governance documentation, and community communications [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Design Principles

- **Primary Accent is Black**: Primary actions use black (`--accent: var(--ink)`) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve as secondary accents within specific surfaces rather than representing the global brand color [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Typography**: The design system uses Instrument Sans (OFL) as its sole typeface across weights 400, 500, 600, and 700 for both display and interface elements [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Monospace typography is restricted strictly to metadata, technical tokens, and eyebrows [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Headings use weight 500 with letter-spacing tracking of `-0.02em` and tight line-heights (1.05–1.15), with weight 600 reserved exclusively for minor headings (h5/h6) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Flat Aesthetic**: The design avoids drop shadows entirely, deriving depth from 1px hairlines, surface tinting (`--paper` to `--paper-2` and `--paper-3`), and inset strokes [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Cards, tables, stats, and chips maintain square corners (`border-radius: 0`), reserving rounded pill geometry (`--radius-pill`) solely for actionable buttons and badge counters [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Two Surfaces (No Dark Mode)**: The system defines two first-class surfaces: white editorial and black plate [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. There is no automatic dark mode or `prefers-color-scheme` flipping; surfaces are intentionally selected per component [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

## Brand Asset and Logo Rules

- **Canonical Mark Assets**: Official vector brand assets are maintained in `assets/`:
  - `aaif-mark.svg`: Full horizontal lockup (mark + wordmark) in black [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
  - `aaif-mark-square.svg`: Mark alone in black for headers, favicons, and avatars [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
  - `aaif-logo-white.svg`: Full lockup in white for black plate surfaces [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- **Asset Integrity**: The AAIF mark must never be redrawn, traced from screenshots, or approximated [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] [^evt-community-events-pr-41]. Canonical vector files must be used directly, altering only the fill color when necessary [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Agent Motif Usage**: The agent robot motif derived from the mark's geometry is reserved for empty states, loading indicators, dividers, and community event graphics; it is strictly prohibited in governance, board, or press materials [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group bridging global AI policy instruments with technical specifications through landscape and gap analysis.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) serves as the bridge between international AI legislative and regulatory developments and AAIF technical architectures [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]. The group provides landscape mapping, gap analysis, and policy extraction frameworks to help practitioners align autonomous agent systems with emerging compliance mandates [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Leadership and Governance

- **Chairs**: Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
- **Parent Body**: Reports to the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).

## Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group executes against a structured three-phase roadmap [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]:

1. **Phase 1: Landscape Analysis**: Identification and synthesis of global policy instruments, standards, and regulatory frameworks affecting agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
2. **Phase 2: Thematic Mapping and Gap Analysis**: Mapping policy instruments against core foundational themes using standardized AI information extraction prompts to highlight interoperability and governance gaps [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
3. **Phase 3: Final Recommendations and Harmonized Guidance**: Publishing concrete compliance crosswalks and technical architectural guidance for AAIF member organizations [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Standard operating procedure and application requirements for submitting open source projects for hosting under the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process defines the formal intake, evaluation, and approval lifecycle for open source software seeking official hosting under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]. Open source projects apply for placement within the AAIF maturity levels—Sandbox, Growth, or Impact—via structured proposals reviewed by the Technical Committee and Governing Board [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake and Submission

Proposals are submitted via the `aaif/project-proposals` intake repository using standardized templates that capture [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]:
- Project name, origin, scope, and technical description [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
- Alignment with the AAIF mission and ecosystem architecture [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
- Relationship and interoperability with existing AAIF projects and working groups [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
- Project maturity stage request (Sandbox, Growth, or Impact) [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].

## Approval Gates and Legal Execution

Admission into the foundation requires strict dual-body approval and legal execution sequence [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]:

1. **Technical Committee (TC) Evaluation**: The [Technical Committee](technical-committee.md) assesses architectural fit, technical maturity, community engagement, and ecosystem overlap [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
2. **Contribution Agreement**: A formal Contribution Agreement is generated and must be signed by the project maintainers/owners before the Governing Board can complete its vote [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
3. **Governing Board (GB) Vote**: The Governing Board votes on the intake following successful TC recommendation and agreement signing [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].
4. **Countersignature**: The Linux Foundation countersigns the Contribution Agreement only after a successful GB vote [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].

> Projects are legally prohibited from representing themselves as official AAIF projects or 'donated' to AAIF until both TC and GB votes have passed and the Contribution Agreement has been fully executed [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and architectural guidance for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Its focus is enabling agents to prove who they are, identify the principals they act for, verify human approvals, and operate securely across institutional boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operations

The working group operates under individual neutrality guidelines where participants contribute as individuals rather than employer representatives [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]:

- **Chair:** Grant Miller (IBM) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Co-Chair:** Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Meeting Schedule:** Alternating Thursdays between 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM US Pacific Time [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

## Workstreams and Breakouts

Working group initiatives are organized into three primary breakout streams [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:

1. **Use Cases:** Grounds requirements in enterprise and consumer agent workflows (Coordinated by Wei Chen) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
2. **Reference Architecture:** Identifies trust relationships, identity carriers, actor chains, and boundary interoperability gaps (Coordinated by Brian Malone) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
3. **Taxonomy Coordination:** Aligns identity and trust terminology with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) (Liaisons: Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

## Referenced Frameworks and Inputs

The working group analyzes emerging agent identity implementations and specifications, including:

- **Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD):** Resource and capability federation across distributed agent systems [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **SPIFFE/SPIRE Workload Attestation:** Cryptographic workload verification applied to dynamic agent processes [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Uber Agent Identity Architecture:** Workload registration, actor chains, per-hop token exchange, and policy enforcement [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **NVIDIA Secure Agent Workspace Reference Design:** Layered execution controls, identity scoping, and runtime security [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization Draft:** Protocol specifications for agent authorization tokens and delegation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

proposed_concept.title: Core Workflow Terms
proposed_concept.description: Foundational vocabulary for agentic AI workflows defining activities, executions, state, context, control flow, and determinism layers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Core Workflow Terms establish the foundational lexicon for agentic AI orchestration, separating high-level coordination and execution lifecycles from probabilistic and deterministic implementation steps [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. The terminology clarifies how execution state, branching logic, and task delegability are represented across hybrid human, agent, and deterministic compute environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

# Architecture / Specification

## Layered Determinism

Determinism is treated as a property of a specific execution layer rather than a monolithic all-or-nothing workflow state [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]:

- **Control Flow Determinism:** The branching and sequencing logic behaves deterministically based on input parameters and condition evaluations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Activity Determinism:** Individual activities may be probabilistic (e.g., LLM generation) or deterministic (e.g., standard code execution, schema validation) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Workflow Determinism:** A workflow can maintain deterministic control flow while hosting non-deterministic activities within bound execution steps [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

## Clarified Core Concepts

- **Control Flow:** The logic that governs sequencing, conditions, loops, and parallel executions. Control flow remains agnostic to whether decisions are fixed at compile time or evaluated dynamically by an orchestrating agent [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Workflow Execution Identity:** The persistent identity of a workflow execution survives runtime replanning, recovery steps, and retries; modifications to an execution plan constitute lifecycle state transitions rather than new execution entities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Handoff:** The transfer of task responsibility and execution context across agents, systems, or human operators, coordinating closely with observability trace boundaries defined in [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Observability
proposed_concept.description: Observability specification and telemetry propagation pattern capturing causal trace contexts across agent runtimes and locally spawned CLI tool processes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary architecture defines the telemetry model, context propagation mechanisms, and causal span relationships when an AI agent directly invokes a local CLI tool subprocess [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]. This architecture addresses the operational and semantic boundary where an agent runtime makes a tool decision and spawns an independent operating-system process without an intermediary service protocol [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Boundary Model

The execution boundary consists of two interacting surfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:

1. **Semantic Agent-to-Tool Surface:** Captures agent turn context, tool name, call identifier, and argument preparation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
2. **Operating System Process Surface:** Captures command resolution, child environment construction, process creation, execution lifespan, and process exit codes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

```text
Agent Turn / Invocation
  └── Tool Execution Span (execute_tool)          [Agent → Tool Semantic Boundary]
      └── [Optional CLI Caller Span]
          └── Local CLI Execution Span            [Agent Runtime → Local Process Boundary]
              └── CLI Sub-operations & Downstream Calls
```

## Telemetry and Context Propagation

Because finite local CLI subprocesses lack HTTP/RPC carrier headers, propagation occurs at process creation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:

- **Environment-Variable Carriers:** Active W3C trace context and invocation baggage must be injected into the child process environment before spawn [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Pre-execution Reservation:** The agent runtime generates tool execution span identifiers prior to process launch so that independently instrumented child processes can reference the tool span as their causal parent [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Authoritative Transcript Reconciliation:** Runtimes that discover tool execution details asynchronously via transcripts reconcile post-execution observations with the pre-reserved span tree [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

## Observability Matrix Fields

| Observable Dimension | Standard Coverage | Current Gaps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Identity** | OpenTelemetry GenAI `gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, and CLI process attributes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Missing cross-runtime bindings between tool call, executable artifact digest, and delegating principal [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |
| **Context** | W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry normalized environment carrier spec [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Runtimes filter child environments; lack of unified budget/deadline CLI carriers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |
| **Lifecycle** | GenAI tool execution duration, CLI start/exit timestamps, exit codes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Inconsistent representation of spawn failures, approval wait times, and background task cancellation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |
| **Outcome** | Exit codes (`process.exit.code`), error classification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Unstructured stdout/stderr side-effects and resource mutations are not systematically described [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing multi-layer telemetry standards, behavioral trace models, and agent identity context propagation specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, causal lineage models, and distributed context propagation standards for agentic AI systems. It develops architectural patterns and telemetry conventions that connect low-level runtime execution with high-level agent reasoning, delegation, and multi-agent workflows.

# Workstreams and Initiatives
The working group maintains several active specification and standardization initiatives:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A multi-phase execution plan defining structural execution patterns, conversation entry points, and lifecycle spans, designed to contribute upstream telemetry standards to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- **Agent Identity Telemetry and Context Propagation**: Scoping standardized OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and W3C Baggage propagation rules to preserve agent identity, roles, delegation depth, and invocation IDs across asynchronous task queues, sandboxes, and distributed agent hops[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]. This effort cross-collaborates with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **Multi-Layer Telemetry Correlation**: Standardizing trace context propagation spanning GPU hardware metrics, kernel hooks, agent tool CLI boundaries, and LLM orchestration frameworks.

# Governance and Cross-Group Collaboration
The working group coordinates with upstream standards organizations including the OpenTelemetry project and W3C distributed tracing groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]. Telemetry boundary policies and sanitization guidelines are co-developed with security workstreams to ensure sensitive credentials and execution payloads are redacted from distributed traces while maintaining causal auditability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: The technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for technical oversight, project lifecycle transitions, and working group coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation, tasked with overseeing technical standards, best practices, project lifecycles, and technical vision across foundation initiatives [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# Architecture / Specification

## Committee Membership and Leadership

The founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board with an active term of March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:

- **David Soria Parra** (Chair) — Anthropic
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (Co-Chair) — Microsoft
- **Alan Blount** — Google
- **Bradley Axen** — Block
- **James Ward** — Amazon Web Services
- **Nick Cooper** — OpenAI
- **Sambhav Kothari** — Bloomberg
- **Steve Faulkner** — Cloudflare

## Hosted Projects

The TC oversees foundation projects spanning all lifecycle stages defined in [Project Lifecycle Policy](../governance/project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:

- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** (*Impact Stage*): Open protocol enabling LLM applications to integrate with external data sources and tools.
- **Goose** (*Impact Stage*): Extensible open-source AI agent runtime executing multi-turn tool commands and local edits.
- **AGENTS.MD** (*Impact Stage*): Standardized format for declaring agent skills, constraints, and operational metadata.

# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group defines vendor-neutral specifications, ingestion data models, and instrumentation patterns for capturing causal execution traces across agent interactions, tool calls, and host environments.

# Architecture / Specification

## Agent Behavior Trace Model

The working group is developing a standardized Agent Behavior Trace Model to bridge AAIF behavioral semantics with industry observability frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]:

- **Core Entities & Relationships**: Formally defining scopes across conversations, sessions, turns, tool calls, proposed actions, and observations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Decoupled Identifiers**: Enabling turn and action tracing where approvals, rejections, or missing tool executions reference proposed actions independently of span lifetimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **OpenTelemetry Crosswalk**: Mapping AAIF trace terminology directly to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions while preserving parent execution contexts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline defines architectural safeguards, authentication standards, and operational controls required to securely deploy autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents into production environments.

# Architecture / Specification

## Workload Identity & Cross-Boundary Delegation

While baseline guidance relies on 1-hour cloud IAM role scopes, multi-cloud and hybrid deployments introduce additional trust boundary constraints under active specification [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]:

- **Federated OIDC Workload Identity**: Standardizing OIDC federation patterns between distinct cloud IAM systems to avoid static credentials during cross-cloud agent tool execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Cross-Cloud Role Assumption**: Enforcing strict least-privilege boundaries when an agent executing in one cloud provider requests access to resources hosted in an external cloud or on-premises environment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Token Lifetime & Rotation Controls**: Evaluating bounded short-lived token lifetimes tailored to autonomous execution runs to minimize delegation blast radius [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

# References

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows & Process Integration Working Group defines runtime execution models, compositional patterns, activity schemas, and validation methodologies for reliable agent orchestration within enterprise workflows.

# Architecture / Specification

## Reference Architecture Contribution Model

The working group organizes its technical assets into distinct structural artifact types [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]:

- **Patterns**: Context-free, independently reusable solutions addressing recurring failure modes (e.g., durable wait, human approval gate) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Reference Architectures**: Reusable compositions of patterns, capability roles, boundaries, and exit guarantees that fulfill a recognizable practitioner job (e.g., bounded autonomous remediation) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Worked Scenarios & Validation Records**: Concrete implementation instances used to validate whether an architecture satisfies real-world use cases without creating domain-locked architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

## Open Schema Classifications

The group maintains active discussions resolving taxonomy and use case schema ambiguity, such as distinguishing parallel fan-out (timing/concurrency) versus sequential pipelines (dependency order) in multi-agent execution flows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

# References

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Use Case Validation Guide
proposed_concept.description: Standardized methodology and criteria for evaluating whether a real-world use case aligns with an AAIF reference architecture.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Reference Architecture Use Case Validation Guide defines a repeatable, lightweight evaluation process for assessing whether an AAIF Reference Architecture (RA) is an architectural fit for a specific real-world use case [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. Intended for both human contributors and AI coding agents, validation focuses on matching the primary job and defining boundaries rather than verifying implementation-level mechanics [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# Architecture / Specification
Validation determines whether an RA provides the architectural controls needed to implement a target use case safely [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

## Core Validation Principles
- **Job and Boundary Fit:** A use case is marked `Validated` when the source demonstrates the RA's primary job and key operational boundaries, even if specific runtime mechanics (such as credential storage or exact retry backoff) are not detailed [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Sourced Evidence Requirement:** Evidence must derive from stated facts in the Use Case Inventory or cited external artifacts, rather than illustrative scenario text embedded within RA specifications [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Constrained Check Counts:** Evaluations must establish two or three concise checks derived from the RA's purpose, checklist, boundaries, and guarantees [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

## Evaluation Outcomes
1. **Validated:** The RA's primary job, actor roles (agent, workflow engine, human, external system), and boundaries match the use case [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
2. **Partial:** Some architectural boundaries or capabilities align, but key operational requirements or control paths diverge [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].
3. **No Fit:** The use case core requirements contradict the structural guarantees or authority model of the RA [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].
4. **Candidate:** Initial alignment observed, but essential evidence is missing or requires further investigation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

## Contributor and Agent Guidelines
AI and human contributors follow standardized intake workflows, submitting a GitHub Issue when guidance or evidence is lacking, or opening a focused pull request against the RA's validation record when evidence is clear [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64, ^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# References

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Job-oriented reference architecture orchestrating autonomous agent iteration over fenced problems under deterministic gates and constrained effect executors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a job-oriented reference architecture designed to autonomously resolve bounded, fenced problems using independent acceptance evidence and deterministic escalation when execution fails to converge [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. It serves tasks with pre-declared boundaries, constrained effects, and objective success conditions without requiring continuous human approval during iterations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture composes three core workflow patterns: [Bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [Deterministic acceptance gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md), and [Proposal/execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

## Architectural Guarantees
- **Bounded Autonomy:** The agent operates strictly within task-scoped credentials, data, tool sets, and iteration/cost budgets [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Independent Acceptance:** A deterministic gate (such as a test runner, schema validator, or policy engine), not the agent itself, evaluates whether proposed changes satisfy acceptance criteria [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Controlled Effect:** Only accepted, validated outputs reach the constrained effect executor; the agent cannot invoke external side effects directly [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Safe Non-Convergence:** Exhausted budgets, repeated failures, or out-of-scope conditions cleanly terminate into recorded failure states and escalate to human operators [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

## Component Structure
The logical capabilities comprise:
1. **Execution Engine:** Manages workflow admission, sequencing, retry policies, timeouts, and state tracking [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
2. **Bounded Agent Environment:** Executes model-driven reasoning and tool dispatches within isolated context boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
3. **Isolated Work Area:** Maintains candidate artifacts and non-authoritative scratchpads during convergence attempts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
4. **Deterministic Acceptance Gate:** Executes definitive verification criteria (e.g., test suites, linters, contract checks) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b, ^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
5. **Constrained Effect Executor:** Applies verified modifications to external systems (such as pushing PRs or emitting corrected records) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
6. **Audit Log & Escalation Surface:** Records immutable telemetry and surfaces blocked or non-convergent runs for operator triage [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

## Fit Checklist
Practitioners evaluate applicability using five baseline criteria:
1. Explicitly bounded problem scope prior to execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
2. Verifiable deterministic acceptance criteria [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
3. Constrained, reversible, or low-impact external effects [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
4. Strict agent sandboxing and isolated working state [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
5. Defined non-success and escalation paths [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

## Validated Scenarios
- **Autonomous Maintenance Run ("Night Shift"):** Validated for scheduled, routine dependency upgrades, lint fixes, and test remediations where CI test suites act as the acceptance gate before generating pull requests [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

# References
- [Bounded Convergence Loop Pattern](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md)
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate Pattern](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- [Proposal/Execution Split Pattern](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Workflow Architecture Principles](../policies-guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md)

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating a shared SKOS-Lite agentic AI vocabulary and ecosystem market map across all technical working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across all Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Technical Working Groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Its mandate is to eliminate siloed terminology, prevent duplicated research across working groups, and maintain a unified SKOS-Lite taxonomy alongside a CNCF-style ecosystem market map[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac], the workstream coordinates nominated Domain Editors from each technical working group to ingest, harmonize, and standardize cross-cutting vocabulary without infringing on domain-specific working group sovereignty[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Scope Boundaries
The workstream operates under the "Horizontal Index" principle[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]:
- **Shared Index (In-Scope):** Foundational terms and cross-cutting concepts affecting two or more working groups, along with universal market categorization[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Domain Payload (Out-of-Scope):** Specialized whitepapers, internal technical helper definitions, schema variables, and wire protocol designs belong exclusively to vertical working group repositories[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Contribution Scope Gate:** Active contributions are limited strictly to the Taxonomy; Landscape contributions are deferred on the future roadmap until intake processes are formally approved[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].

## Domain Editors and Working Group Delegates
Each vertical working group nominates Domain Editors to shepherd candidate terms into the shared vocabulary[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
- [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md): Casper Nielsen, Matthew Khouzam[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md): Leonardo Galesky[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Amithash Kankanallu Jagadish[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md): Julianna Mealin[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md): Pavan Sudheendra, Matt Lee[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md): Jautau White, Katherine Druckman[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md): Sumanth Sathyanarayana[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]

## Taxonomy Lifecycle & Schema Specifications
Candidate terms are logged in the Taxonomy Working Spreadsheet and triaged as `Debate`, `Keep`, or `Cull`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. Merged terms in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` follow a SKOS-Lite object structure[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]:
- **Epistemological Disambiguation:** Contrasting concepts (e.g., Tool vs. Skill) must explicitly define boundaries in their definitions and link via `relatedTerms` (`skos:related`) or `contrastsWith`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Anti-Erasure Guardrails:** Concepts cannot be deleted or aliased without explicit written approval from the owning working group's Domain Editor[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Deferred Initial Check-in Fields:** Definitions, broader terms, and category assignments are temporarily deferred while cross-group scope boundaries are established[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

## Automated Quality Metrics
The workstream tracks ecosystem health through four KPIs: Citation Utility, Vendor-Neutral Diversity (no corporate entity authoring >50%), Ecosystem Coverage (>=10 terms per active working group), and Arbitration Velocity[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Accuracy & Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey instrument gathering empirical data on real-world AI agent deployments, failure modes, and industry priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Accuracy & Reliability Survey is a platform-neutral, 16-question empirical evaluation instrument published by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. It collects firsthand operational experiences from practitioners building, operating, and evaluating agentic AI systems in production and pilot environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

The survey is designed to identify common failure modes, quantify human oversight patterns, and prioritize open standards development across the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligibility and Focal-System Gating
The instrument requires respondents to anchor answers to a single focal system worked with during the preceding six months[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. Eligibility is evaluated in Q1 through five qualifying deployment stages[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]:
- **Serious pilot:** Tested in an intended work setting to assess real task performance.
- **Limited deployment:** Integrated into normal work for select users or workflows.
- **Broad deployment:** Operational across most intended users or workflows.
- **Paused or retired:** Reached pilot or deployment before discontinuation.
- **Uncertain real-world stage:** Confirmed real work use with undefined classification.

Respondents with only demo, prototype, secondhand, or non-work experience are routed to an early-exit termination path[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

## Survey Structure and Core Domains
The survey covers five analytical sections using single-select, multi-select, Likert matrix, and inline text formats[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]:
1. **System & Role Profile (Q1–Q5):** Deployment stage, direct technical/operational activities, work domain, architectural structure, and organization headcount[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
2. **Benefits & Operational Constraints (Q6–Q8):** Operating constraints, human output checking practices, and top operational benefits[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
3. **Accuracy & Reliability Metrics (Q9–Q13):** Frequency of unacceptable results, root-cause reliability factors, pre-impact failure detection mechanisms, consequence severity, and quality evidence sources[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
4. **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16):** Industry-wide technical priorities, preferred open source deliverables, and qualitative input[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative responsible for maintaining the foundation's shared technical vocabulary (Taxonomy) and ecosystem map (Landscape) across all active technical working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu and Gala Malbasic, the workstream provides standardized terminology schemas and intake processes to ensure cross-working-group interoperability[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope and Current Focus
The workstream structures foundation knowledge across two main assets[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8]:
- **Taxonomy Glossary:** Active core scope using a SKOS-Lite-compliant schema capturing display terms, categories, broader hierarchy terms, definitions, aliases, and working group alignments[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8]. Terms must be cross-cutting ($\\ge 2$ working groups), pre-competitive, technically precise, and deduplicated without unverified alias folding[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].
- **Ecosystem Landscape:** Market landscape map visualizing projects and runtimes; public community intake remains paused on the roadmap pending accepted review processes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].

## Governance and PR Review Workflow
Curation is distributed across three designated roles[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8]:
- **Contributors:** Community members submitting glossary terms via Git pull requests or GitHub issue proposal templates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].
- **Domain Editors:** Working group delegates nominated from the seven active Technical Working Groups who author and peer-review entries. Approvals require consensus from at least two or three Domain Editors representing distinct working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].
- **Maintainers (Co-Chairs):** Administrative maintainers with repository write access who conduct final administrative checks and merge accepted pull requests[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-333c16a8].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync-badges` skill automates the generation, styling, and idempotent distribution of official AAIF community organizer badge assets across regional chapter workspaces[^evt-community-events-pr-39]. It produces vector and raster badges using foundation design tokens and synchronizes them directly into Google Drive folder hierarchies[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification
## Badge Styles and Generation
The generation pipeline supports two parallel badge variants, yielding six files per chapter[^evt-community-events-pr-39]:
- **Classic Badge:** Hand-tuned orange badge layout generated via `make_badges.py`[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Agent Design-System Badge:** Generated via `make_agent_badge.py` consuming live tokens from `design/aaif-tokens.css`, embedded Instrument Sans typography, and per-chapter agent mascot artwork (`agent_art.chapter_scene()`), rendered through headless Chrome[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

## Storage Hierarchy and Synchronization
- **Per-Chapter Destination:** Badges are stored in a designated `Badges/` subfolder inside each chapter's root Google Drive folder rather than a flat global bucket[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Drive Migration:** Includes `migrate_legacy_badges.py` for atomic Drive reparenting (`addParents`/`removeParents`) and non-destructive trash cleanup[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Security and Escaping:** Untrusted chapter display names are XML-escaped prior to SVG injection to prevent template injection vulnerabilities[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand & Visual Design Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual design, typography, surface, and asset usage standards defining the neutral, flat design system across AAIF materials.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand & Visual Design Guidelines define the neutral, flat visual identity, typography hierarchy, token palettes, and asset creation rules across all Agentic AI Foundation digital and document surfaces[^evt-community-events-pr-34][^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification
## Typography System & Document Embedding Policy
AAIF typography strictly enforces designated typefaces across prose and technical metadata[^evt-community-events-pr-34]:
- **Prose Typeface:** Instrument Sans is used for body copy, titles, and headings[^evt-community-events-pr-34][^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Monospace Typeface:** JetBrains Mono is designated for field labels, table headers, dates, statuses, IDs, and code runs[^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Metric Fallback:** Manrope serves as the embedded metric-compatible fallback font for environments where primary web fonts are not locally present[^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Embedding Rules (`NEVER_EMBED`):** To optimize document payload size across OOXML (`.docx`) exports, ubiquitous Google Fonts such as Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono are declared in document tables but excluded from physical font binary embedding, retaining embeds only for fallback metrics like Manrope[^evt-community-events-pr-34].

## Design Tokens & Renderers
- **Token Single Source of Truth:** Live palette and surface tokens are defined centrally in `design/aaif-tokens.css`[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

proposed_concept.description: Visual design, typography, surface tokens, and OOXML asset styling standards defining the AAIF brand design system.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the visual design language, typographic hierarchy, surface palettes, and asset formatting standards across web, PDF, and office document surfaces [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. The system emphasizes a neutral, minimal, flat design aesthetic with distinct ink ramps and spectrum accents.

# Architecture / Specification
The brand system enforces tokenized styling across HTML, PDF, and OOXML documents (`.pptx`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`) to eliminate manual hex and ad-hoc font drift [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Typography
- **Primary / Display / Theme Face**: Instrument Sans serves as the canonical face across presentation decks, word processing documents, and tracking sheets [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Code / Monospace**: Monospace fonts are restricted to structured data and code blocks rather than body copy [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Palette and Design Tokens
- **Neutrals**: AAIF ink and line ramp tokens (`--line-2`, `--ink-4`, `--ink-3`) govern borders, metadata text, and secondary copy [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Headers & Plates**: Table and tracker headers utilize black plates with hairline borders rather than arbitrary dark navy fills [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Spectrum Accents**: Status and geographic indicators use tokenized spectrum accents such as `--spec-3` for map markers [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Contrast and Legibility Validation
Color applications must undergo automated background-to-foreground contrast resolution checking (shape fill -> slide background -> layout -> master -> white) to prevent illegible token pairings [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

# Lifecycle History
The OOXML estate was conformed to `design/aaif-tokens.css` standards to reconcile office documents and chapter slide decks with web token standards [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

- **Slack Organizers & Directory Automation**: Reconciles chapter organizer invitations across private organizer rooms and public Country Channels (`--scope {organizer,country,both}`) while maintaining additive country-level chapter directory postings without overwriting human edits [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

# Overview

The `aaif-sync-chapters` skill provides standardized automation for synchronizing community chapter CRM records, intake decisions, Slack channels, and organizer permissions.

# Architecture / Specification

## Report-First Safety and Write Gates

The skill implements a strict report-first boundary aligned with the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) patterns. Every engine within `aaif-sync-chapters` defaults to dry-run reporting, summarizing intended mutations before performing state changes [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. Live CRM modifications and downstream permission updates require explicit approval rather than executing straight to writes [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

## Intake Routing

The skill is triggered during intake decision workflows when chapter proposals or application statuses require synchronization across tracking sheets and communications infrastructure [^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a].

# Lifecycle History

Automated eval graders in the `aaif/community-events` repository test both skill invocation on intake decisions [^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a] and enforcement of the pre-write approval gate [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Overview
The `aaif-triage-intake` skill is an automated workflow capability designed to inspect applicant queues for AAIF community programs, generate intake digests, and preserve execution safety against indirect prompt injections embedded in user submissions [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92][^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates under a strict data-instruction separation model when evaluating free-text intake fields [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf]:
- **Queue Inspection**: Triggers when human operators query pending decisions across intake queues, reading records without executing unauthorized state mutations [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92].
- **Untrusted Input Isolation**: Treats quoted application responses exclusively as evaluation data rather than execution instructions, neutralizing attempts to override status transitions or channel memberships via prompt injection [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf][^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].
- **Human Escalation**: Requires ambiguous or directive-laden submissions to be flagged for explicit human review rather than executing autonomous state mutations [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf].

proposed_concept.title: Core Workflow Terms
proposed_concept.description: Foundational vocabulary for agentic AI workflows defining activities, executions, state, context, and business tasks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF core workflow vocabulary establishes formal definitions and disambiguations for orchestrating agentic AI systems across heterogeneous runtimes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]. It separates deterministic orchestration infrastructure from probabilistic execution units and business-level domain work items.

# Architecture / Specification

## Activity vs. Business Task

To prevent ambiguity between orchestrator-level execution steps and domain work items, AAIF workflow standards maintain an explicit distinction [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]:

- **Activity**: A granular, composable workflow subunit representing a distinct deterministic or agentic execution step managed by the workflow orchestrator.
- **Business Task**: The high-level bounded business problem or work item admitted to and resolved by a workflow execution run.

This boundary ensures that reference architectures such as [bounded autonomous remediation](../reference-architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) and patterns like the [bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md) cleanly delineate between workflow engine execution boundaries and external business state.

## Core State and Execution Concepts

- **Execution**: A distinct, state-tracked invocation of a workflow or activity.
- **Context**: The cumulative durable and ephemeral parameters available during an execution.
- **State**: The recorded checkpoints ensuring durable recovery and determinism across agent steps.

proposed_concept.title: Public Agent Skills and Evaluation Harnesses
proposed_concept.description: Standardized skill definitions, prompt triggers, negative regression suites, and comparative evaluation harnesses for agentic AI workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

AAIF public agent skills are portable, standardized execution units and prompt descriptions designed to run safely across AI agent runtimes [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd]. To guarantee that skills fire reliably without triggering neighbouring capabilities or violating safety boundaries, skills are verified through structured, dual-arm evaluation test harnesses [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].

# Architecture / Specification

## Skill Evaluation Framework

Deterministic checks such as static schema validation and script unit tests verify syntax, but behavioral reliability requires prompt-driven triggering and constraint evaluations [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].

### Trigger Disambiguation and Negative Gradings
Skills operating in close semantic domains (e.g., event announcements, recaps, and reminders) are susceptible to misclassification [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76]. Evaluation suites assert two distinct criteria:
1. **Target Activation**: Validates that the intended skill fires given a natural conversational prompt [^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76][^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e].
2. **Negative Neighbour Exclusion**: Asserts via trace regex matching that adjacent domain skills are not erroneously invoked [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

### Dual-Arm Delta Evaluation (`arm: with-only`)
Evaluations execute in paired runs: once with the candidate skill enabled and once without [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd]. Gradings designated as `with-only` ensure assertions only pass when the skill documentation actively enforces constraints (such as stripping PII or enforcing authorization gates) that the base model fails by default [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines vendor-neutral specifications, data models, and reference architectures for tracing AI agent execution, causal context, tool interactions, and infrastructure telemetry across distributed boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's scope spans multiple telemetry layers and operational deliverables:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A structured nine-task execution plan establishing causal relationships connecting model inference calls, retry attempts, approval decisions, tool executions, and external effects across service boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44] The model correlates proposed actions to approval events and observed tool execution receipts without presuming that observation constitutes proof of enforcement.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Reference patterns and telemetry propagation models capturing context across agent routers, gateways, and external registries, integrating standards such as W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-25] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]
- **Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) Alignment**: Investigating federation and discovery interfaces for agent registries to ensure unified end-to-end trace context propagation across heterogeneous agent frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]
- **Best Practices and Standards**: Developing vendor-neutral agentic observability white papers and exploring future standardization submissions (such as IETF RFC drafts).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09-16**: The working group approved monthly APAC/APJ synchronization meetings, tracked taxonomy submissions, reviewed Agent Behavior Trace Model milestones, and initiated planning for vendor-neutral observability white papers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Observability
proposed_concept.description: Observability architecture and context propagation specification for agent tool dispatches across local CLI subprocess boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Observability specification defines how causal trace context, execution metadata, and security boundaries propagate when an AI agent runtime invokes tools via local CLI subprocesses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. It distinguishes the abstract semantic boundary (`Agent → Tool`) from its operational realization (`Agent Runtime → Local Process`), providing standard mechanisms to prevent causality loss during detached or direct subprocess execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].

# Architecture / Specification

## Boundary Separation and Telemetry Propagation

The specification addresses eight cross-boundary observability dimensions across agent execution contexts:
- **Identity & Context**: Propagated across process boundaries using standard W3C Trace Context and W3C Baggage mapped via the OpenTelemetry environment-variable context carrier Release Candidate specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Span Composition**: Reconciles `execute_tool` spans emitted by the agent runtime with process-level CLI spans created upon subprocess invocation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Pre-execution Span Reservation**: Supports pre-execution span-ID allocation patterns (as validated in LoongSuite Pilot) to ensure child subprocess telemetry correctly attaches to parent causal graphs prior to fork/exec cycles [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Span Links for Detached Execution**: Uses OpenTelemetry Span Links rather than strict parent-child causality when tools execute asynchronously or detached in background daemon processes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Resource Bootstrap**: Ensures process environment bootstrap properties remain isolated from dynamic per-invocation baggage [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

## Cross-Boundary Gap Coverage

This architecture directly addresses the direct invocation gaps documented in the Observability and Traceability Working Group gap matrix [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29], ensuring tool telemetry preserves causal attribution back to originating agent reasoning steps.

# References

- OpenTelemetry Environment Variable Context Carrier RC [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-sync-chapters` skill automates the synchronization, lifecycle maintenance, and health auditing of AAIF regional community chapters across Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Slack [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. The automation enforces estate governance rules, including a hard ceiling of 100 chapters, standardized chapter lifecycle status tracking, and synchronization for the workspace-wide `#local-champs` leadership room [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification

## Estate Governance & Lifecycle States

Chapter estate growth is bounded by `CHAPTER_CAP = 100` [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. New chapter creation requires retiring, merging, or deprecating existing entries. Chapter records maintain explicit lifecycle statuses:
- `Active`: Verified active chapter with regular community events and communication [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- `Provisioned`: Initialized chapter infrastructure pending launch [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- `Dormant`: Inactive chapter identified through health sweeps [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- `Merged`: Consolidated chapter pointing to a companion `Merged Into` chapter [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- `Deprecated`: Decommissioned chapter record [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

## Slack Organizer Synchronization

The skill synchronizes accepted organizers into the global `#local-champs` Slack channel as part of standard invitation workflows, preventing drift between intake rosters and channel membership [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

## Audit and Measurement Bounds

Activity evaluations respect strict Slack API scope and visibility boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]:
- Silence is distinguished from lack of data: lack of recorded event history alone does not mark a chapter dormant if recent human messaging is observed in Slack [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- Token capabilities are validated pre-flight to prevent scope missing errors from misreporting organizer presence or channel activity [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

proposed_concept.description: Hosted open interoperability protocol standardizing communication, discovery, and signed agent cards between autonomous AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A) is an AAIF hosted project establishing a vendor-neutral interoperability layer for direct communication, capability discovery, and task delegation between autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]. A2A introduced signed agent cards to declare capabilities and trust metadata, providing a foundation for multi-agent coordination and mediation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Capabilities

- **Signed Agent Cards**: Self-describing cryptographically signed metadata documents detailing agent capabilities, authentication endpoints, and operational constraints [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **Interoperability & Mediation**: Compatible with runtime traffic mediation gateways such as `agentgateway` for policy enforcement and routing across MCP and A2A networks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **Verification & Telemetry**: Integrates with observability standards to enable runtime verification of signed card claims against observed agent behavior and execution telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

# Lifecycle History

- **March 2026**: A2A v1.0 specification released introducing signed agent cards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **August 2026**: Formally joined the Agentic AI Foundation as a hosted project [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, causal lineage formats, and independent verification models for autonomous AI agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29]. The group coordinates specifications across execution runtimes, tool boundaries, gateways, and external standards bodies including the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams & Deliverables

- **Cross-Boundary Observability Gap Model**: Systematic mapping of observability properties (identity, context, relationship, lifecycle, outcome, provenance, security, timing) across six critical agent interaction boundaries (`Agent → Skill`, `Skill → Tool`, `Agent → Agent`, `Agent → MCP server`, `Agent → A2A peer`, `Agent → Gateway/Runtime`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].
- **Control-Plane Telemetry & Evidence Modeling**: Framework modeling independent boundary observations (gateways, sidecars, runtimes) along observation source and observation relationship dimensions to reconcile agent self-reports into verified agreement, contradiction, or absence of independent evidence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
- **Tool & CLI Process Instrumentation**: Telemetry propagation standards bridging agent execution contexts across local CLI subprocesses, containers, and remote APIs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Hosted Project Interoperability**: Telemetry and verification surface analysis for hosted projects including [A2A](../projects/a2a.md) and `agentgateway` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].

# References

- [Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Observability](../reference-architectures/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md)

# Overview
`aaif-sync` is the front-door orchestration skill responsible for managing whole-estate synchronization across AAIF community assets, coordinating execution across underlying phase skills.[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836] It establishes an ordered pipeline ensuring estate health reports and data reconciliation precede any downstream state writes or credential grants.[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]

# Architecture / Specification
When whole-estate drift occurs across spreadsheets, Google Drive folders, and Slack channels, `aaif-sync` serves as the primary entry point rather than invoking phase-specific skills independently.[^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a] [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5]

### Pipeline Execution Order
The synchronization workflow enforces a strict phase sequence to prevent premature privilege grants or uncoordinated messaging:[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]
1. Reconcile chapter database rows and CRM records.
2. Emit validation reports before proposing or executing mutation steps.
3. Coordinate individual phase skills (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, and `aaif-sync-slack`) in sequence.[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5] [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]
4. Grant storage permissions (e.g., Google Drive access) and post external channel updates only after base entity schemas are settled.[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Audit Slack Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized automation skill auditing Slack channel mappings, coverage classifications, and matching configurations against the AAIF Community Chapters List.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-audit-slack` audits Slack workspaces against the AAIF Community Chapters List spreadsheet, matching regional, organizer, and public community channels against chapter registries.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] Configuration rules and channel alias mappings are maintained in shared spreadsheets to enable direct community organizer curation without repository pull requests.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

# Architecture / Specification
The audit engine reads mappings and matching configurations directly from the Community Chapters List spreadsheet rather than static JSON files.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

### Chapter List Schema Columns
- `Slack Channel`: Dedicated public channel for a chapter when slug conventions diverge (e.g., `San Francisco → bay-area`).[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- `Organizer Channel`: Chapter organizer channel when naming departs from `<city>-organizers`.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- `Country Channel`: Regional broadcast room serving an area without representing a local city chapter; reported as regional coverage only.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- `Ops Notes`: Free-text field reserved for human operator notes; excluded from automated mutation.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

### Matching Engine and Sentinel Values
- **Sentinels**: A blank cell triggers fallback scanning across prioritized prefixes and suffixes, while the explicit string literal `none` designates that no channel exists.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- **Slack Config Tab**: Configures prioritized matching lists such as `Public channel prefix` (starting with `(none)` for bare slugs, followed by `meetup-`, `aaif-`) and `Organizer channel suffix` (`-organizers`, `-organisers`). Row order is strictly load-bearing.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- **Human Confirmation Gate**: Candidate aliases and near-misses must be proposed to an operator for explicit verification before write-back, preventing automated assignment of ambiguous channel aliases.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared trace identity and relationship contract defining agent conversation, runtime session, turn, and tool execution boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a shared identity and relationship contract drafted by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize agent telemetry across heterogeneous runtimes and platforms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]. It formalizes how behavioral observations—such as conversations, sessions, turns, model dispatches, approval gates, and tool executions—relate to one another and to external environmental side effects.

The model establishes standard crosswalks with [OpenTelemetry](../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md) GenAI conventions while defining formal interpretation rules for correlation, deduplication, and incomplete telemetry sequences.

# Architecture / Specification

### Identity Taxonomy

The contract delineates eight distinct telemetry entity identities[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
- **Conversation**: The top-level user or multi-agent interaction context.
- **Runtime Session**: The execution boundary of the host process or agent runtime.
- **Turn**: An iteration step initiated by an input and bounded by model decisions.
- **Model Call**: A discrete inference invocation dispatched to a language model.
- **Proposed Action**: An action intent emitted by the model prior to authorization.
- **Approval Decision**: A deterministic or human gate decision granting or denying execution.
- **Tool Execution**: The dispatch and outcome of an external tool or capability.
- **External Effect**: State changes produced outside the immediate runtime fence.

### Interpretation and Boundary Rules

The specification prescribes deterministic telemetry ingestion and evaluation semantics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
- **Missing Observation**: A missing event in a sequence must be treated as `unknown`, never inferred as zero or absent.
- **Deduplication**: Duplicate telemetry events must deduplicate strictly by correlation key.
- **Order Invariance**: Reordered event arrival at an ingestion sink must not alter the derived trace topology or evaluation outcome.

# Lifecycle History

- Proposed as draft v0.1 in the Observability and Traceability Working Group under PR #51 updating baseline requirements[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Community Sync Orchestrator
proposed_concept.description: Standardized automation skill managing end-to-end community estate synchronization across a 7-phase x 3-stage execution pipeline.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

`aaif-sync` is the top-level automation skill and primary entry point for orchestrating AAIF community infrastructure, CRM state, chapter lifecycles, organizer permissions, and Slack channels[^evt-community-events-pr-49]. It coordinates execution across a matrix of operational phases while enforcing deterministic human approval gates, state safety guards, and idempotent workspace mutations.

# Architecture / Specification

### Pipeline Structure

The synchronization pipeline is structured along two axes: subject **Phase** and execution **Stage**[^evt-community-events-pr-49]:
- **Phases**: Seven domain phases governing intake, chapter status, organizer credentials, badges, Slack channels, CRM state, and audit reporting.
- **Stages**: Every phase executes sequentially through `gather`, `plan`, and `execute`.

### Safety and Execution Guarantees

- **Human Triage Gate**: Intake triage acts as a strict human gate; the runner reports queue depth and halts modifications (exit code 2) while unreviewed candidates remain[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Non-Idempotent Write Guard**: Google Workspace mutations that risk creating duplicate resources (e.g., folder creation, tab addition, dimension insertion) are explicitly protected with `NO_RETRY` to prevent orphan duplicates on network timeouts[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Stateless Runs and Findings**: The runner preserves no state between executions, emitting standard findings data (`findings.py`) that render a consolidated HTML run report summarizing estate health[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Lifecycle History

- Refactored into a procedural, code-driven 7-phase pipeline with unified findings reporting and `NO_RETRY` mutation guards[^evt-community-events-pr-49][^evt-community-events-pr-51].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared trace identity and relationship contract defining agent conversation, runtime session, turn, and tool execution correlation across OpenTelemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a shared trace identity and relationship contract that enables tracking an AI agent's execution across turns, interruptions, and distributed system boundaries using OpenTelemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model defines standard identities and relationship conventions connecting model calls, retries, approval decisions, tool executions, and independently observed effects[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

The initial implementation and validation harness centers on four core evaluation questions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
1. **Continuity:** Identifying which turns belong together across pauses or restarts.
2. **Calls and retries:** Mapping model dispatches to their respective turns without double-counting work.
3. **Approvals:** Correlating human or automated approval decisions to corresponding action executions.
4. **Effects:** Connecting external state changes to specific agent actions via independent telemetry.

# Architecture / Specification

The trace model operates across distinct identity and boundary abstractions to separate conversation continuity from protocol-level transport[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:

- **Session and Conversation Identity:** Explicitly distinguishes persistent conversational continuity from short-lived protocol or runtime transport sessions.
- **Turn Boundaries:** Evaluates a candidate default of one trace per turn while preserving inbound caller trace context, turn-entry span identification, and approval wait/resumption state transitions.
- **Evidence and Telemetry Semantics:** Treats missing spans or signals as unknown state rather than zero or success, keeping payload capture opt-in while separating observed approval telemetry from cryptographic policy attestation.
- **Execution Plan of Record:** Implemented across a nine-task plan covering baseline capture, contract specification, test fixture generation, multi-runtime reference implementations (in [Goose](goose.md) and an independent SDK), multi-reader verification, and upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI contributions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

# References

- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture](opentelemetry.md)
- [Goose Runtime](goose.md)
- [Human Approval Gate Pattern](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
