# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to define vendor-neutral specifications, telemetry conventions, and trace relationship models for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. The working group focuses on the intersection of agent reasoning, tool execution, and observable trace signals, bridging AI application runtimes with upstream telemetry standards such as OpenTelemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group operates under the governance of the AAIF Technical Committee[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]:

- **Chairs:** Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and co-chaired by Matthew Lee (Datadog) for the March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 term[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Meeting Cadence:** Meets biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM PT, with public agendas, meeting minutes, and recordings published on LFX[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Key Deliverables:**
  - [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../reference-architectures/agent-behavior-trace-model.md): A nine-task specification and evaluation plan defining multi-turn continuity, call/retry mappings, approval gating, and external effect correlation in OpenTelemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
  - Semantic convention proposals and gap analyses submitted to upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI working groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
  - Cross-layer tracing architectures spanning userspace frameworks, kernel profilers, and accelerator hardware.

proposed_concept.description: Standardized automation skill managing end-to-end community estate synchronization across multi-step report and write workflows with run-scoped caching.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-sync` skill is a multi-step orchestration engine responsible for synchronizing AAIF community estate data across Google Workspace (Sheets, Drive) and Slack[^evt-community-events-pr-52]. It executes a modular sequence of sync steps (including chapters, organizers, and CRM workbooks) while enforcing consistency and preventing redundant external API calls[^evt-community-events-pr-52].

# Architecture / Specification

The sync engine uses a modular execution harness optimized for rate-limited upstream APIs[^evt-community-events-pr-52]:

- **Run-Scoped Memos:** Ephemeral, append-only JSONL run memo caches (`AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO` and `AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO`) maintain query results during execution runs and are strictly deleted upon run completion or interruption[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Read/Write Consistency Boundaries:** The Google Workspace memo cache operates exclusively during report runs (`--report`); write-enabled runs (`--write`) bypass read memoization to guarantee that downstream engines read freshly committed mutations from preceding steps[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Parallel CRM Resolution:** Multi-worker thread pools (such as a six-worker pool in `sync_crm`) accelerate chapter workbook queries while maintaining deterministic, sequential folder planning[^evt-community-events-pr-52].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Sync Automation Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized automation skill executing the end-to-end 18-step community estate pipeline with process sleep suppression.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Sync automation skill manages the end-to-end synchronization pipeline for the Agentic AI Foundation community estate[^evt-community-events-pr-53]. It coordinates the complete 18-step operational workflow spanning member access, chapter health metrics, and event indexing without narrowing steps to save execution time[^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification
The sync runner executes an 18-step serial pipeline to ensure state consistency across foundation repositories and external tracking systems[^evt-community-events-pr-53].

## Process Execution and Sleep Suppression
To prevent stalled execution and expired third-party session tokens during multi-step runs, the runner implements system sleep inhibition[^evt-community-events-pr-53]:
- On macOS systems, the runner spawns a child process invoking `caffeinate -i -w <runner pid>` via standard library process handlers (`subprocess.Popen` and `shutil.which`)[^evt-community-events-pr-53].
- The sleep inhibition process automatically terminates when the main runner process finishes, crashes, or is interrupted[^evt-community-events-pr-53].
- Environments outside macOS or systems lacking `caffeinate` execute the pipeline standardly without spawning extraneous helper processes[^evt-community-events-pr-53].
- Full sync runs execute as a unified 18-step pass taking approximately 11.5 to 20 minutes of wall clock time rather than selective partial executions[^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) develops standard execution models, activity schemas, and workflow integration patterns for agentic systems within the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group structures its core initiatives across reference architectures, taxonomy definitions, and critical use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into three active work streams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]:
- **Reference Architectures**: Defining and prioritizing reference architectures for multi-turn agent execution and enterprise process integration[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Cataloging, evaluating, and prioritizing real-world enterprise agent integration scenarios[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

## Cross-Group Alignment and Governance
To prevent terminology divergence across disparate working groups, the group actively collaborates with global taxonomy leads to coordinate core definitions and advocates for Technical Committee oversight to resolve cross-WG term overlaps[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

proposed_concept.title: Evidence Record Specification
proposed_concept.description: Testable JSON Schema and data model encoding observation sources, verification vantages, integrity grades (E0-E4), and claim reconciliation for tamper-evident agent evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Evidence Record Specification is a testable data model and schema designed to address the E4 tamper-evident evidence gap in agent telemetry and audit trails[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37]. It establishes an implementation-free, evidence-grade trace interchange format and validation framework for agent observations, claims, and verification states[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification defines a JSON Schema and semantic validation rules covering four primary structural dimensions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37]:
- **Observation**: Identifies the telemetry source (spanning agent self-reporting through external authoritative monitors) and relationship semantics (direct, corroborating, contradictory, or derived)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37].
- **Verification**: Encodes verification basis as a composition of vantage (substrate vs. artifact) and capture method (intercepted vs. reconstructed)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37].
- **Integrity Grades**: Adopts an E0 to E4 ladder (Declared, Observed, Enforced, Corroborated, Anchored) with explicit grade-to-integrity baseline requirements[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37].
- **Claims and Reconciliation**: Standardizes emission-conformant and operationally-conformant claims alongside a three-state reconciliation model (agreement, contradiction, or no independent evidence)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in the Observability & Traceability Working Group as a concrete, testable interchange artifact evaluated alongside the working group's use case catalog[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-37].

mutations.rationale: Introduces the hard constraint human-in-the-loop pattern separating permanent structural regulatory mandates from confidence-based approval gates.

proposed_concept.title: Hard Constraint Gate
proposed_concept.description: Human-in-the-loop pattern enforcing permanent, non-negotiable regulatory or policy accountability requirements that do not relax as agent reliability improves.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Hard Constraint Gate is a human-in-the-loop (HITL) workflow pattern where human execution or authorization is mandatory due to external regulatory, legal, or institutional policy requirements rather than agent capability limitations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42] Unlike confidence-driven checkpoints, hard constraint gates are structural invariants that remain permanent throughout the system lifecycle and are explicitly excluded from autonomy graduation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

# Architecture / Specification
In agentic workflows, oversight checkpoints historically collapsed two distinct failure modes into generic approval gates: temporary verification because the model is not yet sufficiently trusted, and permanent verification mandated by external accountability structures.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

Hard constraint gates enforce non-negotiable boundaries, such as:
- Physician signatures and medical order approvals in clinical workflows.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]
- Licensed attorney certifications and statutory filings in legal systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]
- Fiduciary and board-level financial authorizations exceeding specified transaction thresholds.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

The pattern operates alongside [Human Approval Gate](./human-approval-gate.md) and [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](./deterministic-acceptance-gate.md), but is formally decoupled from [Autonomy Graduation](./autonomy-graduation.md). While transitional approval gates relax into exception escalation as empirical trust increases, hard constraint gates cannot be bypassed or automated away regardless of model performance.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

# Lifecycle History
Proposed within the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to resolve classification ambiguities in human oversight schemas and distinguish capability-based gates from regulatory requirements.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

mutations.rationale: Documents the autonomy graduation lifecycle pattern where oversight transitions from approval gates to exception escalation while preserving hard constraints.

proposed_concept.title: Autonomy Graduation
proposed_concept.description: Lifecycle pattern governing the progressive relaxation of human oversight from active approval gates to exception escalation as empirical reliability is demonstrated.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Autonomy Graduation is a workflow deployment pattern that models the progressive evolution of human oversight over an agentic system as empirical performance, verification data, and operational trust accumulate.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42] The graduation progression transitions operational checkpoints through defined oversight tiers while holding structural regulatory constraints static.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

# Architecture / Specification
Autonomy Graduation models the operational maturity of agent tasks across three canonical phases:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]
1. **Approval Gate**: Every agent execution or proposal requires explicit human sign-off prior to state mutation (see [Human Approval Gate](./human-approval-gate.md)).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]
2. **Exception Escalation**: The agent executes autonomously within bounded parameters, pausing and alerting an operator only when uncertainty metrics, invariant violations, or policy exceptions occur.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]
3. **Autonomous Execution (None)**: Routine execution proceeds without real-time human intervention, relying on downstream asynchronous audit trails and deterministic bounds.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

### Invariants
- **Exclusion of Hard Constraints**: Structural, regulatory, or statutory requirements (such as clinical signatures or fiduciary thresholds) are classified under [Hard Constraint Gate](./hard-constraint-gate.md) and are permanently barred from graduating to exception-only or autonomous tiers.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]
- **Evidence-Based Progression**: Transitioning between graduation tiers requires empirical validation against predefined accuracy, deterministic checks, and safety metrics.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

# Lifecycle History
Introduced in the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group classification schema to formalize enterprise deployment lifecycles and disambiguate graduated trust from fixed compliance gates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

mutations.rationale: Updates human approval gate to clarify its role as a transitional trust checkpoint distinct from permanent hard constraint gates.

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow architecture pattern requiring an authorized, uniquely identified human to explicitly approve an agent-generated proposal before execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Human Approval Gate is a workflow pattern requiring an authorized, uniquely identified human to explicitly inspect, validate, and approve an agent-generated proposal before any side-effecting action is committed to production state.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42] It serves as a capability-verification and risk-mitigation checkpoint during early deployment stages.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

# Architecture / Specification
A Human Approval Gate intercepts proposals produced by probabilistic agent runs and pauses execution via [Durable Wait](./durable-wait.md) until a valid approval token is recorded.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

### Distinction from Hard Constraints
Within the AAIF workflow taxonomy, Human Approval Gates represent confidence-driven checkpoints established because an agent system is not yet fully trusted to operate autonomously.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42] As empirical reliability metrics meet target thresholds, approval gates may transition through [Autonomy Graduation](./autonomy-graduation.md) into exception-based escalation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

In contrast, requirements rooted in statutory mandates, legal certifications, or enterprise policy are modeled as [Hard Constraint Gate](./hard-constraint-gate.md) patterns, which are non-negotiable and cannot be relaxed through autonomy graduation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

# Lifecycle History
Updated to reflect the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group classification schema distinguishing transitional approval gates from permanent hard constraints.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group establishes standardized execution models, capability boundaries, interface contracts, and architectural patterns for integrating AI agents into business workflows and software processes.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29] The group standardizes the compositional primitives and topologies governing deterministic control over probabilistic agents.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across multiple core workstreams:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]
- **Primitive Vocabulary (P1–P19)**: Foundational building blocks (including Trigger, AgentStep, Budget, and Handoff) used to construct single- and multi-agent execution graphs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]
- **Reference Architectures**: Standardized drafts for Single-Agent and Multi-Agent workflow execution.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]
- **Boundary Contracts**: Interface specifications (such as the AgentStep boundary contract and Handoff contract) that primitive-crossing steps must satisfy.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]
- **Topologies (T1–T6)**: Structural multi-agent interaction shapes routing multi-agent coordination.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]
- **Shared Guidance**: Factored evaluation criteria covering verification checklists, execution loop tiers, anti-patterns, and cross-working-group boundaries.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]

# Lifecycle History
Expanded technical assets to include primitive vocabularies, topology classifications, and formal step-boundary contracts.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging open specifications, capability maps, delegation validity, and protocol interfaces for agent-mediated economic transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group develops vendor-neutral capability maps, interoperability profiles, and reference architectures for autonomous and semi-autonomous commercial transactions conducted by AI agents.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]

# Architecture / Specification
The group's capability mapping evaluates protocols across transaction lifecycle requirements, addressing specific multi-layer compliance and execution dimensions:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]
- **Buyer Capacity and Verification**: Standardizing representations for legal capacity, age verification, and delegated authority to prevent void or voidable delegations across differing jurisdictions.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]
- **Multi-Layer Record Retention**: Specifying data retention obligations across three regulatory tiers:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]
  - *AI Regulatory Layer*: High-risk AI system record-keeping rules (e.g., EU AI Act Articles 19 and 26(6) 6-month retention).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]
  - *Data Protection Layer*: Storage limitation ceilings under GDPR and related privacy frameworks.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]
  - *Financial and AML Layer*: Statutory transaction log durations under anti-money-laundering directives, the US Bank Secrecy Act (5-year periods), and payment rules such as Regulation E (2-year periods).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]

# Lifecycle History
Active discussions ongoing regarding protocol capability evaluation criteria for autonomous agent checkouts and multi-party retention responsibilities.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]

proposed_concept.title: Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group bridging global AI policy instruments with technical specifications through landscape mapping, 16-theme gap analysis, and regulatory alignment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group on Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment (WG GRR) bridges global AI policy instruments with technical specifications for agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319] Co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group translates regional compliance frameworks, risk controls, and regulatory requirements into actionable engineering guidance and reference architectures.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group established a baseline of 16 core themes against which comparative and gap analyses across regional AI regulatory instruments are evaluated:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]
- **Governance & accountability**: Ownership, approvals, RACI matrices, and risk acceptance.
- **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Allowed vs. prohibited uses and tiered controls.
- **Architecture**: Reference patterns, trust boundaries, and control placement.
- **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication/authorization models, acting-on-behalf-of semantics, and registries.
- **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Business rules, policy-as-code, and hard constraints.
- **Data protection & privacy**: PII handling, data minimization, retention schedules, and residency.
- **Security & access controls**: Least privilege, secrets management, network segmentation, and tool permissions.
- **Model/agent risk management**: Model validation, robustness benchmarks, drift monitoring, and change control.
- **Human oversight**: Human-in-the-loop (HITL), human-on-the-loop (HOTL), escalation paths, and automated overrides/kill switches.
- **Action management**: Pre-execution verification checks, dual control, and reversibility.
- **Monitoring & logging**: Audit trails, prompt/tool invocation logs, and decision logs.
- **Testing & red teaming**: Prompt injection defense, tool abuse mitigations, and autonomy failure modes.
- **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence and model/tool provenance.
- **Incident response**: Detection, containment, and reporting protocols.
- **Transparency & user disclosure**: Notices, automated explanations, and user expectation setting.
- **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Retention schedules and deterministic reproducibility.

The group utilizes standardized "golden source" extraction prompts to ensure uniform, objective analysis across geographic jurisdictions.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

proposed_concept.description: Unified gateway and registry control plane for centralizing discovery, enterprise authentication, tool-level authorization, and A2A federation for MCP servers and agent skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
MCP Gateway & Registry is an open-source unified platform and control plane that centralizes access to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, AI agents, and reusable agent skills.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29] It addresses tool sprawl, credential isolation, and audit visibility across enterprise coding assistants and autonomous multi-agent environments.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]

# Architecture / Specification
The platform operates across four primary functional areas:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]
- **Unified MCP Server Gateway**: Proxies traffic to registered MCP servers, providing dynamic semantic tool discovery, tool aggregation into virtual MCP servers, and method-level access controls.
- **MCP Servers Registry**: Implements the Anthropic MCP Registry REST API v0.1 specification, enabling standards-compliant client discovery, server cataloging, and automated security scanning.
- **Agent Registry and A2A Communication Hub**: Hosts signed `../projects/a2a.md` agent cards for authenticated agent discovery, enabling direct peer-to-peer communication without proxying wire traffic.
- **Agent Skills Registry**: Maintains a governed catalog of reusable agent skills with per-skill credential isolation and security scanning.

Federation features include peer-to-peer registry federation, upstream imports from Anthropic MCP Registry, and federation with AWS Agent Registry / Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29] Enterprise identity support spans Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Auth0, and Amazon Cognito.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]

# Lifecycle History
- Submitted as an AAIF project proposal via issue #29 under Apache 2.0 licensing.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a shared telemetry and trace specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group (`../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`). It establishes standardized schemas and relationship semantics for capturing multi-turn agent conversations, runtime sessions, execution steps, tool calls, and human approvals.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model specifies structured relationship graphs across agent execution lifecycles:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Session and Turn Graphs**: Links root agent conversations to execution turns, sub-agent delegations, and tool boundaries.
- **Tool and CLI Observability**: Integrates with `../reference-architectures/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md` for tool dispatches, receipts, and execution states.
- **Relationship Conformance Test Kit**: Standardized check suites verify telemetry resilience against out-of-order, repeated, or lost events (e.g., verifying that duplicate receipt delivery retains single-ticket confirmations, while dropped receipts yield unconfirmed states).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Evidence Integrity**: Telemetry payloads map to verification vantages and evidence models in `../reference-architectures/evidence-record-spec.md`.

proposed_concept.title: Proposal-Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern separating probabilistic agent intent generation, deterministic authorization, and separate write-scoped execution into distinct permission boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal-Execution Split is a workflow architecture pattern that divides agentic automation into distinct stages: read-only intent generation, deterministic validation, and separate write-scoped execution.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51] By isolating analysis from privileged side effects via job-level permissions rather than dynamic runtime gates, systems prevent untrusted context from directly modifying infrastructure or repositories.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern isolates privileges across distinct pipeline stages:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
1. **Analysis and Proposal Phase**: The agent executes within an isolated, read-only job with restricted tool grants (e.g., read, grep, glob without shell, network, or write access) to inspect untrusted inputs or upstream releases.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
2. **Deterministic Validation Gate**: Intermediate artifacts are scanned deterministically (such as credential leak detection or schema compliance) before handoff to downstream jobs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
3. **Privileged Write Execution**: Authorized output artifacts are handed off to a separate, write-scoped runner or human operator to apply modifications.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

Unlike dynamic convergence loops (`../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md`) that iterate until acceptance, sequential proposal-execution splits enforce hard boundaries at the environment level without requiring continuous approval loops.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

# References
- `../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md`
- `../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md`
- `../policies-guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md`

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, review checklists, and security best practices for agentic AI architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an [Agentic AI Foundation](../governance/technical-committee.md) technical body charged with identifying threat surfaces, cataloging defense-in-depth patterns, and authoring baseline security guidelines for autonomous agents, protocol gateways, and multi-agent execution environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]. It coordinates cross-cutting security reviews across AAIF working groups and interfaces with external standards efforts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Active Deliverables and Workstreams

- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive security baseline authored to address code smells, credential isolation, and least-privilege token boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Threat Modeling and Gap Analysis**: Framework for analyzing attack vectors across agent runtime environments, tool dispatch layers, and egress communication channels [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Review instrument evaluating security and privacy considerations across peer working groups, including [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural patterns cataloging secure isolation mechanisms such as [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and microVM sandboxing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Active maintenance of security definitions using LLM provenance-tracking review tooling [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# External Coordination

The working group collaborates with external standards bodies including ETSI TC SAI on European cybersecurity norms for AI agents, OWASP on agent security standards, and FINOS Labs on enterprise governance architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing multi-layer telemetry standards, cross-boundary context propagation, prior-work landscape surveys, and agent observability use cases.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is the [Agentic AI Foundation](../governance/technical-committee.md) body chartered to survey, coordinate, and standardize agent observability and tracing architectures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra, the working group standardizes telemetry conventions across agent frameworks, multi-agent protocol boundaries, and infrastructure layers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# Core Specifications and Living Documents

- **Prior Work Landscape Survey**: Comprehensive survey tracking telemetry initiatives including OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions, [Agent Trace](../reference-architectures/agent-trace.md), OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS), AGNTCY Observe, OCSF v1.9 AI Operations, and [A2A](../projects/a2a.md) traceability extensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Agent Observability Use Cases**: Standardized catalog spanning root-cause debugging, cost optimization, AI code attribution, multi-agent protocol tracing, cross-surface identity resolution (I1), and tamper-evident audit evidence (E4) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability Framework**: Architecture enabling context propagation across protocol boundaries such as MCP, A2A, and agent gateway proxies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# Telemetry Requirements

The working group defines cross-cutting telemetry requirements requiring clear differentiation between agent self-reporting and trusted vantage points (host OS, eBPF, network, sandbox), verifiable sampling and completeness declarations, schema versioning, and causal correlation across asynchronous sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

mutations.rationale: Update the security best practices guideline concept to reflect its authoring status, static analysis alignment, and review intake rules.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Security guidance detailing threat models, least-privilege token boundaries, action pinning, kill switches, and static code smell mitigations for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes standard security baselines for organizations deploying autonomous AI agents, tool runtimes, and multi-agent coordination topologies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. Developed within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document synthesizes threat analysis, common implementation anti-patterns, and static analysis code smells [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Core Principles

- **Least-Privilege Token Boundaries**: Scoping credentials and capability tokens to the narrowest viable API surfaces and action permissions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
- **Sandbox Isolation**: Confining agent execution and tool execution environments to hardened microVM or hardware-isolated runtimes to prevent host compromise and unconstrained egress [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Static Code Smell Mitigation**: Identifying and eliminating common anti-patterns in agent prompts, tool invocations, and parameter passing that invite prompt injection or privilege escalation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
- **Deterministic Gates and Kill Switches**: Enforcing deterministic authorization checks before high-impact tool dispatches, alongside immediate kill switch mechanisms [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Lifecycle History

Initial drafting began in August 2026 under the Security and Privacy Working Group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. Following extensive community feedback, subsequent revisions are tracked via tracked GitHub issues and standard PR review windows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

proposed_concept.title: Core Workflow Terms
proposed_concept.description: Foundational vocabulary for agentic workflows defining activities as primary units of execution and workflows as activity compositions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Core Workflow Terms establish a shared, standardized vocabulary for specifying agentic AI workflows, defining the discrete units of execution, lifecycle states, and orchestration structures across AAIF reference architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Voted through at the August 2026 plenary by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this Phase One taxonomy represents the foundation's first formalized vocabulary artifact [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Architecture / Specification

### Primary Terms
- **Activity**: The foundational unit of work within an agentic workflow, defined independently without circular references to workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. The working group formally adopted "activity" over alternative terms like "step" or "workflow step" to decouple atomic execution units from broader orchestration topologies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Workflow**: A structured composition of activities executed in sequence, parallel, or cyclic iterations according to deterministic or agent-driven policies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Lifecycle**: The progression of state transitions managing execution, replacing prior ambiguous references to "execution engine" [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

### Scope Boundaries
To prevent conceptual overlap, gate, check, and evaluation terminology is explicitly scoped out of the core workflow terms and assigned to the Security & Privacy, Observability & Traceability, and Accuracy & Reliability working groups [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the Phase One Core Terms draft was reviewed and formally voted through by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Ongoing reconciliation continues with upstream global taxonomy workstreams to align agentic AI specific terminology with baseline definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared workflow execution models, activity schemas, reference architectures, and validation guides.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group defines vendor-neutral standards, execution topologies, and reference architectures for agentic AI workflow orchestration [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group focuses on bridging business processes, human-in-the-loop controls, and autonomous agent loops into composable patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its deliverables across three primary workstreams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]:
- **Taxonomy**: Curates foundational execution terminology, having shipped the Phase One [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md) defining activities and workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Reference Architectures**: Standardizes workflow patterns including human-approved operations and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../reference-architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md), employing a 4-outcome validation method (validated, partial, candidate, no fit) against real-world use cases [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Evaluates inventory use cases across three priority cohorts: human-approved operations, bounded autonomous remediation, and exception detection and escalation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group shipped the Phase One Core Terms taxonomy as the first delivered artifact across the foundation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Deliverable scope was locked to two reference architectures, core taxonomy, architecture principles, and a contributing guide [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared trace identity and relationship contract defining agent conversation, session, turn, execution, and effect interpretation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model defines a shared identity and relationship contract for instrumenting, exporting, and interpreting agentic AI telemetry across heterogeneous runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. Managed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the specification standardizes how external consumers reconstruct proposals, observed executions, and independently reported effects without relying on proprietary runtime internals [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Architecture / Specification

### Independent Interpretation Verification
To validate interoperability, trace exports must be independently interpretable by external query engines and consumers under varying arrival conditions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]:
- **Zero Private Runtime State**: Readers must reconstruct execution status strictly from standardized trace records without access to private session state, fixtures, or shared reconstruction code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Out-of-Order Resiliency**: Readers must produce identical semantic interpretations (identifying approved proposals, observed executions, and external effects) regardless of event arrival order [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Degraded and Conflicting Evidence Handling**: In the absence of corroborating evidence (e.g. missing service receipts), readers must deterministically flag external effects as unconfirmed rather than silently succeeding or failing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History

The trace model is tracked under a multi-task execution plan by the Observability and Traceability Working Group, incorporating multi-reader compliance benchmarks to verify cross-agent export consistency [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.title: OpenSandbox
proposed_concept.description: Open-source general-purpose sandbox platform providing unified lifecycle and execution APIs for isolated AI agent workloads.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
OpenSandbox is an open-source, general-purpose sandbox platform designed for safely running AI-generated code, coding agents, browser automation, and reinforcement learning workloads[^evt-project-proposals-issue-26]. Proposed for AAIF hosting, OpenSandbox provides a vendor-neutral isolation substrate across container and microVM execution layers[^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].

# Architecture / Specification
The platform is organized as a unified control plane and execution daemon architecture supported by multi-language SDKs and tooling[^evt-project-proposals-issue-26]:
- **Sandbox Lifecycle APIs**: Standardizes remote management interfaces for provisioning, inspecting, renewing, pausing, snapshotting, and terminating sandbox environments[^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].
- **In-Sandbox Execution Daemon**: Exposes execution endpoints for shell commands, code execution, filesystem manipulation, and streaming telemetry[^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].
- **Network & Runtime Isolation**: Implements granular per-sandbox ingress and egress network filtering alongside support for Docker, Kubernetes, and hardened runtimes such as gVisor, Kata Containers, and Firecracker microVMs[^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].
- **MCP Integration**: Ships with `opensandbox-mcp`, allowing Model Context Protocol clients to create sandboxes and execute operations through standard tool calls[^evt-project-proposals-issue-26].

Related concepts: `../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md`, `../reference-architectures/goose.md`, `../projects/mcp-gateway-registry.md`.

# References
- [OpenSandbox AAIF Proposal](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/26)

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey instrument gathering empirical data on real-world AI agent deployments and reliability priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) survey is a platform-neutral 16-question instrument designed to collect empirical data on production AI agent deployments, operational hurdles, failure modes, and recovery priorities[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The survey is organized into five structured sections with explicit branching and validation rules[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]:
- **Eligibility (Q1)**: Screens respondents based on active deployment or evaluation of agentic AI systems, directing non-qualifying respondents to a dedicated exit page[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **About the System (Q2–Q5)**: Gathers information on agent system architecture, frameworks, and operational domains (Q5 is optional; Q2 includes structured write-in fields)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Benefits and Challenges (Q6–Q8)**: Measures observed operational advantages and integration barriers using standardized five-choice response matrices[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Accuracy and Reliability (Q9–Q13)**: Identifies verification patterns, failure categories, automated recovery behavior, and evaluation tooling[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16)**: Surveys community demand for benchmark standards, reference architectures, and open feedback (Q16 is optional)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

Related concepts: `../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md`, `../policies-guidelines/ra-use-case-validation-guide.md`.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared trace identity and portable telemetry context preserving causal execution relationships across agents, SDKs, and gateways.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry framework establishing canonical identity, causal linking, and execution context across heterogeneous AI agents, SDKs, tool gateways, and observability collectors[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Designed to complement OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions, the model defines portable context representations that link planning decisions to downstream execution outcomes without exposing raw chain-of-thought traces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification
The model defines standard attribute propagation and correlation across multi-tier agent interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]:
- **Portable Telemetry Context**: Maintains session lineage, turn identifiers, and causal execution graphs across distributed runtime and gateway hops[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Cross-Boundary Mappings**: Provides structured metadata mappings for agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool dispatches[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **ARD Trust Pipeline Tracing**: Captures verification spans across Agent Resource Discovery (ARD), identity attestation, and authorization decision checkpoints[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Standard Alignment**: Operates under an adopt/extend/new specification framework evaluated against OpenTelemetry, W3C Trace Context, and related observability specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

Related concepts: `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`, `../reference-architectures/opentelemetry.md`, `../reference-architectures/evidence-record-spec.md`.

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, review checklists, and security best practices for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group is an AAIF body tasked with establishing threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, cross-working-group review checklists, and security best practices across agentic AI ecosystems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-938e481e]. Co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group operates several active workstreams addressing threat modeling, practical security guidelines, and design patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its deliverables across multiple targeted workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Evaluates existing frameworks including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF against agentic paradigms, incorporating STRIDE, PASTA, and Human-User-Agent (HUA) considerations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Develops actionable configuration and operational guidance, integrating identity boundaries and runtime controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f] (see also [../policies-guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md](../policies-guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)).
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Establishes reusable architectural patterns and templates for hardened agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Provides an overlap and security review checklist bridging deliverables across other AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Taxonomy & Landscape Coordination**: Coordinates domain-specific security and privacy terminology with the cross-cutting workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f] (see [../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)).

# Lifecycle History

Formed in mid-2026, the working group stood up five primary workstreams in June 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-938e481e]. In July 2026, initial drafts of the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Best Practices Guide were published as pull requests [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-938e481e]. In August 2026, the working group resolved to make meeting recordings public by default and sought Technical Committee guidance regarding the integration of protocol-level security efforts such as [../projects/a2a.md](../projects/a2a.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate July 2026 progress report detailing workstreams for reference architectures, critical use cases, execution profiles, and taxonomy alignment.

proposed_concept.title: Workflows & Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared workflow execution models, activity schemas, reference architectures, and design flow specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows & Process Integration Working Group defines standardized execution models, workflow patterns, and integration architectures connecting AI agent activities with enterprise process infrastructure [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. Co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group focuses on creating formal reference architectures, cataloging critical enterprise use cases, and establishing shared operational vocabularies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group drives three primary technical workstreams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]:
- **Reference Architectures**: Defines a spectrum of 7 execution profiles (ranging from fully deterministic Profile 1 to fully agentic Profile 7) underpinned by a "least agentic default" principle [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. Implements a specification-driven design flow compiling use-case definitions into machine-readable YAML specifications and architecture documentation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Evaluates and categorizes extensive production use cases against core execution primitives (triggers, human-in-the-loop gates, coordination models, and agent counts), standardizing on fewer than ten reusable workflow patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26] (see [../resources/agentic-workflow-patterns-comparison.md](../resources/agentic-workflow-patterns-comparison.md)).
- **Taxonomy**: Coordinates cross-group workflow terminology (such as core terms in [../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md)) in alignment with the broader [../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) effort [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Lifecycle History

During July 2026, the working group validated its specification-driven design flow on invoice processing and autonomous maintenance use cases [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The group converged its catalog of 89 use cases into a shortlist of reusable patterns (including bounded convergence loops) while establishing cross-workstream alignment between reference architecture primitives and taxonomy short codes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

mutations.rationale: Clarify evidence grade designations and document jurisdiction/legal-weight requirements from WG Observability and Traceability PR #56.

proposed_concept.title: Evidence Record Specification
proposed_concept.description: Testable JSON Schema and data model encoding observation sources, verification vantages, integrity grades, and jurisdiction requirements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Evidence Record Specification defines an interoperable telemetry and verifiable audit schema capturing execution evidence, agent-generated actions, and causal proof chains across agentic systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]. Curated under [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it establishes unambiguous structures for integrity verification, non-repudiation, and cross-boundary evidentiary exchange [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

# Architecture / Specification

The specification standardizes structured verification layers and telemetry invariants [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]:
- **Evidence-Grade Ladder**: Categorizes record integrity through explicit evidence grades (such as Grade E1 through Grade E4) to avoid naming collisions with specific functional use-case identifiers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].
- **Jurisdiction and Legal Weight Separation**: Enforces a strict separation between a record's technical integrity mechanism (such as RFC 3161 cryptographic timestamping) and its legal weight [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]. Where records satisfy regulatory retention or evidentiary duties (e.g., EU AI Act provider recording obligations under Article 12, or retention under Articles 19 and 26(6)), the schema mandates explicit declaration of the governing jurisdiction and legal role of the record holder rather than hardcoding a single legal system into schema enumerations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].
- **Vantage Point & Identity Attestation**: Bridges cryptographic attestation with verifiable identities (such as [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)) and isolated runtimes (see [../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)).

# Lifecycle History

In working group drafts, qualifying revisions were made to clearly separate the lettered evidence grades from document use-case identifiers and to disclaim standalone legal claims from technical RFC 3161 timestamps [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate proposals for expanding landscape categories to include third-party verifiable attestation and provenance tools.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive CNCF Landscape2 market map and project directory cataloging runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, observability stacks, and attestation systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape provides an interactive, structured overview of open-source and member-driven projects, protocols, runtimes, and tooling across the agent ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44]. Maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), it organizes technologies across core functional layers to ensure architectural clarity and discoverability.

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is structured into defined categories and subcategories that reflect the lifecycle and operational boundaries of AI agents [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44]:

- **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Preventative boundary controls, policy enforcement points, and prompt safety filters operating before execution.
- **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Runtime monitoring, tracing, metrics collection, and evaluation telemetry capturing execution paths while and after actions occur [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].
- **Attestation & Verifiable Evidence**: Mechanisms and standards providing third-party verifiable proof without requiring total trust in the execution operator [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44]. Subcategories include:
  - *Attestation Standards & Verification*: Hardware and enclave verification frameworks including IETF RATS, Veraison, and Keylime [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].
  - *Transparency & Provenance*: Supply chain and transparency ledgers including IETF SCITT, in-toto, Sigstore, and SLSA [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].
  - *Agent Action & Runtime Evidence*: Signed execution proof and action capsules such as Agent Action Capsule, TRACE, and Agent Manifest [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed additions to the landscape schema require cross-working-group review, notably spanning [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) working groups prior to final inclusion [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].
