proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating shared SKOS-Lite agentic AI vocabularies and ecosystem market maps.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream establishes vendor-neutral terminology, ontology mappings, and ecosystem landscape visualizations across the Agentic AI Foundation. It provides the structured foundation used by working groups to define interoperability boundaries, skill signatures, and evaluation criteria.

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream maintains both the agentic terminology taxonomy and the landscape data repository [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44]:

- **Taxonomy Data Store & Validation**: The taxonomy terms are stored in structured JSON (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`) and validated in CI using Zod schemas [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79]. This structure replaces custom JavaScript parsing logic, ensuring field-level error reporting, safe ingestion of contributions, and consistent serialization across web explorers and consumers [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].
- **Landscape Mapping**: Landscape definitions are maintained as structured YAML and rendered via the CNCF Landscape2 engine, classifying ecosystem projects under standardized member and external taxonomies [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-44].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream continuously coordinates terminology additions with domain working groups, including the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), ensuring domain-specific terms conform to foundation-wide schema standards [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

mutations.rationale: Defines standardized agentic commerce taxonomy terms covering transaction autonomy levels, checkout interactions, delegated payments, and commerce protocols.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Terms
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary defining transaction autonomy levels, checkout interactions, delegated payment models, and commerce protocols.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce taxonomy defines standardized terms for AI agent interactions across purchasing, transactions, payment delegation, and commerce protocol exchanges. Maintained in coordination with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) and the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), these terms establish clear boundaries between human oversight levels and autonomous agent execution in financial interactions.

# Architecture / Specification

The agentic commerce domain categorizes interactions into transaction autonomy tiers, execution checkpoints, payment mechanisms, and protocol layers:

## Transaction Classifications

- **Agent-Completed Transaction**: An end-to-end commerce transaction where an AI agent executes discovery, negotiation, checkout, and settlement fulfillment autonomously without inline human intervention during execution [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70].
- **Agent-in-the-Loop Transaction**: A commerce transaction where an AI agent assists, mediates, or executes specific stages of the transaction lifecycle while maintaining human oversight or interactive verification gates (renamed from *Agent-mediated transaction*) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71].
- **Agent-Initiated Transaction**: A commerce transaction triggered autonomously or programmatically by an AI agent based on predefined criteria, environmental triggers, or delegated objectives, regardless of whether downstream fulfillment requires human approval [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72].

## Checkout and Payment Mechanisms

- **Agentic Checkout**: The automated or assisted workflow through which an AI agent traverses merchant interfaces, cart evaluations, shipping configurations, and payment authorizations to finalize a purchase on behalf of a principal [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-73].
- **Delegated Payment**: A payment execution pattern wherein an authorized agent is granted scoped financial authority (such as spending limits, merchant constraints, or time-bounded credentials) to transact funds on behalf of a human principal or corporate entity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-76].

## Protocol Infrastructure

- **Agentic Commerce Protocols**: Standardized communication specifications, interchange schemas, and interaction flows governing how autonomous agents discover merchants, negotiate terms, transmit cart payloads, and process transactions interoperably across distributed commerce ecosystems [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-75].

# Lifecycle History

- PR#70 introduced definitions for *Agent-completed transaction* [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70].
- PR#71 introduced *Agent-in-the-loop transaction*, renaming the prior draft term *Agent-mediated transaction* based on working group consensus [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71].
- PR#72 introduced definitions for *Agent-initiated transaction* [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72].
- PR#73 introduced definitions for *Agentic checkout* [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-73].
- PR#75 defined *Agentic commerce protocols*, pluralizing and formalizing the protocol classification [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-75].
- PR#76 introduced definitions for *Delegated payment* [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-76].

mutations.rationale: Add OpenEnv as a proposed AAIF hosted project providing a standardized execution environment framework and container specification for agentic reinforcement learning.

proposed_concept.title: OpenEnv
proposed_concept.description: Unified open-source framework and container packaging specification for agentic reinforcement learning execution environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
OpenEnv is an open-source framework for building, packaging, deploying, and interacting with isolated execution environments for agentic reinforcement learning (RL)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]. It provides Gymnasium-style lifecycle APIs (`reset`, `step`, `state`) and standardizes the model-to-environment boundary using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to ensure consistency between agent training, evaluation, and production deployment[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].

# Architecture / Specification
OpenEnv standardizes agent RL environments as containerized units published to hubs and executed across trainers, harnesses, and sandboxes[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]:
- **Model-to-Environment Protocol**: Uses MCP (built on `fastmcp`) as the communication interface so environments expose tools identical to production runtime surfaces[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
- **RL Lifecycle Interface**: Exposes standardized step, reset, reward, rubric, and state inspection operations[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
- **Harness & Sandbox Support**: Integrates with agent harnesses such as Goose ([`../reference-architectures/goose.md`](../reference-architectures/goose.md)) via RFC 005 wrapping patterns, alongside execution sandboxes like Modal, Daytona, and Azure Container Apps[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
- **Trainer Compatibility**: Compatible with RL post-training frameworks and inference engines including TRL, Unsloth, SkyRL, Axolotl, Lightning AI, vLLM, and SGLang[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].

# Lifecycle History
- **October 2025**: Launched as a joint initiative between Hugging Face and Meta (Meta-PyTorch) at the PyTorch Conference[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
- **June 2026**: Transitioned repository to `huggingface/OpenEnv` under a multi-company Technical Committee spanning Meta, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Hugging Face, Modal, and others[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
- **September 2026**: Proposed for AAIF hosted project status under the sponsorship of Caitie McCaffrey (Microsoft)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].

mutations.rationale: Add ContextForge as a proposed AAIF hosted project federating MCP, A2A, and REST/gRPC interfaces under a central gateway and registry control plane.

proposed_concept.title: ContextForge
proposed_concept.description: Open-source registry and gateway federating MCP, A2A, and REST/gRPC interfaces with centralized governance, discovery, and observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
ContextForge is an open-source registry and proxy control plane that federates Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and REST/gRPC endpoints under centralized discovery, governance, and observability controls[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]. It provides extensible infrastructure enabling developers and enterprise operators to manage tool calling, reference implementations, and access policies across heterogeneous AI agent ecosystems[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].

# Architecture / Specification
ContextForge is built with a plugin-driven extensible architecture designed to operate across developer workstations and production clusters[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]:
- **Protocol Federation**: Bridges MCP servers, A2A agents ([`../projects/a2a.md`](../projects/a2a.md)), and traditional REST/gRPC APIs into a unified registry and discovery surface[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].
- **Extensible Plugin Model**: Supports over 40 modular plugins extending transports, identity, security boundaries, and telemetry integrations without modifying core runtime logic[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].
- **Governance & Policy Plane**: Integrates centralized authentication, authorization, token-level access controls, and runtime monitoring to enforce enterprise guardrails alongside projects such as MCP Gateway and Registry ([`../projects/mcp-gateway-registry.md`](../projects/mcp-gateway-registry.md))[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].

# Lifecycle History
- **2025–Early 2026**: Developed at IBM Consulting by Mihai Creviti to standardize MCP proxying and registry capabilities[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].
- **July 2026**: Reached over 4,100 GitHub stars and 2.6 million downloads; submitted as an AAIF hosted project proposal transitioning from IBM stewardship to open foundation governance[^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].

mutations.rationale: Create taxonomy concept defining foundational universal terms including Subagent, Agent swarm, and Context.

proposed_concept.title: Universal Agent Taxonomy Terms
proposed_concept.description: Standardized universal vocabulary defining subagents, agent swarms, and context boundaries within agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Universal Agent Taxonomy defines foundational, domain-neutral terms established by the Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream ([`../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)) to standardize agentic AI concepts across AAIF working groups and specifications[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-80][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82].

# Architecture / Specification
Universal terms provide unambiguous semantic baselines for architecture specifications and runtime protocols:
- **Subagent**: An agent spawned by an existing agent[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68]. Subagent status describes structural lineage only; properties such as identity, authentication, execution environment, access rights, and permissions are not implied by subagent status and must be explicitly specified[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68].
- **Agent Swarm**: A group of subagents working cooperatively or independently toward a task or shared objective[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-80]. Swarm size and temporal lifecycle (transient vs. persistent) are unspecified, and coordination is commonly managed by an orchestrator agent[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-80].
- **Context**: The collective information available to an agent when making a decision[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82]. Context encompasses user messages, tool results, retrieved documents, memory records, and system instructions assembled for the active execution step, linking to operations such as context assembly, retrieval, propagation, and memory access[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #68**: Merged universal taxonomy term *Subagent* and related scope notes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68].
- **PR #80**: Proposed universal term *Agent swarm* with links to Subagent and Orchestrator concepts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-80].
- **PR #82**: Proposed universal term *Context* and associated scope notes spanning context assembly, exhaustion, and propagation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82].

mutations.rationale: Update taxonomy workstream concept with contribution process guidelines, review outcomes, and recent universal vocabulary definitions.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating shared SKOS-Lite agentic AI vocabularies, contribution workflows, and ecosystem market maps.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative responsible for maintaining the foundational SKOS-Lite vocabulary of agentic AI terminology, coordinating term contributions across Working Groups, and maintaining the interactive ecosystem market map ([`../ecosystem/agentic-ai-landscape.md`](../ecosystem/agentic-ai-landscape.md))[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates a structured terminology curation process to maintain conceptual integrity across AAIF domains[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83]:
- **Contribution Pipeline**: Working groups propose domain-specific terms via assigned delegates who submit proposals into the taxonomy repository for schema validation and cross-WG review[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83].
- **Review Outcomes**: Proposed terms undergo triage resulting in `KEEP` (accepted into taxonomy), `CULL` (rejected or consolidated), or `DEBATE` (referred for technical deliberation)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83].
- **Universal Vocabularies**: Curates cross-domain baseline terms including Subagents, Agent Swarms, and Context ([`../taxonomy/universal-agent-terms.md`](../taxonomy/universal-agent-terms.md)) alongside domain-specific sets such as core workflow terms ([`../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md`](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md)) and commerce terms ([`../taxonomy/agentic-commerce-terms.md`](../taxonomy/agentic-commerce-terms.md))[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-80][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-82].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #68**: Merged universal term *Subagent* into taxonomy data definitions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68].
- **PR #83**: Clarified end-to-end contribution workflow, review outcome taxonomy (`KEEP`/`CULL`/`DEBATE`), and delegate governance rules[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83].

mutations.rationale: Record the Open Responses project proposal submitted to the AAIF for hosting a vendor-neutral model-inference specification and conformance suite.

proposed_concept.title: Open Responses
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral specification and conformance test suite for model APIs standardizing requests, output items, tool calls, and streaming events.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Open Responses is a vendor-neutral specification and conformance project for language-model inference APIs, derived from the OpenAI Responses API design[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]. It provides model providers, inference gateways, client SDKs, and agent frameworks with a standardized representation for prompt requests, multimodal output items, tool calls, and streaming lifecycle events[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

Within the Agentic AI Foundation stack, Open Responses operates at the model-inference layer, complementing runtime agent frameworks like [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md) and communication protocols such as [A2A](../projects/a2a.md)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification and its accompanying test suite establish consistent semantics across model backends while maintaining explicit extension points[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]:
- **Standardized Payloads**: Common schemas for model requests, responses, tool calls, and structured streaming events[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].
- **Transport and Lifecycle**: Support for HTTP/REST and WebSocket transports, along with context compaction capabilities[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].
- **Acceptance and Conformance**: Browser-based and command-line test suites validating provider compliance against date-versioned OpenAPI definitions[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].
- **Ecosystem Integration**: Designed to integrate with routing gateways and client SDKs without proprietary vendor lock-in[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

# Lifecycle History
The proposal was submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) under the [Project Proposal Process](../governance/project-proposal-process.md) sponsored by OpenAI[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]. The project operates under an Apache-2.0 license for code and CC-BY-4.0 for specifications with an open Technical Steering Committee (TSC) governance model[^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

mutations.rationale: Add proposed vocabulary covering tool poisoning, rug pulls, verification, and data leakage across agent tool supply chains.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Tool Supply Chain Terms
proposed_concept.description: Standardized security vocabulary defining tool poisoning, rug pulls, manifest verification, and cross-client leakage in agent tool supply chains.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent tool supply chain terms define attack vectors, integrity checks, and data exposure risks specific to agent tool definitions and shared execution runtimes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].

The taxonomy is curated across the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), and [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].

# Architecture / Specification
The supply chain terms define distinct operational and threat concepts:
- **Tool Poisoning**: A pre-deployment attack where a tool definition or implementation is maliciously crafted prior to adoption to manipulate agent reasoning or hijack executions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].
- **Rug Pull**: A post-approval attack where a previously trusted or verified tool definition is altered after deployment to introduce malicious capabilities or alter behavior[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].
- **Tool Definition Verification**: The deterministic process of validating tool manifests, schemas, and cryptographic signatures prior to agent invocation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].
- **Cross-Client Data Leakage**: The unauthorized exposure or sharing of state, session context, or tool output between distinct client sessions on a shared tool server[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed under [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) PR #88 in alignment with MITRE ATLAS and OWASP security classifications[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88].

mutations.rationale: Update universal agent taxonomy to incorporate agent-to-agent coordination definitions proposed in PR #81.

proposed_concept.title: Universal Agent Terms
proposed_concept.description: Standardized universal vocabulary defining subagents, agent swarms, context boundaries, and agent-to-agent coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The universal agent vocabulary standardizes core architectural terms across multi-agent systems, interaction models, and execution boundaries within the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-81].

# Architecture / Specification
The vocabulary defines universal terms for agent architectures and system boundaries:
- **Agent-to-agent (A2A interaction)**: A general interaction pattern where an agent communicates, delegates tasks, or coordinates with another autonomous agent, distinct from specific wire protocols or hosted implementations like [A2A](../projects/a2a.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-81].
- **Subagents**: Specialized secondary agents spawned or invoked by a primary supervisor agent to execute bounded sub-tasks within a constrained scope.
- **Agent Swarms**: Decentralized collectives of peer agents executing collaborative problem-solving without a single central orchestrator.
- **Context Boundaries**: Logical and cryptographic perimeters isolating memory, tool permissions, and state across disparate agent roles.

# Lifecycle History
Terms are maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) in coordination with cross-cutting working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-81].

mutations.rationale: Captures the Kill Switch pattern from WG-Security and Privacy establishing an independent runtime control plane for containment, halting, and token revocation.

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch Pattern
proposed_concept.description: An independent out-of-band runtime control plane that halts agent execution, revokes active credentials, and triggers containment loops outside model context.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Kill Switch pattern defines an independent, out-of-band runtime control plane capable of immediately halting an AI agent's execution, severing network communications, and invalidating session credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]. By decoupling containment controls entirely from agent prompt context, memory, and reasoning loops, it prevents model evasion, stops recursive runaway loops, and cleans up asynchronous orphan tasks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern establishes a containment loop composed of three discrete stages: detection, halting, and rollback [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]:

- **Containment Plane Independence:** Policy criteria defining *when* an agent halts are decoupled from the technical control plane that *executes* the halt, ensuring enforcement occurs server-side outside model reach [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].
- **Token and Network Invalidation:** Halting invalidates active API keys, ephemeral OAuth sessions, and network ingress/egress rather than merely terminating host processes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].
- **Orphan Task Cleanup:** Active asynchronous child tasks and spawned background routines are explicitly tracked and terminated to prevent unmonitored zombie executions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].
- **Reversibility and Rollback:** Uses execution journals to trigger compensating transactions or rollback actions for external state modifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].

# References

- Maintained within the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) Design Patterns Catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50].
- Complements hardware isolation in [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and dispatch binding in [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].

proposed_concept.title: Approval Checkpoint Pattern
proposed_concept.description: Runtime governance pattern binding approvals to exact executed actions and separately maintaining decision, execution, and confirmed service effect records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Approval Checkpoint pattern binds a human or policy approval directly to the exact action that executes, constraining its validity interval and usage count while strictly separating the approval decision from execution attempts and confirmed target effects [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]. This prevents common failure modes such as approval reuse, action alteration post-approval, and treating unverified approvals as proof of execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern structures runtime action governance around cryptographic binding and three-tier record keeping [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]:

- **Action Binding:** The approval record explicitly identifies the target action, arguments or artifact digest (computed over a defined canonical form), validity window, permitted variations, and usage limits [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5].
- **Enforcement Point Verification:** The policy enforcement point recomputes argument bindings from the action about to run and checks them against its local clock, rejecting expired, exhausted, or mismatched approvals without granting new authority [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5].
- **Three-Tier Record Model:** Decouples the *decision* (approval record), the *execution attempt* (bearing an enforcement execution ID), and the *confirmed effect* (target service receipt/identifier) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5].
- **Explicit Absence and Conflict Tracking:** Unconfirmed actions are recorded as unconfirmed rather than non-occurrences, and disagreeing service receipts for retried execution identifiers remain visible as audit conflicts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5].

# References

- Developed under the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) Design Patterns Catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50].
- Related to [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5].

proposed_concept.title: AI Agent Bill of Materials
proposed_concept.description: A machine-readable inventory detailing an AI agent's models, harness, callable tools, and underlying software dependencies, including suppliers and versions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

An AI agent bill of materials (AI-BOM) is a standardized, machine-readable inventory of the components an AI agent is composed of and depends upon, including its foundational models, runtime harness, callable tools, and third-party software dependencies along with their respective suppliers and versions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification

The AI-BOM concept extends traditional Software Bills of Materials (SBOM) into agentic environments [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]:

- **Scope of Coverage:** Extends beyond executable binary code to encompass prompt harnesses, tools, skills, pre-trained model weights, and system prompts governing agent behavior [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10].
- **Regulatory Alignment:** Maps to supply chain and documentation requirements under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation 2024/2847, Art. 3(39) & Annex I) and the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689, Annex IV point 2(a) & Art. 25(4)) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10].
- **Format Agnosticism:** Accommodates existing and emerging packaging profiles including CycloneDX ML-BOM and SPDX 3.0.1 AI profile without mandating a single serialization standard [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10].

# References

- Proposed within the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10].
- Related terms: [Agent Tool Supply Chain Terms](../taxonomy/agent-tool-supply-chain-terms.md).

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, review checklists, and security best practices for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. It produces open threat models, taxonomies, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership

The working group is led by Chairs appointed by Platinum and Gold members for terms running from March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]:
- **Chair:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer)
- **Co-Chair:** Junjie Bu (Google)

## Core Workstreams and Deliverables

1. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis & Framework Design:** Evaluates existing AI security frameworks (CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, NIST AI RMF) against agentic-specific threats like multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation vulnerabilities, and supply chain integrity [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]. Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].
2. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Living guidance covering defense-in-depth and runtime boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821] (see [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../policies-guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)).
3. **Design Patterns Catalog:** Reference security patterns including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26], co-led by Sagar and Dan [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
4. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Multi-group collaboration instrument with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
5. **Taxonomy & Landscape:** Unified terminology curation coordinated through the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-14:** Charter and initial scope unanimously approved [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-06-23:** Repositories made public, establishing standard workstream and deliverable directory trees [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-09-29:** Approved deliverable merge policies restricting self-approval in `/deliverables` and scheduled alternate-week APAC time slots [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch Pattern
proposed_concept.description: An independent out-of-band runtime control plane that halts agent execution, revokes active credentials, and closes lateral-movement attack surfaces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Kill Switch pattern defines an independent, out-of-band runtime control plane capable of terminating agent execution, revoking active credentials, and enforcing network and tool access denial [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]. Designed as a fail-safe mechanism, it guarantees deterministic containment when an agent exhibits unaligned, adversarial, or out-of-bounds behavior.

# Architecture / Specification

## Containment Actions

When activated, the kill switch executes three containment phases:
1. **Execution Halting:** Pauses or terminates active agent processes, subagents, and queued workflow tasks.
2. **Network and Tool Denial:** Disables network access and blocks tool invocation dispatch paths.
3. **Credential Revocation:** Invalidates session tokens, delegation grants, and service credentials to eliminate lateral movement surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].

## Residual Risks and Implementation Nuances

- **Revocation Read as an Outage:** Where the policy enforcement point runs within the agent workload (e.g., an in-process SDK or sidecar), revoking the credential it presents to its upstream policy service causes subsequent authorization requests to return HTTP 401/403 status codes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]. If the enforcement point includes an availability breaker or 'fail-open' fallback, it may erroneously treat this credential rejection as a transient service outage and reopen tool dispatch [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]. Enforcement points must treat authentication rejections as strict policy refusals rather than availability outages [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].
- **Circuit Breaker Integration:** Authorization rejections must trigger halt counters within circuit breaker logic rather than triggering bypass fallbacks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09-26:** Merged initial design pattern specification under the Security and Privacy Working Group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26].
- **2026-09-29:** Issue #27 opened proposing clarification on credential revocation failure handling in local sidecar enforcement points [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical implementation guidance and architectural controls covering secrets management, MCP protocol security, supply chain verification, guardrails, eval frameworks, and post-incident forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, actionable controls for engineers deploying agentic AI systems across five primary operational domains: secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Authored under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide shifts agent security posture away from static long-lived credentials and unverified tool execution toward ephemeral workload attestations, runtime protocol controls, and bounded execution environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

Identity architecture and cross-boundary delegation models (such as SPIFFE/SVID attestation, RFC 8693 token exchange, and UCAN tokens) are coordinated with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) rather than duplicated in this guide [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Architecture / Specification

### 1. Secrets Management
Static credentials and environment variables present severe blast-radius risks when exposed to prompt injection and unsafe agent state deserialization (e.g., CVE-2025-68664) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. The guide mandates a transition to ephemeral credentials ordered by adoption priority [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:
- **Workload Identity:** Native platform identity (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) exchanging cluster OIDC tokens for short-lived credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Dynamic Secrets Engines:** Per-request scoped credentials with automatic expiry via HashiCorp Vault or equivalent dynamic engines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecar and proxy credential injection isolating sensitive keys from agent process space [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Confidential Computing:** Enclave-attested key release utilizing Intel SGX/TDX or AMD SEV-SNP for high-assurance or multi-tenant regulated workloads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

### 2. Secure Tool Invocation and MCP Protocol Security
Because Model Context Protocol ([MCP](../projects/mcp-gateway-registry.md)) standardizes agent-to-tool connections without cryptographically validating payload contents, defenses must address tool poisoning, rug pulls, cross-server shadowing, and conversation hijacking [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:
- **Pre-Deployment Evaluation:** Verification of repository activity (>=90-day activity threshold), cross-referencing against the Vulnerable MCP Project and CVE databases, and static scanning (Cisco MCP Scanner, Snyk Agent Scan) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Transport Security:** Mandatory OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, TLS enforcement, and RFC 8707 resource parameter token audience binding for HTTP transport [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Stdio Transport Containment:** Treating `stdio` MCP servers as untrusted local binaries requiring isolated sandboxing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Enforcement Gateways:** Routing multi-server agent traffic through unified enforcement gateways (such as Linux Foundation `agentgateway` or Cloudflare MCP Portals) to enforce per-tool policies, description hash comparisons, and full payload logging [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

### 3. Supply Chain and Skill Verification
Agent skill packages, MCP server packages, and A2A Agent Cards must undergo multi-tiered vetting [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:
- **Tier 1 (Automated Pre-scanning):** Automated static pattern matching and behavioral dataflow analysis blocking on Critical/High findings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Tier 2 (Elevated Permission Review):** Manual validation of `allowed-tools` declarations, checks for undeclared external domain calls, `eval()` dispatches, and Base64-obfuscated payloads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

# Lifecycle History

Deliverable 4 of the Security and Privacy Working Group, led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]. Originally released as Draft v0.1 in September 2026 and maintained as a living deliverable alongside the feature matrix [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defense-in-depth patterns, security best practice guides, and cross-working-group review checklists for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) is an AAIF technical body focused on defining threat modeling baselines, architectural defense patterns, operational security guidelines, and review checklists for autonomous and multi-agent AI architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

The group establishes alignment across established industry frameworks—combining OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (developer controls), MITRE ATLAS (adversarial technique detection), CSA MAESTRO (architectural hardening), and NIST AI RMF (governance scaffolding)—to address agentic vulnerability surfaces without duplicating existing classification systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification

### Deliverable Structure
The working group organizes its output across five core deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157]:
1. **D1: Taxonomy of Terms:** Shared vocabulary for agentic security threats (transitioned to the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../workstreams/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157].
2. **D2: Threat Modeling Gap Analysis & Framework Design:** Evaluation of existing frameworks against agentic-specific threats including memory poisoning, tool invocation risk, delegated authorization, rogue agent derailment, and payment risks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
3. **D3: Design Patterns Catalog:** Architectural specifications for newly identified gap areas, including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) and [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).
4. **D4: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Operational and engineering practices covering secrets elimination, MCP protocol hardening, skill scanning, and post-incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
5. **D5: Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Governance handoff framework routing agent identity and delegation architecture to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and commerce-specific risks to the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Lifecycle History

- **Leadership:** Deliverable leads include Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), and Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].
- **2026-06-22:** Initial vocabulary definitions transitioned to `ws-taxonomy-landscape` to anchor foundation-wide taxonomy consistency [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157].
- **2026-09-30:** Draft v0.1 milestones achieved for both the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and the Security Best Practices Guide [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157].

proposed_concept.title: Agent to MCP Server Boundary Observability
proposed_concept.description: Observability architecture and telemetry matrix defining context propagation, session versus request lifecycles, and evidence grades across Model Context Protocol boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent to MCP Server boundary observability architecture defines telemetry propagation, cross-boundary context correlation, and gap analysis for interactions between AI agents and Model Context Protocol servers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711]. While termed semantically as Agent to MCP Server, the underlying protocol transport executes between an MCP Client (such as a host application, agent runtime, or gateway) and an MCP Server over JSON-RPC 2.0 via stdio or Streamable HTTP [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification separates session lifecycle instrumentation from request lifecycle instrumentation to prevent operational conflation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711]:
- **Session Lifecycle**: Spans connection establishment (`initialize` handshake, protocol capability negotiation), client and server metadata, capability sets, and session identity until shutdown or transport error [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].
- **Request Lifecycle**: Spans individual JSON-RPC method dispatches, request identifiers, parameter payloads, execution latencies, streaming progress subscriptions, and result or error outputs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].

Cross-boundary distributed tracing correlates client-side and server-side spans using W3C Trace Context propagated via `params._meta.traceparent` aligned with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711]. The architecture establishes that evidence grades are determined by telemetry consumers rather than producers, and highlights key open gaps including declared-versus-observed execution divergence, server-side side-effect manifests, and consent-chain verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-32].

# References
See also [Agent-Tool CLI Boundary](../reference-architectures/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md) and [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../reference-architectures/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automation engine generating chapter slide decks and community assets using paragraph-level OOXML rebranding and Gall Stereographic map projection.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Create Chapter skill automates the creation and rebranding of localized chapter presentation decks and community assets from canonical template decks [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. The execution engine handles paragraph-level OOXML transformations, Drive asset synchronization, and accurate geographical map dot placement [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

# Architecture / Specification
The chapter generation engine (`create_chapter.py`) is structured around two core subsystems [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]:
- **OOXML Rebranding**: Transforms slide content at the paragraph level by concatenating text runs before applying city replacements and writing back to the initial text run, preventing layout degradation caused by arbitrary OOXML run-splitting [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. Case rules for abbreviation variants are dynamically evaluated from surrounding tokens [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].
- **Map Projection Engine**: Places chapter location markers on template overview slides using a fitted Gall Stereographic projection mapping latitude and longitude coordinates into pixel offsets (`lon2x` linear in longitude; `lat2y` linear in `(1 + √2/2)·tan(lat/2)`) [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. Projection parameters are calibrated against coastline vertices using Nelder-Mead optimization against high-resolution coastline rasters [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

# References
See also [AAIF Sync Chapters](../skills/aaif-sync-chapters.md) and [AAIF Sync Badges](../skills/aaif-sync-badges.md).

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared trace identity and portable telemetry context preserving causal execution relationships across agent runtimes, subagents, and tool boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model establishes a shared trace identity and portable telemetry context that preserves causal execution relationships across distributed agent runtimes, tool boundaries, and multi-agent interactions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]. The model defines structured span hierarchies and semantic conventions that correlate high-level agent intentions with low-level execution dispatches and runtime evidence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Architecture / Specification
To account for widespread variance in OpenTelemetry GenAI implementation across production coding agents and SDKs, the trace model development follows an evidence-first four-phase execution plan [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]:
1. **Agree**: Establish initial dimension coverage and evaluation scopes across behavioral tracing dimensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
2. **Evidence**: Capture and analyze empirical trace telemetry emitted by reference implementations, utilizing [Goose](../reference-architectures/goose.md) as the primary open reference baseline [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
3. **Interpret**: Maintain a shared gap register documenting divergences between declared specifications and observed runtime emissions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
4. **Contribute**: Formulate and upstream concrete semantic convention enhancements to OpenTelemetry and related standards bodies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# References
See also [Agent-Tool CLI Boundary](../reference-architectures/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md), [Agent to MCP Server Boundary Observability](../reference-architectures/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md), and [Working Group Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Announcement Post Generation Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized automation skill for drafting LinkedIn launch announcements from event tracker records while enforcing strict privacy rules.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-announcement-post` skill generates concise, structured LinkedIn announcement posts when RSVPs open for AAIF chapter and online events [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710]. It extracts structured metadata from an event's `Event Tracker.docx` via `fetch_tracker.py` and produces publisher-ready copy conforming to AAIF editorial standards [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710].

# Architecture / Specification

## Copy Structure and Editorial Voice
Posts generated by the skill follow explicit layout and stylistic constraints [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710]:
- **Length and Layout**: Approximately 120 words structured into a one-line hook, the what/when/where particulars, speaker details with one concrete takeaway, and an RSVP call to action [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710].
- **Formatting Limits**: Maximum of one emoji and at most three hashtags [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710].
- **House Voice**: Emphasizes a builder-to-builder tone prioritizing technical signal and shared practice over promotional product copy [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710].
- **Standard Standing Footer**: Concludes with standing links to the Linux Foundation Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710].

## Public-Copy Privacy Rule
To prevent leaking sensitive operational data into public channels or agent interaction traces, the skill enforces strict information withholding [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710]:
- Suppresses private contact details including attendee intake data, speaker emails, phone numbers, and venue door codes [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710].
- Forbids echoing withheld values back in agent confirmation dialogues, omission explanations, or transcript transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710].

# Overview

The `aaif-event-status` skill is a deterministic, read-only operational tool that inspects an AAIF chapter or online series `Event Tracker.docx` to report overdue and upcoming task deadlines [^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30]. It pairs local timeline evaluation with optional Luma calendar API queries to provide real-time RSVP counts and attendee check-in metrics [^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30].

# Architecture / Specification

## Tooling and Execution Constraints
- **Google Workspace CLI Integration**: Operates strictly through the `gws` CLI and Python without writing back to Google Drive or Microsoft Office documents [^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30].
- **Rendering and Fidelity Safeguards**: Disallows desktop office suites or headless renderers such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` to prevent font substitutions and OOXML corruption [^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30].

## Operational Workflow
1. **Tracker Retrieval**: Executes `scripts/fetch_tracker.py` to resolve the target Google Drive directory and download `Event Tracker.docx` into a secure `0700` temporary directory [^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30].
2. **Local Digest Computation**: Runs `scripts/event_status.py` to evaluate task due dates relative to the execution timestamp, grouping overdue items and items due within seven days by owner [^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30].
3. **Registration Telemetry**: Fetches participant metrics (confirmed, waitlisted, and checked-in attendees) when a Luma event URL is configured [^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30].

While in-person chapters created via [`aaif-create-chapter`](./aaif-create-chapter.md) manage venue contracts, A/V logistics, and physical access controls, online series utilize a dedicated runbook focused on virtual platforms, streaming links, technical dry runs, recording pipelines, and chat moderation [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca].

- **Platform Slugs**: Updates Luma URLs and hyperlink targets to the assigned series slug [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill interacts with Google Drive via the `gws` CLI tool and local Python OOXML modification scripts[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93]:

- **Tracker Customization**: Differentiates between in-person chapters (requiring `VENUE` and `LOCATION / CITY` fields) and online series (requiring `PLATFORM` and `STREAM / JOIN LINK` fields)[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].

- **Approval Checkpoints**: External API creation is gated behind explicit human approval, aligning with [patterns/approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].
- **Tooling Constraints**: Forbids third-party office conversions such as LibreOffice/`soffice` or `unoconv` to preserve brand typography and embedded OOXML metadata[^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].

# Overview
`aaif-backup` is an operational safety skill that captures immutable, timestamped local snapshots of critical AAIF operations data before high-risk mutations such as schema changes, column restructuring, or bulk cleanup scripts [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-30b3ce2e]. By default, it creates versioned exports of the Community Intake Ops sheet and can snapshot arbitrary Drive files or local paths [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-30b3ce2e].

# Architecture / Specification
The backup engine executes via `scripts/backup.py` and strictly enforces read/export paths [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-30b3ce2e].

### Key Features and Guardrails
- **Immutable Versioning**: Snapshots are saved to timestamped paths (e.g., `<dest>/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>`) without overwriting previous runs, preserving an audit trail [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-30b3ce2e].
- **Native API Integration**: Interacts with Google Drive via the `gws` CLI to export Google Workspace files directly to native Office formats (.xlsx, .docx, .pptx) without intermediary desktop office suite conversions [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-30b3ce2e].
- **Tooling Constraints**: Prohibits third-party conversion binaries (like LibreOffice/`soffice` or `unoconv`) to prevent font corruption and XML schema stripping [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-30b3ce2e].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Slack Community Audit Skill
proposed_concept.description: Standardized automation skill auditing Slack channels, organizer memberships, workspace activity, and generating composite health reports.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-audit-slack` provides a comprehensive, read-only operational audit of the AAIF Slack community workspace [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65]. It serves as phase 8 of the estate synchronization pipeline (`../skills/aaif-sync.md`), acting as an independent verification layer to ensure chapter coverage, organizer inclusion, and topic channel activity without modifying Slack state directly [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65].

# Architecture / Specification
The audit system is split into three report engines, a shared measurement layer, and a unified HTML summary generator [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65][^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-93d6c214]:

### Report Engines and Scripts
- **Organizers Audit (`audit_organizers.py`)**: Confirms every chapter has active public and organizer channels and verifies that accepted community organizers are present [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65].
- **Topics Audit (`audit_topics.py`)**: Evaluates subject-matter channels for message recency, overlap, and newcomer discoverability [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65].
- **Members Audit (`audit_members.py`)**: Analyzes workspace composition and user experience from the perspective of standard members [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65].
- **Activity Measurement (`audit_activity.py`)**: Supplies message metrics, distinct poster counts, and timestamp of the last human interaction [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65].
- **Summary Engine (`summarize_audits.py`)**: Compiles engine outputs into `slack-full-audit.html`, combining chapter, organizer, topic, and member metrics into an actionable priority index [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-93d6c214].

### Caching and Security Guardrails
- **Atomic Caching**: Cache files are written with 0600 permissions in a 0700 cache directory (`.slack-audit-cache`) stamped with workspace metadata to prevent cross-workspace contamination [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-93d6c214].
- **Git Safety Check**: Scripts refuse to execute if cache or output directories risk inclusion via `git add -A`, safeguarding private member identities and emails from accidental commit to public repositories [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-93d6c214].
- **Prompt Injection Defense**: Member profiles, channel topics, and CRM cells are strictly treated as untrusted data and cannot trigger administrative mutations or authorization grants [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter
proposed_concept.description: Standardized automation skill creating and provisioning new AAIF city chapters by cloning TemplateCity and rebranding drive assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-create-chapter` skill provisions new AAIF city chapters in Google Drive by cloning the `TemplateCity` template directory and executing multi-surface asset rebranding.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7] It ensures chapter collateral—including event trackers, attendee CRMs, slide decks, and banner assets—consistently adopts the new chapter's identity, coordinates, and Luma registration targets without manual document manipulation.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]

# Architecture / Specification
## Tooling and Mutation Strategy
Chapter generation and asset customization enforce strict tooling guardrails:
- **`gws` CLI and Python**: All Drive file discovery, replication, and metadata updates execute via the `gws` Google Workspace CLI driven from Python scripts.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]
- **Native Formats vs OOXML Surgery**: Native Google Workspace files (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) are modified using the Docs, Sheets, or Slides APIs. Stored Office files (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) undergo direct byte-level OOXML surgery on internal zip parts to preserve embedded fonts and untouched structures.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]
- **Prohibition on Desktop Suites**: Tools like LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are explicitly banned due to font substitution issues and silent dropping of unhandled OOXML attributes.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7] Local preview rendering is delegated to headless API exports.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]

## Rebranding and Token Substitution
Chapter cloning replaces template placeholders while preserving event-specific fillable fields (dates, speakers, agenda placeholders):[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]
- **City Names**: Replaces `San Francisco` / `SAN FRANCISCO` with the new target city name, preserving casing.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]
- **Abbreviations**: Replaces `SF` tokens with full city name casing appropriate to the context.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]
- **Luma Slugs**: Rewrites `aaif-sanfrancisco` URLs and link references to `aaif-<slug>` according to slug conventions.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]
- **Map Dot Positioning**: Repositions the network location indicator dot and `<CITY> · TONIGHT` marker on slide 5 of `Event Template/Slides.pptx` using geocoded latitude/longitude coordinates.[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]

## Chapter Renaming Protocol
In-place chapter renames are executed across four distinct operational surfaces via `rename_chapter.py`:[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]
1. The Google Drive chapter folder name.[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]
2. File and subfolder filenames.[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]
3. OOXML text within `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` archives.[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]
4. Document metadata properties (`docProps`).[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]

To protect live registrations, Luma slugs are decoupled from name changes and are only updated if explicitly requested with `--slug-from` and `--slug-to` flags.[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3] Relationship parts (`.rels`) only receive slug mutations to prevent dangling relationship corruption.[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]

# Overview
`aaif-community-pulse` is an automation skill that collects community activity data and drafts biweekly update digests across three distinct target audiences: organizers (`#local-champs`), community members (`#general`), and external social networks (LinkedIn/X)[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-63272570][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-ceb51f5d].

# Architecture / Specification
- **Multi-Audience Triad**: From a single gathering pass, generates three separate drafts:
  - *Organizer Post* (`.pulse-cache/pulse-local-champs.txt`): Focuses on actionable chapter operational tasks, admin/tooling updates, and requests[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-ceb51f5d].
  - *Member Post* (`.pulse-cache/pulse-general.txt`): Highlights past event recaps and upcoming community calendar listings[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-ceb51f5d].
  - *Public Post* (`.pulse-cache/pulse-social.txt`): Provides ecosystem-facing overviews of community growth[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-ceb51f5d].
- **Security & Untrusted Source Guardrails**: Channel messages and spreadsheet cells are strictly treated as data rather than execution directives. Drafts are written exclusively to local files in `.pulse-cache/` and never directly posted to remote networks via API[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-63272570][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-ceb51f5d].
- **Plugin Packaging**: Conforms to Agent Plugins v1 portable packaging rules declaring explicit runtime dependencies and portable directory resolution tokens[^evt-community-events-pr-54].

proposed_concept.title: Critical Use Cases Workstream
proposed_concept.description: AAIF Workflows & Process Integration WG workstream curating a verified production use case inventory and workflow classification schema.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Critical Use Cases workstream operates under the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to identify reusable workflow patterns derived from verified, production-deployed AI agent applications [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]. The workstream maintains a standardized classification schema and an empirical inventory of real-world use cases spanning horizontal enterprise functions, software engineering, and vertical industries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

# Architecture / Specification
## Classification Dimensions
The workstream classifies agentic workflows across five structural design dimensions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]:
- **Trigger**: External system events, recurring schedules, or direct user requests.
- **HITL Pattern**: Human-in-the-loop oversight points, including approval gates, asynchronous reviews, or full execution autonomy.
- **Agent Count**: Number of distinct reasoning agents deployed and the explicit rationale for separation (e.g., specialized models, isolated tool scopes).
- **Coordination**: Sequencing mechanism controlling activity transitions, distinguishing deterministic code from dynamic LLM runtime reasoning.
- **Workflow Pattern**: Execution topology, such as linear sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out/fan-in branching, or [Bounded Convergence Loops](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md).

Seven non-dimensional supporting fields capture empirical metrics and context: execution duration, tools and systems, key failure modes, preconditions, and rationale notes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

## Evidentiary Standards
To prevent speculative or unverified claims, all inventory entries must meet strict evidentiary standards [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]:
- **Preferred**: Primary vendor product documentation or announcements citing named production customer deployments, with a target of three independent citations per row [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Acceptable**: Primary vendor feature documentation demonstrating production deployment at scale without named case studies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303].
- **Excluded**: Secondary blogs, analyst commentary, academic preprints, market projection statistics, and personal anecdotal accounts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream drafted the foundational classification schema and inventory, followed by a comprehensive cleanup in PR #41 that established strict evidentiary filtering, removed secondary citations, and aligned multi-agent rationales [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

# Overview
The Workflows & Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical governance body established to standardize workflow execution models, activity schemas, coordination patterns, and runtime control interfaces across heterogeneous AI agent systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group directs multiple workstreams and architectural deliverables:
- **Critical Use Cases**: Maintains a verified cross-industry inventory of production agent deployments and a five-dimensional structural classification schema ([Critical Use Cases Workstream](../workstreams/critical-use-cases.md)) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Execution Semantics & Vocabularies**: Standardizes foundational workflow definitions, lifecycle boundaries, and activity contracts (see [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md) and [Workflow Architecture Principles](../policies-guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md)).
- **Pattern Catalog**: Defines architectural patterns for reliable agent execution, including [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md), and [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md).

# Lifecycle History
The working group formed the Critical Use Cases workstream to establish an empirical, evidence-backed foundation for reference architectures through real-world deployment data [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Critical Use Cases workstream operates under the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to identify, categorize, and document reusable workflow patterns from real-world, deployed agentic AI applications [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]. The workstream prioritizes empirical verification over speculative architecture by indexing real deployments against shared taxonomy schemas [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream maintains two core artifacts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]:
- `schema-agentic-use-cases.md`: The standardized metadata schema and classification taxonomy used to evaluate agent workflows.
- `use-case-inventory.md`: The inventory of real-world use cases mapped to workflow patterns and classification tags.

### Evidentiary Citation Standards
To ensure all cataloged use cases reflect genuine production systems, the workstream enforces tiered citation requirements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]:
- **Verification Threshold**: Each inventory entry must cite at least one primary source confirming production deployment, targeting three verified citations per use case [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].
- **Source Tiers**: Classifies source credibility across preferred (primary vendor product pages, confirmed production engineering posts), acceptable, and non-acceptable tiers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

# Lifecycle History
The category groupings, metadata schema, and evidentiary rules are prepared for working group approval, while individual inventory rows undergo continuous citation verification [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical implementation guidance, control feature matrix, and architectural controls across people, process, and technology pillars.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides defensive architectural controls, operational procedures, and implementation patterns for securing autonomous agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]. Maintained by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), it links technical enforcement mechanisms with organizational governance and skills training [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline organizes security controls across a three-pillar feature matrix to ensure balanced implementation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]:

- **People**: Features requiring specialized training, operational skills, security awareness, and human readiness across all personnel interacting with agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].
- **Process**: Features requiring formalized policies, documented operational procedures, compliance reviews, and governance strategies for security execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].
- **Technology**: Features enforced via physical or digital tools, hardware roots of trust, runtime execution sandboxes, automated authorization gates, and cryptographic telemetry pipelines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

These capabilities directly inform runtime patterns such as the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md).

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing vendor-neutral standards for AI agent identity, verifiable delegation, and appraisal-driven evidence strength.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and vocabularies for AI agent identity, verifiable delegation, provenance, and cross-organizational trust evaluation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5]. The group focuses on how agents authenticate their operational context, prove authorization chains, and provide verifiable evidence of user approval [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5].

# Architecture / Specification
Key technical models under development include:

### Evidence-Strength Vocabulary
The group defines evidence-strength labels as outputs of relying-party appraisal rather than self-asserted credential fields [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5]:
- **Axis A (Who Asserts)**: Evaluates assertion independence across *Declared* (self-asserted), *Platform-attested* (runtime environment), and *Corroborated* (independent third-party confirmation) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5].
- **Axis B (Chain Construction)**: Evaluates delegation binding across *Composed* (multi-hop chains governed by the weakest-hop rule) and *Anchored* (terminating in an independently verifiable trust root) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5].
- **Freshness and Revocation**: A distinct appraisal dimension tracking real-time status against revocation stores rather than treating freshness as a static rank [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5].

### Attestation Component Architecture
The reference architecture decomposes agent attestation into three distinct layers [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]:
1. **Platform Evidence**: Signed hardware or firmware measurement reports (e.g., AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, NVIDIA H100 reports) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
2. **Identity Binding**: Signed statements explicitly linking the agent's key or identity payload to platform measurement registers (e.g., via `REPORT_DATA`, paravisor runtime claims JSON, or TPM qualifying data) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
3. **Appraisal**: Verifier evaluation against local policy to produce attestation verdicts [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group bridging global AI policy instruments with machine-checkable logging, evidence, and risk controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group bridges international AI governance frameworks, legal instruments, and compliance mandates with machine-checkable technical specifications [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9]. It conducts gap analyses mapping regulatory requirements (e.g., EU AI Act, SOC 2, PCI DSS v4.0.1, ISO/IEC 42001) to concrete architectural verification artifacts [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].

# Architecture / Specification
### Converging Evidence and Logging Standards
The Phase 2 gap analysis identifies convergence across emerging international standards defining checkable audit record shapes [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9]:
- **ISO/IEC 24970 & prEN 18229-1**: Joint international standards specifying machine-checkable logging for AI trustworthiness [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **IETF Agent Audit Trail (`draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail`)**: Open JSON record schema mapping directly to EU AI Act and SOC 2 audit trail mandates [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].

These specifications establish shared technical requirements for agent auditability [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9]:
- Hash-chained, timestamped, tamper-evident log records [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- Mandatory pre-execution capture of authorization denials and escalation events [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- A recording-independence gradient ensuring an autonomous agent cannot act as the sole recorder of its own high-trust actions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- Support for external timestamp anchoring and decision reproducibility metadata [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].

proposed_concept.title: Prismor
proposed_concept.description: Self-hosted runtime control plane for AI agents providing policy-as-code evaluation and tool call interception.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Prismor is an open-source (Apache-2.0), self-hosted control plane for AI agents designed to evaluate and govern tool dispatches using policy-as-code[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]. Operating as an interception layer between agent reasoning harnesses and executable capabilities, Prismor provides pre-execution inspection, verdict enforcement (allow, block, transform, or require human approval), and result redaction across diverse agent frameworks and protocols.

# Architecture / Specification
Prismor enforces policies across three primary integration surfaces[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]:
- **Coding Agent Hooks**: Pre-execution hooks directly embedded within developer agent harnesses and coding tools.
- **In-Process SDK Adapters**: Client-side library wrappers supporting agent runtimes such as LangChain and OpenAI Agents SDK.
- **MCP Gateway**: A proxy fronting downstream Model Context Protocol servers, evaluating `tools/call` invocations against policy rules before dispatch and scanning execution responses before returning context to the model.

The engine evaluates versioned YAML policies scoped across organization, project, repository, or session boundaries[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]. It supports both an *observe mode* for impact telemetry and an *enforce mode* for strict policy gating, emitting signed audit trails and attestation bundles to verify runtime controls[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51].

# Lifecycle History
Originally introduced on PyPI as `immunity-agent` in early 2026, the project rebranded to `prismor` in version 1.13.0[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]. An application for hosting within the Agentic AI Foundation was formally submitted in September 2026[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51].
